findings.title: Fake approval page CSP form-action 'self' blocks the approve/cancel redirect to the app: [B] payment journeys cannot complete
findings.detail:
Revision 2 adds a contract for the fake approval listener (SEC-12). GET /fake-paypal/checkout/:id is served with CSP "default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; form-action 'self'", and the listener 'applies the same security headers ... as the app', whose CSP also ends in form-action 'self'. POST .../approve answers 303 to the stored return_url on http://localhost:<port> (the app), and POST .../cancel answers 303 to the cancel_url. Chromium enforces form-action across the redirect chain of a form submission. I reproduced the spec's page with Playwright's Chromium (ev:ev-mv1dhs2e-012e67d4):
- (A) the spec's CSP: the browser stays on the fake page with 'Refused to send form data ... violates the following Content Security Policy directive', and the return route is never hit.
- (B) form-action 'self' plus the app origin: the browser reaches the return route with the SameSite=Lax session cookie.
- (C) no CSP: same as (B).
- (D) control: a Strict cookie is not sent, so the return really is cross-site, which is what RS-31 requires.
As specified, test/browser/journey-happy (RS-31(a)), journey-replacement (RS-32(a)) and the NFR2 keyboard-only happy path cannot get past the first PayPal approval.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when every Content-Security-Policy header the fake approval listener sends either lists the app's return origin in form-action (form-action 'self' <RS_PUBLIC_URL origin>) or omits form-action. That includes the inherited app security headers, because two CSP headers are both enforced. The same applies to the test helper paypal-stub's approval page. Test: a [B] assertion in journey-happy that the approve and cancel clicks land on /api/paypal/return and /api/paypal/cancel with the session (it would have caught this), plus a [D] header test that pins the listener's CSP value.

findings.title: Per-day request limit and live-reservation cap are not reconciled with the browser suites and the user-run demo
findings.detail: RS_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_CUSTOMER_PER_DAY defaults to 10, and request_create events survive request deletion. The [B] files reuse the seeded customers (cafe1/cafe2) for several journeys: happy at 360 and 1280, the keyboard variant, the a11y states, labelling for both adapters and six-questions. The spec does not say whether each [B] file gets a fresh database (server-proc does use a temp RS_DB_PATH) or whether the limit is raised for tests. The user-run Sandbox journeys and demo-video retakes with one account can also hit 10 per day. With a cap of 1 live reservation, an abandoned journey blocks the next one for up to 30 minutes unless 'Abandon purchase' is used.
findings.recommendation: State that every [B] test file starts its own server on a fresh database (or sets the two limits through the environment in test mode). Add a README runbook line for demo operators: raise or reset the limits, use separate accounts, or abandon before retaking.

findings.title: OQ-D6 and OQ-D7: record the status-set extension; the share default could be on
findings.detail: OQ-D6: 'replanning' is a reasonable, honest extension; my probe confirms RS-36 (i)-(iv) are unchanged with it (ev:ev-mv1dkn6p-01cfa3c8). Because it adds to the user's status vocabulary, it belongs in the decision record and in the brief-deviation list the user sees. OQ-D7: the stated reason for keeping the per-customer share off is that 0.2 would refuse NFR6's first two calls. But NFR6's test can pin RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1 in its own environment; with the production defaults (budget 1.00, cap 0.05), a share of 0.2 allows 4 cap-sized reservations per customer. Deferring to the user (Q10) is acceptable.
findings.recommendation: Record OQ-D6 as a decision (eccode decision add). When the user answers Q10, consider defaulting the share to 0.2 with the NFR6 test pinning 1.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Scope (user, key) with a fingerprint over method, concrete path and body; reservations.idempotency_key UNIQUE per customer; operation_key carries the plan id; collisions mapped explicitly; [D] cases include the second plan before and after purge. On the revised DDL the same customer's key on plan 2 is refused by UNIQUE (customer_id, idempotency_key) with no idempotency_keys row present, another customer may reuse the text, and the key PK refuses a second fingerprint.

The derivation is total: row 4a (replanning) for a queued re-plan, a re-plan queue that never drops entries after the retries run out, and a defensive row 14 with a property test. My own implementation of the revised table gives S13/S13b 'replanning', S15 'collected', S15b 'cancelled', S15c (admin refund unknown) 'refunding', and RS-36 (i)-(iv) unchanged. Exhaustive enumeration of 493,074 abstract states reaches row 14 only in 326 unreachable states: a feasible run with no version, or an unknown whose prev_status cannot occur under P's status.

The Sender table names who sends each queued or retryable call kind. A queued authorize is sent by reconciler step 6, or cancelled with the operation voided locally once cancellation is requested. Row 2(a) escalates 'approved' with an outstanding authorize after the unknown limit, and the return-crash integration test covers it. In my derivation probe, S18 ends 'cancelled' (not stuck in cancelling), while S18b (started authorize unknown, 20 min) and S18c (429 re-queued, 20 min) reach failed_needs_attention.

Every flagged script begins with the flag-free 'node scripts/check-node.cjs &&'. I ran the spec's start line verbatim through /bin/sh and through 'npm run start'. On Node 20.20 and 21.7 it exits 1 with 'RescueStock needs Node >= 22.13 (found ...)', and the 22.5-branch line names 22.5. On 22.22 the app starts. Every flagged script in the block carries the gate prefix.

The hard 429 is keyed on (normalised username, IP), 5 per 15 min, plus 20 per IP. Across IPs a username gets only a 1-10 s delay, and the password is still checked. Unknown usernames are counted alike, and T8 is rewritten. On the revised login_failures schema, five failures from the attacker IP reach the pair limit for that IP only: the pair on another IP is 0 and the cross-IP total stays below the delay threshold.

There is a live-reservation cap (default 1) checked inside the reserve BEGIN IMMEDIATE, giving 409 RESERVATION_LIMIT, and 10 requests per customer per day with count and insert atomic, both asserted in abuse-limits.test.js. Two OS processes reserving two different plans for the same customer give exactly RESERVED + RESERVATION_LIMIT. The RS-32 sequence (void-rule release, then replacement reserve) passes under the cap.

Loopback PayPal and Anthropic base URLs, and a loopback approval host, are accepted only with RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1, which sets labels.testMode and shows the 'Test mode — local stubs, nothing is real' banner. Startup refuses them otherwise, and T18 and the RS-34 traceability name the config and labelling tests for both cases. This is a text-level fix, checked against the spec's Conventions, Security and Deployment sections and the traceability run.

review.summary:
Review of design revision 3 (sub-mv1dvx7j-016948c6; spec.md sha256 ef35826f..., revision-3-notes.md 3a0335cd...). I read the full diff against revision 2 (git dc4fd79). Only the sections the notes name changed, and no SQL changed. I re-ran every check after this submission.
F-TR-14 (blocking) is resolved. Both CSP strings were read from the final spec text and run in Chromium 141 against a stand-in listener that sends the app's other security headers. Approve lands on /api/paypal/return and Cancel on /api/paypal/cancel, both with the SameSite=Lax session and no CSP console error. With the app CSP inherited as a second header the submission is refused (ev:ev-mv1dzo82-01f4b95e).

- NFR6's stated configuration holds with the share pinned to 1.
- The reset's new deletion of request_create rate events leaves the append-only ledgers intact.
All other re-runs on the final text pass: traceability 45/45 with 0 warnings (ev:ev-mv1dzol7-011e6ca6), migrations, constraints and races (ev:ev-mv1dzspa-018c789e), Node floor (ev:ev-mv1dztu7-01dfa34a), derivation totality (ev:ev-mv1dzuec-017fb9d9) and CLI flags (ev:ev-mv1dzupr-01a2dab4).
Every required criterion is met and no blocking or major finding is open. Two new minors are left for the plan: F-TR-17 (the register limit vs a fresh customer per browser journey) and F-TR-18 (the NFR6 evidence must state the share pin).

findings.title: Fresh customer per browser journey vs the 5-registrations-per-IP-per-hour limit
findings.detail: The F-TR-15 fix has every [B] journey register a fresh customer through POST /api/auth/register. All of them come from 127.0.0.1, and registration is limited to 5 per IP per hour. That limit is not configurable and the harness does not raise it. The harness raises only the daily request limit. Each file has a fresh database, but a file with more than five journeys will get 429 register_ip on the sixth registration. a11y-states covers seven states at two widths, and journey-happy covers 360, 1280, the keyboard-only run and the cancel path.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the register limit is an environment setting that the browser harness raises in test mode, or when journeys in one file share pre-registered customers within the per-customer limits. The plan's W6 test-infrastructure task should state which.

findings.title: NFR6's stated configuration holds only with the per-customer share pinned to 1
findings.detail: With the production default share of 0.2 (revision 3), NFR6's stated configuration refuses the first extract with scope 'customer' (my gate model, ev:ev-mv1dzog2-017e0120). That configuration is a fake cap of 0.10 and a budget of 0.25, under which the AC says 'the third extract is refused'. The spec pins RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1 for the NFR6 case and states why, so the design is consistent. However, a reader who checks NFR6 literally, with the brief's settings and the defaults, sees a different outcome.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the NFR6 verification evidence and acceptance report state that the case runs with RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1. The OQ-D7 decision record should also say that NFR6 is asserted with the share off.

resolvedFindings.resolution: The fake approval listener and the paypal-stub approval page now send exactly one CSP, approvalPageCsp(appOrigin) = default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; form-action 'self' <appOrigin>; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none', and no longer inherit the app CSP. I read both strings from the final spec and ran them in Chromium 141. Approve lands on /api/paypal/return and Cancel on /api/paypal/cancel, each with the SameSite=Lax session and no CSP console error. Adding the app CSP as a second header makes Chromium refuse the submission. The spec adds the [B] round-trip assertion (journey-happy, journey-replacement, keyboard-only run) and a [D] test pinning the single header.

Every [B] file starts its own server on a fresh seeded database, and each journey uses a fresh customer. The harnesses raise the daily request limit and keep the live-reservation cap at 1. The README has an operator note for retakes, and the admin reset clears request_create rate events. I checked that deleting those rows is permitted while the append-only ledgers still refuse DELETE. A new consequence of this fix, the register-per-IP limit, is tracked as F-TR-17 (minor).

OQ-D6 and OQ-D7 are in a 'Decisions requested' table for the orchestrator and the user. The share now defaults to 0.2 in production (read from the spec env table), and the NFR6 case pins 1. My gate model confirms that with the defaults one customer's 5th cap-sized call is refused with scope customer while another customer's call succeeds, and that NFR6's configuration with the share pinned gives ok, ok, refused (global).

data.title: OQ-D6: rescue status set gains 'replanning'
data.decision: Adopt the design's row 4a: a request whose approved plan was superseded and whose re-plan is still queued reads 'replanning' (goal.md's status set is extended by one value).
data.rationale: The reviewer showed the brief's derivation table had no row for this reachable state (RS-32 passes through it while the page polls); the alternative, folding it into 'plan_found', would misstate that no plan is currently proposed. Orchestrator default, reversible by the user; recorded as the designer's open question OQ-D6, decision requested.
data.alternatives: fold into plan_found; show the old plan as superseded with no status change

data.title: OQ-D7: per-customer daily model share defaults to 0.2
data.decision: Production default RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=0.2 of the daily model budget per customer (concurrency 1 per customer); the NFR6 evidence runs with the share pinned to 1 and says so; the user may change both with the Q10 answer (daily budget, default USD 1.00).
data.rationale: Security finding SEC-10: a shared daily budget lets a few customers exhaust extraction for everyone. The reviewer (F-TR-18) noted NFR6's stated configuration refuses the first call under 0.2, so the test pins the share to 1 and the acceptance report must state it. Orchestrator default, reversible.
data.alternatives: share off (SEC-10 unmitigated); share 1 everywhere (no per-customer protection)

review.summary:
Review of plan submission sub-mv1eqk2q-01cc29a2 (plan.json 92e23914..., plan.md 9199cc75...), against the approved brief and design revision 3.
What holds, from checks I ran myself:
- `plan validate` is clean (ev:ev-mv1exo5j-01eb88f8).
- Structure: all 29 tasks carry an owner, dependencies, inputs, outputs, files, acceptance criteria and a verification command with cwd '.' (ev:ev-mv1exmy0-01d4615b).
- Dependency graph: no cycle and no dependency on a later phase.
- Concurrency: all 19 concurrent pairs have disjoint ownership; the shared wiring files (src/app.js, src/main.js, src/routes/plans.js, package.json) are only ever owned by serialized tasks; no glob reaches .eccode/, .claude/ or hooks.
- Coverage: all 45 ids are claimed by exactly one phase, and every one of the 59 [D]/[B] test files the design's traceability names is owned in or before its claiming phase and run by a verification command in that phase.
- The criterion moves (RS-15 and RS-38 to F, RS-04 to E, RS-34, NFR3 and NFR5 to G, RS-36 to C) follow real dependencies.
- The live checks are kept outside the tasks and marked Unverified.
- The lesson decision is evidence-backed (ev:ev-mv1eya53-01fe0832).
The problem: on Node 22.22, a node --test command whose globs match nothing exits 0 with 0 tests (ev:ev-mv1exnz5-01303ad6). 11 of the 29 verification commands therefore pass before their task's work exists: b1 and b2 use globs only, the frontend tasks d4, e5, f3 and g1 rerun files that exist from c5, and the test-engineer tasks c6, d5, e6, f4 and g3 run only `npm test && npm run test:browser`. b2 is the task that proves RS-06..RS-11. Changes requested for that one major finding (F-PL-1).
The schedule risk (about 400-600 minutes of work against about 300 left) is recorded as F-PL-2 for the user's decision. It is not a reason to reject.

findings.title: 11 of 29 verification commands pass before the task's work exists
findings.detail:
On Node 22.22, `node --test` with a glob that matches nothing exits 0 with '# tests 0'. A missing explicit file or a missing --import module exits 1 (ev:ev-mv1exnz5-01303ad6). For each command, my plan check looked for a referenced file that the task itself creates first (ev:ev-mv1exmy0-01d4615b). These have none:
- b1-foundation-core and b2-domain: globs only. b2 proves RS-06..RS-11 and the derivation totality.
- d4, e5, f3, g1: the same command as c5, `node --test test/scan/frontend.test.js "test/unit/frontend/**/*.test.js"`, whose files exist from c5.
- c6, d5, e6, f4, g3: `npm test && npm run test:browser`, which are glob-based scripts. Before the task's integration and browser files exist, these pass on whatever exists.
The plan gate requires each verification to fail before the work and pass after. The phase reviewers must rerun exactly these commands, so a green run would not show that the task's own tests exist or pass.
findings.recommendation:
Resolved when every task's command names at least one test file that the task itself creates, so my plan check reports 0 pre-passing tasks. Examples:
- b1: test/unit/config/hosts.test.js, test/unit/db/migrate.test.js.
- b2: test/unit/domain/planner-fixture.test.js, planner-oracle.property.test.js, derive.test.js, states.test.js, test/timing/planner-generator.test.js.
- The frontend tasks: a per-phase file such as test/unit/frontend/extraction.test.js, payments.test.js, recovery.test.js, a11y-labels.test.js.
- The test-engineer tasks: keep `npm test` and append their own files explicitly, e.g. `npm test && npm run test:browser -- test/browser/journey-infeasible.test.js && node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --import ./test/helpers/net-guard.js --test test/integration/rs14-two-process-reserve.test.js test/integration/rs14-db-busy.test.js`.

findings.title: The schedule likely exceeds the remaining runtime budget
findings.detail: status reports 177/480 minutes used, so about 300 remain. The plan's own estimate is 400-600 minutes (29 implementer dispatches, a 20-dispatch critical path, 6 phase reviews, maxConcurrency 2). The plan is close to minimal under one owner per task. The only same-owner, serial merge that does not lengthen the critical path is g3 + g4 (both test-engineer), which saves one dispatch. Other merges would mix owners or serialize concurrent work (e3/e4, d2/d3, f1/f2). The plan already routes the choice to the user (limits.raise or a descoping order). Waiting until the end of phase C risks stopping mid-phase with half-built money paths.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the orchestrator has the user's decision (raise maxRuntimeMinutes, or accept the stated descoping order) recorded before the first implementer dispatch of phase B. Optionally merge g4 into g3.

findings.title: Concurrent f1 and f2 are coupled through files only f2 owns
findings.detail:
f1 (supersession, refusal, RS-15 expiry, re-plan queue) and f2 (saga, reconciler, calls, void-rule, admin) run concurrently with disjoint ownership. However:
- f1's RS-15 ('expiry before execute voids every authorization') and the F-TR-2 drain behaviour exercise void-rule.js and reconciler.js, which only f2 owns in phase F.
- The admin stock_depletion and supplier_refusal faults that f1 says 'use the same services' live in admin.js, which f2 owns.
If f1 needs a change in those files, it is blocked until f2 lands.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when either f1 depends on f2, or f1's acceptance criteria state that it changes no void-rule, reconciler or admin code and only tests the behaviour that e2/e4/c3 already built, so any needed change goes to f2.

Prerequisites reviewed in this phase (proved later as RS-36/RS-38): migrations 001-005 match the spec DDL, apply in BEGIN IMMEDIATE with sha256 checksums and are safe when two processes start together; audit_events and inventory_ledger UPDATE/DELETE fail; derive.js implements the revision-2 table row by row (rows 1-14 incl. 4a, 5a) and its totality property test (>= 20,000 seeded walks x 120 events) never reaches row 14 and asserts RS-36 (i)-(iv); states.js tests every allowed and refused pair
npm test passes offline with the net guard active and launches no browser; every test that proves a criterion or finding carries its id at the start of its name

phases.name: C: auth, dashboards, requests, plans, reservations, supplier confirmations, expiry
phases.goal: Server sessions with CSRF, throttles, Host check and default-deny RBAC; customer requests with manual requirement confirmation, planning, approval with hash and total, idempotent BEGIN IMMEDIATE reservations with per-customer caps; supplier order confirm/ready/handover and inventory PATCH; admin reset/faults/timeline/metrics shells; the request view computing the rescue status through derive.js; the three dashboards built against the contract fixtures; multi-process reservation tests and the browser harness.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-12: a plan whose cups or lids total is below the requirement is never produced as feasible, and approve with a tampered planHash or expectedTotalCents returns 409 PLAN_CHANGED (stored plan failing re-validation: PLAN_INVALID) [D: test/api/approve-guards.test.js + planner-fixture]

RS-14: two OS processes (busy_timeout 5000) reserve A's last bundle concurrently on one SQLite file: one reservation active, the other 409 OUT_OF_STOCK, reserved <= on_hand; with busy_timeout 0 and a held write lock reserve answers 503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After [D: test/integration/rs14-two-process-reserve.test.js, rs14-db-busy.test.js]

RS-16: same Idempotency-Key and body -> same reservation id, no second reservation or ledger row; same key with another body -> 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; same key on a second plan -> 422 with no rows, before and after the key row is purged (F-TR-1); a concurrent same-key race resolves to one reservation [D: test/api/reserve-idempotency.test.js]
RS-28: supplier A patching supplier B's inventory gets 403 and nothing changes (whole PATCH refused) [D: test/api/isolation.test.js]
RS-30: customer and supplier sessions calling admin fault and reset routes get 403; unauthenticated 401 [D: test/api/isolation.test.js]

RS-33: browser journey at 360 px and 1280 px: an infeasible request ends on the explanation screen with blocking constraints, per-candidate codes and computed relaxations; no reservation, order or payment operation exists (checked in the database) [B: test/browser/journey-infeasible.test.js, screenshots in test/browser/out/]

RS-36: GET /api/requests/:id computes rescueStatus with derive.js on every read; a schema query finds no column storing a rescue status [D: test/api/rescue-status.test.js, test/api/schema-no-rescue-status.test.js, test/unit/domain/derive.test.js]; [I] reviewer inspects derive.js against the revision-2 table and the view (F-TR-9)

Auth contract (ARCH-25) with SEC-1 (pair/IP hard limits, cross-IP delay only), SEC-9 (username_key normalisation, case variants), SEC-13 (Host allow-list -> 421), SEC-20 (register rotation, no Access-Control-Allow-* header) and SEC-5 (admin password >= 16 chars from env, admin disabled when unset) asserted in test/api/auth.test.js; SEC-2 asserted in test/api/abuse-limits.test.js with the defaults

F-TR-17 resolved by an environment setting: RS_REGISTER_PER_IP_PER_HOUR (default 5; a value above 5 is refused at startup unless RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1); auth.test.js keeps the default and asserts the 6th registration from one IP -> 429 register_ip; the browser and multi-process harnesses set it to 1000 under RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1 together with RS_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_CUSTOMER_PER_DAY=1000 and RS_MAX_LIVE_RESERVATIONS_PER_CUSTOMER=1, so every journey registers its own fresh customer (F-TR-15: fresh database per browser file)

HTTP contract: test/api/contracts.test.js asserts status, envelope, requestId and success-body field types for every route that exists after this phase, against the example responses in test/fixtures/contracts/ that the frontend uses
npm test and npm run test:browser pass

phases.name: D: model extraction with provenance, uploads and retention
phases.goal: Bilingual extraction through the ExtractionProvider contract (deterministic fake for tests; Claude CLI and Anthropic API adapters verified against a recorded transcript and a loopback stub), strict schema validation, grounding and provenance, the degraded manual path, model budget/rate/concurrency controls in integer micro-dollars, image upload by magic bytes with retention and request deletion, the EXT-1 corpus and the opt-in live-model runner, and the matching UI.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-01 [D]: the RS-FIX-1 Arabic and English wordings yield identical core fields (product type, quantities, capacity, diameter, deadline, budget, max pickups) through POST /api/requests/:id/extract with the fake provider [test/api/extract.test.js]
RS-02 [D]: a clear package image yields capacity and diameter with provenance 'image' [test/api/extract-image.test.js]

RS-03 [D + B]: ambiguous images give unknown fields, >= 1 clarification question and no number absent from the image [test/eval/extraction-fake.test.js]; faults timeout, invalid_json, schema_invalid, error, budget refusal and rate refusal give schema_ok=false, an error code, every field unknown, degraded: true [test/api/extract-degraded.test.js]; the request page shows 'Automatic reading unavailable — please enter the details' with a manual field for every core field, and confirming them creates a requirements version with provenance manual and planning proceeds [test/browser/degraded-extraction.test.js]

RS-05 [D]: injection strings in text, image text and catalog text (planted in products.name through a DB fixture, SEC-17) stay data; permissions, amounts, suppliers, plan versions and roles equal the control run; explanations are template text; with rephrasing on, output carrying a number or supplier code absent from the trace is discarded [test/api/injection.test.js, test/unit/ai/rephrase.test.js]

RS-39 [D]: upload accepts only PNG/JPEG/WebP by magic bytes (declared image/png with other bytes -> 415), <= 5 MB (413 above), stored under a random 128-bit name; customer Y uploading to X's request -> 404 with no file written; owner DELETE removes image file and row, raw text and extraction text (409 PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS while money is held; tombstone with settled payments); with a pinned clock the sweep deletes at 7 d + 1 min, keeps at 6 d 23 h and writes an audit event [test/api/uploads-retention.test.js]

NFR6 [D]: every response and log line carries requestId; config inspection shows haiku as the default model; with fake per-call cost 0.10, cap 0.10, RS_MODEL_DAILY_BUDGET_USD=0.25 and RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1 pinned in the test's environment (F-TR-18; the test name and the evidence label say so) the third extract is refused with 503 MODEL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED without invoking the provider and enters the degraded path; the 11th extract or upload by one customer within 10 minutes -> 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; micro-dollar boundaries (0.30 allowed, 0.299999 refused) hold; a separate SEC-10 case with the production share 0.2 refuses the 5th cap-sized call of one customer with details.scope 'customer' while another customer succeeds [test/api/model-budget-rate.test.js]; the log scan finds no Authorization header value, token, secret, payer data or provider body [test/scan/secrets.test.js]

Live-model parts are not claimed by this phase: npm run test:live-model refuses (exit 2, named message) without RS_LIVE_MODEL=1 [D]; the real-model run over EXT-1 (RS-01/02/03/05 [LM], NFR6 cost report, F-TR-13 schemaAccepted) is the separately listed check LIVE-M1 and stays Unverified until it is run with an authenticated Claude CLI or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and the user's approval of the USD 5 ceiling
ExtractionProvider contract suite (fake, CLI against a stub binary replaying the recorded transcript, Anthropic against a loopback stub) passes [test/unit/ai/provider-contract.test.js]
npm test and npm run test:browser pass

phases.name: E: PayPal payment flow, saga, webhooks and reconciliation
phases.goal: The PaymentProvider contract with a DB-backed fake (faults, PayPal-Request-Id replay model, fake approval listener on a different site with its own CSP) and the Sandbox REST v2 adapter verified against a loopback paypal-stub; the provider call protocol with the sender table; create/return/cancel/abandon with the void rule; the execute claim and captures with lease fencing; the reconciler (stale intents, read-before-resend, pending polls, expiry); verified webhooks; the payment UI; and the two-process execute and browser happy-path journeys.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-04: with budget or deadline missing, POST /api/plans/:id/approve and POST /api/orders/:id/paypal/create return 409 MISSING_BUDGET / MISSING_DEADLINE (budget first) and no reservation or payment operation or provider call is created [D: test/api/approve-guards.test.js, test/api/paypal-create.test.js]

RS-18 [D]: cancel URL leaves the operation created with buyer_cancelled_at (or voided), no capture call or row, execute -> 409; 'Try approval again' and 'Abandon purchase' offered; abandon or expiry voids every other outstanding authorization, releases the reservation, plan non_executable (PAYMENT_CANCELLED or RESERVATION_EXPIRED) [test/api/paypal-cancel.test.js]

RS-19 [D]: client-supplied amount, currency or supplier on every payment route is ignored; the provider request body (fake and Sandbox adapter against paypal-stub) carries the server-approved supplier-order total [test/api/amount-tampering.test.js]

RS-20 [D]: two server processes x 5 concurrent execute: one approved -> executing claim, nine return the current state with no provider call; the fake records exactly N get_authorization + N capture calls and nothing else (F-TR-8), one capture per order with PayPal-Request-Id so:<id>:capture:1; three hits on the return URL give one authorize call [test/integration/rs20-two-process-execute.test.js, test/api/paypal-return-idempotent.test.js]

RS-21 [D]: one DENIED authorization -> no capture on any order, plan non_executable (AUTHORIZATION_FAILED naming the supplier), other authorizations voided, reservation released, the exact buyer message; PENDING -> authorization_pending and execute 409 AUTHORIZATION_PENDING with no capture until the reconciler observes CREATED [test/api/authorization-denied.test.js, test/api/authorization-pending.test.js]

RS-23 [D]: the same webhook transmission id delivered twice applies once; RS-24 [D]: an invalid signature is rejected 4xx, stored with signature_status invalid, no transition; plus SEC-6 (60/min per IP, pre-checks before any provider call) and SEC-16 (merchant, provider and non-archived scoping) [test/api/webhooks.test.js]

RS-25 [D]: a lost capture response leaves the operation unknown; the reconciler reads provider state and then marks captured, capture_pending (polled) or re-sends with the same PayPal-Request-Id; no second capture; an intent left at restart is treated as unknown [test/api/lost-response.test.js]

RS-27 [D]: customer X requesting Y's request or order id gets 404/403 and no data, including /api/paypal/return?token= and /cancel?token= with Y's token (404, no authorize call, no state change) [test/api/isolation.test.js]

RS-31(a) [B]: journey request -> review -> plan -> reservation -> approvals -> supplier confirmations -> capture -> readiness -> collection at 360 px and 1280 px with screenshots, the app on localhost and the fake approval page on 127.0.0.1 (cross-site), each 'Approve (simulated)' landing on /api/paypal/return with the session, one Cancel landing on /api/paypal/cancel, no CSP console message (F-TR-14) [test/browser/journey-happy.test.js]; the listener and paypal-stub send exactly one CSP header equal to approvalPageCsp(appOrigin) [D: test/api/fake-approval-headers.test.js]

Design items asserted: ARCH-22 lost-authorize void hook (test/api/void-rule-lost-authorize.test.js), ARCH-23 claim on stored expiry with the provider read after the claim (test/api/execute.test.js), F-TR-3 sender table and crash_after_return_commit hook implemented, F-TR-11 order presentation, SEC-3 approval-host and base-URL allow-list in the Sandbox adapter, PaymentProvider contract suite on both adapters (test/unit/payments/provider-contract.test.js)

Live PayPal parts are not claimed by this phase: npm run test:live-paypal refuses without RS_LIVE_PAYPAL=1 and credentials; the Sandbox runs (LIVE-P1: RS-18/19/20/23/24 [LP]; LIVE-P2: RS-31(b)/RS-32(b) hosted approval page) need RS_PAYPAL_DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID, RS_PAYPAL_DEFAULT_CLIENT_SECRET, RS_PAYPAL_DEFAULT_WEBHOOK_ID (or per-supplier sets) and network access to api-m.sandbox.paypal.com and www.sandbox.paypal.com, are user-run, and stay Unverified with blocker A6/Q2 until then
npm test and npm run test:browser pass

phases.name: F: replanning, compensation and restart recovery
phases.goal: Supersession on offer and stock changes with the durable re-plan queue, supplier refusal with re-planning that excludes the supplier, expiry voids, capture-failure compensation (voids, refunds, reconciling -> released with restock), lease takeover with epoch and send-token fencing, restart recovery, admin refund_order and forced reset, ledger completeness, the recovery UI, and the restart, takeover and replacement-journey tests.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-13 [D]: a price change of an offer used by an approved plan (order not confirmed, plan not executing) supersedes it, recomputes a new proposed version, reserve/execute on the old one -> 409 PLAN_SUPERSEDED, every old authorization voided (one void call each), reservation released (one ledger row per item), orders cancelled, 'Prices changed: review plan vN' shown; after the supplier confirmed or after the claim the plan is not superseded [test/api/supersession.test.js]

RS-15 [D]: an expired reservation is released exactly once (inventory back, one expire ledger row, second pass no-op); an expiry pass after the claim and before the first capture changes nothing; expiry before execute voids every authorization, plan non_executable (RESERVATION_EXPIRED) and the request shows 'Reservation expired — no money was taken; re-plan with current stock' [test/api/reservation-expiry.test.js]

RS-17 [D + B]: refusal before the claim -> order refused, outstanding authorizations voided, reservation released, plan non_executable (SUPPLIER_REFUSED), status cancelling while a void is outstanding, refusal reason with 'Review the new plan', new version computed without that supplier [test/api/supplier-refusal.test.js; test/browser/refusal.test.js]

RS-22 [D]: capture failing on the second supplier refunds the first capture and voids the rest; refund_requested -> refund_pending -> refunded|refund_failed; plan non_executable (CAPTURE_FAILED); reservation reconciling until every refund and void completes, then released with restock rows (refund_failed keeps reconciling and failed_needs_attention); handover 409 HANDOVER_BLOCKED; a PENDING capture blocks handover and the next capture, and lease_epoch does not grow across reconciler ticks while it is pending (F-TR-7) [test/api/capture-compensation.test.js]

RS-26 [D]: SIGKILL mid-saga and restart keeps orders, operations, provider calls and recovery progress; after the lease expires the reconciler takes over and completes the saga; lease-takeover variants A and B (ARCH-26) give exactly one non-replayed capture per order; return-crash cases (a), (b), (c) (F-TR-3) [test/integration/rs26-restart.test.js, lease-takeover.test.js, return-crash.test.js]

RS-32(a) [B]: B's offer withdrawn by the admin stock-depletion fault before B confirms; the buyer approves the 9500-cent A+E plan; the old plan superseded, its authorizations voided, B's order cancelled; the replacement flow completes through collection with the cross-site approval round-trip assertion [test/browser/journey-replacement.test.js]

RS-37 [D]: admin reset returns 409 RESET_BLOCKED while any operation is approved|authorization_pending|authorized|capture_pending|captured|refund_requested|refund_pending|unknown; forced reset requires a reason, voids authorized operations and runs one bounded read-resolve pass, lists stranded operations (SEC-11), and archives rather than deletes operations and provider calls [test/api/admin-reset.test.js]

RS-38 [D]: any UPDATE or DELETE on audit_events or inventory_ledger fails; every reserve, release, expire, consume and restock writes a ledger row, and for every product the ledger sums equal on_hand and reserved [test/api/ledgers.test.js]

Design items asserted: F-TR-2 re-plan queue never drops an entry and backs off (test/api/replan-queue.test.js); F-TR-6 capture landing after the void intent ends refunded with one capture, one void attempt and one refund call (test/api/void-capture-race.test.js)
npm test and npm run test:browser pass

phases.name: G: final verification, clean checkout, browser UX, labels and submission materials
phases.goal: Accessibility and all UI states, labelling for both payment adapters, the six-answer request page, the full secrets scan over assets, responses, logs, screenshots and submission files, live-suite refusals, performance budgets, final README with runbooks and operator notes, submission materials, a clean-checkout run on the final tree, and the project evidence table that the verification report cites.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-29 [D + I]: a scan of built frontend assets, recorded API responses, logs, browser screenshots and submission files finds no client id or secret value; config redacts secrets in errors [test/scan/secrets.test.js]

RS-34 [D + B]: fake adapter payloads (payments and extraction) carry simulated: true and the UI shows the 'Simulated' badge and the persistent banner; Sandbox adapter payloads carry provider 'paypal-sandbox' and sandbox: true and every payment element shows 'PayPal Sandbox — no real money'; seeded data carries demo: true with the 'Demo data' badge and 'Test prices, not market prices'; with the Sandbox adapter against the loopback stub under RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1, labels.testMode and the 'Test mode — local stubs, nothing is real' banner (SEC-3); config refuses any PayPal base URL other than the Sandbox host or a loopback stub in test mode [test/api/labelling.test.js, test/unit/config/hosts.test.js, test/browser/labelling.test.js]

RS-35 [B + I]: the request page answers all six questions (requirements with provenance, decision trace, rejections, cents totals, offer vs commitment, compensation state and next step) with text rendered from planner codes [test/browser/six-questions.test.js]

NFR2 [B]: at 360 px and 1280 px keyboard-only completion of the happy path (with the approval round-trip assertion), visible focus, labelled controls, text status indicators, and the loading, empty, error, retry, timeout, expired-reservation and degraded-extraction states rendered [test/browser/a11y-states.test.js]

NFR3 [D + I]: npm test, npm run test:browser, npm run test:live-model and npm run test:live-paypal are separate scripts; both live scripts refuse without their flag [test/scan/live-refusal.test.js]; live reports are labelled with suite, provider, model or merchant mode and corpus version (inspection of the runners)

NFR5 [D]: planner < 1 s on RS-FIX-1 and on each of the 200 seeded generator catalogs [test/timing/planner-generator.test.js]; p95 over the deterministic API test calls < 300 ms and suite time < 5 min as reported by scripts/report-p95.js

Final tree: scripts/clean-checkout.sh passes (NFR1 re-check); README documents install, seed, start, tests, the one-time npx playwright install chromium, demo accounts (SEC-5), the operator note for retakes (F-TR-15), RS_REGISTER_PER_IP_PER_HOUR (F-TR-17), live runbooks with the env var names and the allow-list, retention, labelling, the Node floor and Q9 branch, MIT licence

docs/evidence-table.md lists all 45 criteria with suite, test names and evidence ids; every live row (LIVE-M1, LIVE-P1, LIVE-P2) is marked Unverified with its blocker; RS-20/RS-26 Sandbox rows say they rest on the fake's model of PayPal until the live run (SEC-18); single-credential weakened rows are labelled (A2); the NFR6 row states RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1 (F-TR-18)
Full regression on the final tree: npm test and npm run test:browser pass

review.summary:
Re-review of plan revision 2 (sub-mv1fa538-015d094f; plan.json f24269c8..., plan.md b40a1112..., revision-2-notes.md 65192cb3...). All checks below were re-run after the submission.

F-PL-1 is resolved. My probe confirms the delivery lead's finding (ev:ev-mv1fc5sm-0102d93f): on Node 22.22, `node --test` with an existing file or a matching glob next to a missing explicit file exits 0. My revision-1 recommendation (name the new files) would therefore not have been enough. The new `ls <files> >/dev/null &&` guard exits 2 before the files exist and 0 after, both under /bin/sh and in eccode evidence run's `shell: true` mode.

My revision-2 plan check (ev:ev-mv1fe3rh-0160b101) finds:
- 28/28 commands start with a guard. Every guard file is explicit and owned by its task, and by no task in an earlier phase, in its dependency closure or in its phase. Every guard includes a test file that the command runs.
- The 19 concurrent pairs still have disjoint ownership, with no record paths.
- All 45 ids are claimed exactly once.
- All 59 traceability test files are owned and run in their claiming phase.
- All 113 test files the tasks name are owned by the task or by an earlier or dependency task.

The delivery lead's guard check, re-run, gives 28/28 (ev:ev-mv1fe3xu-01f0b894), and plan validate is clean (ev:ev-mv1fe448-01c5aeff).

The other findings are also resolved:
- F-PL-2: the budget decision now precedes phase B, and g4 is merged into g3.
- F-PL-3: f1 is barred from changing f2's files and must fail and be re-sequenced if it has to. That is enforceable, because ownership already excludes those files and the RS-15 void path runs through e2's void rule and e4's reconciler wiring into reservations.js, which f1 owns.
- F-PL-4: limits.test.js is in b1's guard.

The .gitignore additions (test/.out/, test/browser/out/) hide only generated output from git-based completion accounting. The lesson decision still holds (ev:ev-mv1feiv1-01239edf).

One new minor (F-PL-5) remains open: e5 and f3 run all frontend unit tests but do not own d4's extraction.test.js.

findings.detail: The frontend commands run "test/unit/frontend/**/*.test.js". e5 owns format, dashboards and payments; f3 owns format, dashboards, payments and recovery. Neither owns test/unit/frontend/extraction.test.js (d4), although both own public/**. resolvedFindings.resolution: Every command now starts with an ls existence guard over explicit files that only that task creates. My probe confirms that naming new files is not enough on Node 22.22, because a missing explicit file is ignored when anything else matches; the guard exits 2 before the files exist and 0 after, including under evidence run's shell mode. My revision-2 check finds 28/28 valid guards, each including a test the command runs. The delivery lead's guard check, re-run, gives 28/28.

plan.md now requires the user's budget decision (raise maxRuntimeMinutes, or accept the descoping order) to be recorded before the first phase-B dispatch. g4 is merged into g3, giving 28 tasks and a 19-dispatch critical path. f1 has a new acceptance criterion: it changes none of void-rule.js, reconciler.js, saga.js, calls.js, admin.js or routes/admin.js, and fails and is re-sequenced after f2 if it would need to. Ownership already excludes those files. RS-15's void path (e2's void rule, e4's reconciler expiry wired into reservations.js, which f1 owns) and the re-plan drain (into supersession.js, f1) need no f2-owned change. The constraint is therefore enforceable and its fallback is explicit.

handoff.completedWork: Wrote package.json first (type module, engines >=22.13, zero dependencies, devDependency @playwright/test 1.56.1, the nine scripts of Testing Strategy > Commands verbatim). Wrote .gitignore, scripts/check-node.cjs (ES5, exports check/meetsFloor, prints the exact message and sets exit code 1), src/index.js (no static imports; floor check, then node:sqlite probe, then dynamic import of main.js), src/main.js (umask 077, config, directories created 0700, openDb, migrate, csrf_key and fake_webhook_secret in meta via INSERT OR IGNORE, listening line with the port, SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown), src/app.js (createApp with injected db, clock, config, log, ai, payments; pipeline request id -> security headers -> Host allow-list 421 -> route or static -> policy -> handler; default deny of non-public policies when no authorize hook is supplied), src/config.js (every Deployment variable, Secret, ConfigError naming variables only, base-URL allow-lists, registration limit, lease rule), src/log.js, src/clock.js (also Intl-based zonedTimeToUtcMs and localDateInZone), src/db/* (connection with PRAGMAs and db.tx, migrate with BEGIN IMMEDIATE per file and checksums, errors, meta helpers, migrations 001-005 byte-identical to the spec fences, checked by ev:ev-mv1g5zww-0182816a), src/http/* (body, cookies, envelope with the full error catalog and AppError, headers with approvalPageCsp, host, request-id, router, server, static, validate), src/routes/* (health and config implemented; auth, requests, plans, orders, paypal, supplier, admin, webhooks are empty register() stubs), scripts/seed.js. Tests: 171 across test/unit/config, db, http and seed, including the eight files named in the verification command. The final run of the task command, recorded as the declared command string (ev:ev-mv1g9bkw-01abf3c8, also ev:ev-mv1g7ma5-01bc9fb8 wrapped in sh -c), passed with 171 tests and the same tests also pass under a loopback-only network guard at concurrency 4 (ev:ev-mv1g7yel-017eb8cd). The failing-state run before any work is ev:ev-mv1fm7gt-0123f65c (existence guard failed).
remainingIssues: Upload timeout: the spec gives uploads 60 s, but Node has one server-wide requestTimeout. server.js sets 30 s and exports UPLOAD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS; task d3 (upload route) must enforce its own 60 s deadline while streaming, or change the server value deliberately.

Password hash format is defined here (scripts/seed.js hashPassword): scrypt$16384$8$1$<salt base64url>$<64-byte key base64url>. Task c1 (src/auth/password.js) must verify exactly this format, since c1 does not own the seed; the dummy hash for unknown users must use the same parameters.

Config refuses placeholder-shaped values for every secret it reads (SEC-5, literal reading of the spec), including unused PayPal and Anthropic ones. A .env.example copied verbatim with <placeholder> values therefore fails startup and seed, naming the variable. Task b4 should ship .env.example with those lines commented out or explain it in the README.

Two AppError classes exist: src/domain/errors.js (b2, constructor (status, code, message, details)) and src/http/envelope.js. The HTTP layer adopts the domain one by duck typing (name AppError, status 400-599, code in the catalog), answering with the catalog message and only plain-object details; the envelope class also accepts the domain-style argument order. A domain error with a code outside the catalog becomes 500 INTERNAL by design.

The router requires a policy on every route and non-public policies are denied with 401 until task c1 passes an authorize hook to createApp (and adds the Origin/CSRF checks, session cookie handling and rate limits, none of which are in b1).

main.js starts only the HTTP server. The fake approval listener, reconciler and retention sweep are added by e1, e4 and d3. The model-provider fallback to fake when the claude binary is absent is left to d1/d3; config only forces fake under RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1.

config.publicUrl is null when RS_PUBLIC_URL is unset (PORT=0 has no port yet). Code needing the app origin must call deps.publicUrl() (http://localhost:<bound port> by default). The log allow-list has one addition to the spec list: port, needed for the harness 'listening' line.

scripts/seed.js embeds RS-FIX-1 as a constant; it was not cross-checked against test/fixtures/rs-fix-1.json (b2's file) because that file was not part of this task. The seed test asserts the brief table values.

The loopback-only guard used in ev:ev-mv1g7yel-017eb8cd is a scratch stand-in (.eccode/drafts/b1-net-guard.mjs) because test/helpers/net-guard.js belongs to b3; re-run these tests under the real guard once it exists.
The ES5 property of check-node.cjs is checked by a regex scan plus real runs on Node 20 and 21, not by an ES5 parser.

handoff.objective: Implement the pure domain layer: money, time, canonical, compat, planner with brute-force oracle, state tables, rescue-status derivation (revision 2) and explanation templates, with the fixture and the unit, property and timing tests of the plan.
handoff.context: Built against the architecture brief (RS-FIX-1, planner rules, state machines, derivation, RS-06..RS-11, RS-36, NFR5) and the design spec (internal module contracts, Rescue status derivation revision 2 rows 1-14 incl. 4a/5a, Testing Strategy). The reference model .eccode/drafts/design-r2-derive-walk.mjs and the reviewer scripts tr-design-r2-derive.mjs / tr-design-derive-totality.mjs were ported into the tests. Memory search for planner, derivation and oracle returned no records.
handoff.expectedOutput: src/domain/{money,time,canonical,compat,planner,oracle,states,derive,explain}.js, test/fixtures/rs-fix-1.json, eight domain unit test files and the NFR5 planner timing test, all passing.
acceptanceCriteria: src/domain imports nothing outside src/domain; the clock is injected; equal inputs give deep-equal outputs

RS-06..RS-11 hold exactly as worded in the brief, each in a test named 'RS-0n: ...' in planner-fixture.test.js, including the multiplicity guard (A on_hand 2 -> Ax2 at 7000, 1 pickup) and RS-12's planner half
planner-oracle.property.test.js compares the planner with oracle.js on 500 seeded random catalogs (<= 6 offers, on_hand 0-3) for feasibility, total, pickups, readyAt and the per-candidate codes
states.js holds the four transition tables of the brief and the OQ-D1 reasons; states.test.js checks every allowed and every refused pair; assertTransition throws AppError(409, INVALID_STATE)

derive.js implements the revision-2 table row by row (rows 1-14 incl. 4a, 5a, row-2 clauses (a) and (b), row-3 unknown-refund clause); derive.test.js has table cases for every row, RS-36 (i)-(iv), reviewer scenarios S09-S20 and the totality property test (25,000 walks x 120 events, row 14 never reached)
money.js uses integer cents, basis-point tax rounded half up per supplier order, toPayPalValue without floating point; time.js converts Asia/Amman local times through Intl, not a constant offset
explain.js renders template text from planner and derive codes, including the brief's exact sentences and the server question templates per field (SEC-7)
test/timing/planner-generator.test.js runs RS-FIX-1 and generator seeds 1-200 with the brief's parameters and asserts < 1 s each (NFR5 planner part)
handoff.completedWork: All nine domain modules plus src/domain/errors.js (the domain's own AppError(status, code, message, details), name 'AppError') exist and pass 110 tests through the plan's verification command. Planner: exact lexicographic search (total, pickups, plan-ready time, sorted supplier-code string, then multiplicity vector) by branch-and-bound over bundle multiplicities 0..min(availability, ceil(need/units)); candidate filter codes INCOMPATIBLE_LID_DIAMETER, READY_AFTER_DEADLINE, OUT_OF_STOCK, OFFER_WITHDRAWN; infeasible output carries per-candidate codes (INSUFFICIENT_QTY, TOO_MANY_PICKUPS, OVER_BUDGET from the cheapest covering combination), computed relaxations (budget, deadline, maxPickups, each re-solved with only that constraint removed) and blocking constraints; up to 3 irredundant ranked alternatives and trace comparisons. RS-FIX-1 results: A+B 8400/2 pickups/10:30; A on_hand 2 -> Ax2 7000/1 pickup; without B A+E 9500/10:40; budget 9000 -> exactly budget 9500 (A+E) and deadline 11:20 (D, 8000) relaxations; max pickups 1 -> A, B, E coded INSUFFICIENT_QTY + TOO_MANY_PICKUPS. The oracle enumerates every 0..availability vector with no pruning and its own constraint logic; 500 seeded catalogs agree on feasibility, best total/pickups/readyAt/suppliers/bundles, alternatives, rejections, candidate codes, relaxations and blocking. Planner time over RS-FIX-1 and seeds 1-200 is about 1 ms each (limit 1 s). Derive: revision-2 table row by row (rows 1, 2 with clauses (a) and (b), 3 with the unknown-refund clause, 4, 4a, 5, 5a, 6, 7-9 with r2 scoping, 10-13, 14 with fallback flag and state vector), consuming persisted rows with the data-model column names. The totality test runs 20,000 default-profile walks plus 5,000 progress-profile walks of 120 events over the composed plan/reservation/payment/fulfilment machines, void rule, hooks, compensation, re-plan queue, admin refunds and clock jumps; every model move is asserted against states.js, every step is compared with the reference table, RS-36 (i)-(iii) are checked as invariants, rows 1-13, 4a and 5a are all hit and row 14 is never reached. A deliberate mutation of the row-3 unknown-refund clause was caught by three tests and reverted. Other decisions: a planner node cap (MAX_SEARCH_NODES 2,000,000, PlannerLimitError with code PLANNER_LIMIT) guards absurd inputs; offers whose capacity or cup diameter differ from the requirement are skipped and marked SPEC_MISMATCH in the trace only (not in rejections, because the Rejection code enum has no such code); excluded suppliers are dropped silently and recorded in trace.inputs; several offers of one supplier form one supplier order (one pickup, largest prep fee, one tax rounding); the fixture file is pinned by sha256 in planner-fixture.test.js.
remainingIssues: Interface for the services (W4): deriveRescueStatus takes persisted rows with snake_case column names (plan_versions, reservations, supplier_orders incl. an optional joined supplier_code, payment_operations, provider_calls, planning_runs, replan_queue as { failed_drains }); the spec only named the argument groups, so this shape is the contract to build the view service against (documented in the header of src/domain/derive.js). Limits are camelCase: { unknownEscalateMin, pendingEscalateMin, replanFailedDrainsBeforeManual } with defaults 15, 1440, 5.

src/domain/errors.js defines its own AppError (domain may not import src/http). The HTTP envelope must map it by duck typing (err.name === 'AppError', status, code, message, details) or re-export this class; two distinct AppError classes will otherwise not satisfy instanceof.
PlannerLimitError (RangeError, code PLANNER_LIMIT) can be thrown for absurd catalogs; the plans service should map it to a typed 4xx/5xx, not let it surface as an untyped 500.

The brief gives the NFR5 generator no deadline or budget; the generator in test/unit/domain/helpers/catalog-gen.js fixes the deadline at 11:30 and draws the budget from 6000-30000 cents (164 of 200 seeds feasible). If the delivery lead wants other values, change those two lines.

Relaxations are emitted in the order budget, deadline, maxPickups (the brief's listing of constraints); RS-11's text in the brief names TOO_MANY_PICKUPS first, so consumers and tests should look relaxations up by constraint, not by position (the tests do).

The derivation's per-row nextStepCode and messageCode values beyond the spec's exact sentences (for example CAPTURES_IN_PROGRESS, AUTHORIZATION_IN_PROGRESS, APPROVAL_CANCELLED) are my choices within the spec's nextStep code set; texts live in explain.js.
Nothing outside the task's ownership globs was changed. The PreToolUse guard refused one attempt (an inline python3 program that wrote a file); the same edit was then made with the Edit tool.

review.summary:
Phase B review of sub-mv1h2gly-014b868a. I read the code against plan.json's task criteria, the approved design and the brief, and ran every declared verification command myself.

What holds:
- b1, b2, b4 and b3 pass: 171, 110, 9 and 364 tests, and the clean checkout passes (ev:ev-mv1h8qn0-01c0fa75, ev:ev-mv1h94yt-010d769d, ev:ev-mv1h959y-01ee5954, ev:ev-mv1h9yvi-018dc008).
- My independent checks (ev:ev-mv1ha378-01c9beab):
  - the five migrations equal the spec DDL;
  - approvalPageCsp and the app CSP equal the spec strings;
  - package.json scripts equal the spec;
  - the planner matches the brief's RS-06..RS-11 wording exactly;
  - on 3000 random catalogs (807 feasible), the planner agrees with my own brute force written from the brief's rules on best plan, rejections, per-candidate codes and relaxations.
- derive.js matches the revision-2 table row by row, including 2(a)/(b), 3's unknown-refund clause, 4a, 5a and 14. states.js matches the brief's four tables and the OQ-D1 reasons.
- Config, host check, body cap, static confinement, check-node.cjs and the harness meet their criteria.

The blocking defect: my own run of the phase suite failed (ev:ev-mv1h5bbh-010aae6e, 363/364).
- NFR1's 'two processes starting at the same time' test died with SQLITE_BUSY 'database is locked' thrown by `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` in src/db/connection.js, although busy_timeout is set first.
- A reproduction failed 1 of 10 isolated runs (ev:ev-mv1h6fnx-0154466d).
- This is a production race on concurrent start against a fresh database. b1's criterion says such a start is safe, and the later multi-process tests (RS-14, RS-20, RS-26, lease-takeover) depend on it.

Minor findings: six design-item tests lack their id, and two deviations need follow-ups in later tasks. The security reviewer's draft (phase-b-security-1.md) did not exist when I recorded this review.

findings.title: Concurrent start on a fresh database fails: PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL throws SQLITE_BUSY despite busy_timeout
findings.detail:
src/db/connection.js sets `PRAGMA busy_timeout` and then `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` (L29-L30). When several processes open a new database file at the same time, SQLite can return SQLITE_BUSY for the journal-mode switch without calling the busy handler. It does this when waiting could deadlock: one connection holds a shared lock and needs an exclusive one while another holds or waits for a write lock.
- In my phase run of `npm test`, 'NFR1: two processes starting at the same time apply each migration exactly once and both succeed' failed: a child exited with 'Error: database is locked' at openDb, connection.js:30 (ev:ev-mv1h5bbh-010aae6e, 363/364).
- The reproduction ran that test 10 times in isolation; 1 failed with the same error (ev:ev-mv1h6fnx-0154466d).
b1's criterion requires that 'a second process starting at the same time skips applied versions', and the spec calls migrations multi-process safe. The later multi-process tests (rs14, rs20, rs26, lease-takeover, return-crash), and any two-server deployment, start processes on one fresh file and would inherit the race as flaky failures or startup crashes. The delivery lead's 364/364 run and my b1/b3 runs passing does not contradict this: the failure is intermittent.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: b1-foundation-core (backend-engineer), src/db/connection.js.
Fix: openDb retries the journal-mode switch, and any other SQLITE_BUSY raised while opening, with a short bounded back-off up to the busy timeout, then gives a clear error. A synchronous sleep such as Atomics.wait on a SharedArrayBuffer is fine.
Add a regression test (or raise the existing one to at least 25 rounds of 3 processes) named with its id.
Resolved when the reviewer's reruns pass: `npm test` and `node .eccode/drafts/tr-phb-migrate-race.mjs 20` with 0 failures.
If a retry does not remove the failures, dispatch learning-debugger on PB-1 to find the root cause.

findings.title: Six tests that prove a design item do not carry its id
findings.recommendation:
Owner: b1-foundation-core (backend-engineer).
Rename the six tests with their ids (ARCH-26, SEC-10, SEC-12, the deployment item as 'SEC-3/T18' or its spec row, RS-14, ARCH-25) in the same rework as PB-1.
Resolved when a name scan of test/unit finds no test that checks a listed design item without its id.

findings.title: Deviations that need follow-ups in later tasks
findings.detail:
I accept these deviations, but each creates an obligation the plan does not yet record:
- PlannerLimitError (PLANNER_LIMIT) must not surface as an untyped 500 from POST /api/requests/:id/plan (c2).
- Offers that fail the capacity or cup-diameter match are recorded only in the trace as SPEC_MISMATCH. The request page's 'What was rejected' (RS-35) will not show them, and no design code exists for them (G review, c5/g1).
- The 60 s upload deadline must be enforced in the upload route (d3).
- The seed's embedded RS-FIX-1 is not cross-checked against test/fixtures/rs-fix-1.json: both are only checked against the brief.
- The two AppError classes rely on duck typing in the envelope; that is tested in app.test.js and acceptable.
findings.recommendation:
Owners: c2 (map PLANNER_LIMIT to a catalogued error, e.g. 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, or 503 with a named code added to the catalog through the orchestrator); d3 (upload deadline); c5/g1 (decide with the orchestrator whether SPEC_MISMATCH offers are shown).
Resolved when each item is named in its task's acceptance criteria or handoff. Optionally, b2 adds a test asserting the seed constant equals the fixture file.

handoff.completedWork: REWORK after phase B review rev-mv1hc5zg-01a3fc75. PB-1 (blocking), root cause: on a fresh database file, PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL needs an exclusive lock. When another process holds or awaits a write lock while this connection holds a shared one, waiting could deadlock, so SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately and never calls the busy handler, so busy_timeout does not help. Reproduced with the reviewer's script (ev:ev-mv1hf138-016b38f3: 3 of 40 sequential runs failed with 'database is locked'; the script always exits 0, so the counts are the result) and with a minimal probe (.eccode/drafts/b1-pb1-probe.mjs, error code 5 from the WAL switch, about 1 in 180 opens). Fix in src/db/connection.js: openDb reads the journal mode first and switches only when the file is not WAL, and both that step and the later pragmas run under retryWhileBusy, a bounded back-off (2 ms doubling to 50 ms with jitter) on SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED up to max(busyTimeoutMs, 1000 ms), after which the busy error is rethrown; the handle is closed on failure. New test/unit/db/open-race.test.js (all named PB-1): retry unit tests, bounded give-up against a real lock-holder process, success when the holder releases, and a stress of 25 rounds x 4 processes on a fresh file. The same reproduction command now shows 0 failures in 160 runs (ev:ev-mv1hidob-01eb30b6); six more stress runs also passed; npm test passes 370/370 (ev:ev-mv1hjizn-013960db); the declared verification command passes with 177 tests (ev:ev-mv1hj5be-01ed33dd). PB-2: six tests renamed with ARCH-26, SEC-10, SEC-12, SEC-3 (RS_TEST_HOOKS row), RS-14 and ARCH-25. Original work: Wrote package.json first (type module, engines >=22.13, zero dependencies, devDependency @playwright/test 1.56.1, the nine scripts of Testing Strategy > Commands verbatim). Wrote .gitignore, scripts/check-node.cjs (ES5, exports check/meetsFloor, prints the exact message and sets exit code 1), src/index.js (no static imports; floor check, then node:sqlite probe, then dynamic import of main.js), src/main.js (umask 077, config, directories created 0700, openDb, migrate, csrf_key and fake_webhook_secret in meta via INSERT OR IGNORE, listening line with the port, SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown), src/app.js (createApp with injected db, clock, config, log, ai, payments; pipeline request id -> security headers -> Host allow-list 421 -> route or static -> policy -> handler; default deny of non-public policies when no authorize hook is supplied), src/config.js (every Deployment variable, Secret, ConfigError naming variables only, base-URL allow-lists, registration limit, lease rule), src/log.js, src/clock.js (also Intl-based zonedTimeToUtcMs and localDateInZone), src/db/* (connection with PRAGMAs and db.tx, migrate with BEGIN IMMEDIATE per file and checksums, errors, meta helpers, migrations 001-005 byte-identical to the spec fences, checked by ev:ev-mv1g5zww-0182816a), src/http/* (body, cookies, envelope with the full error catalog and AppError, headers with approvalPageCsp, host, request-id, router, server, static, validate), src/routes/* (health and config implemented; auth, requests, plans, orders, paypal, supplier, admin, webhooks are empty register() stubs), scripts/seed.js. Tests: 171 across test/unit/config, db, http and seed, including the eight files named in the verification command. The final run of the task command, recorded as the declared command string (ev:ev-mv1g9bkw-01abf3c8, also ev:ev-mv1g7ma5-01bc9fb8 wrapped in sh -c), passed with 171 tests and the same tests also pass under a loopback-only network guard at concurrency 4 (ev:ev-mv1g7yel-017eb8cd). The failing-state run before any work is ev:ev-mv1fm7gt-0123f65c (existence guard failed).
remainingIssues: The reviewer's race script tr-phb-migrate-race.mjs always exits 0, so its pass/fail is read from the printed counts (0 failed in the PB-1 verification run), not from the exit code.

openDb now waits up to max(busy_timeout, 1000 ms) at open time even when RS_DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=0, because the WAL switch happens once per process at startup; ordinary statements still honour the configured timeout.

Upload timeout: the spec gives uploads 60 s, but Node has one server-wide requestTimeout. server.js sets 30 s and exports UPLOAD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS; task d3 (upload route) must enforce its own 60 s deadline while streaming, or change the server value deliberately.

Password hash format is defined here (scripts/seed.js hashPassword): scrypt$16384$8$1$<salt base64url>$<64-byte key base64url>. Task c1 (src/auth/password.js) must verify exactly this format, since c1 does not own the seed; the dummy hash for unknown users must use the same parameters.

Config refuses placeholder-shaped values for every secret it reads (SEC-5, literal reading of the spec), including unused PayPal and Anthropic ones. A .env.example copied verbatim with <placeholder> values therefore fails startup and seed, naming the variable. Task b4 should ship .env.example with those lines commented out or explain it in the README.

Two AppError classes exist: src/domain/errors.js (b2, constructor (status, code, message, details)) and src/http/envelope.js. The HTTP layer adopts the domain one by duck typing (name AppError, status 400-599, code in the catalog), answering with the catalog message and only plain-object details; the envelope class also accepts the domain-style argument order. A domain error with a code outside the catalog becomes 500 INTERNAL by design.

The router requires a policy on every route and non-public policies are denied with 401 until task c1 passes an authorize hook to createApp (and adds the Origin/CSRF checks, session cookie handling and rate limits, none of which are in b1).

main.js starts only the HTTP server. The fake approval listener, reconciler and retention sweep are added by e1, e4 and d3. The model-provider fallback to fake when the claude binary is absent is left to d1/d3; config only forces fake under RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1.

config.publicUrl is null when RS_PUBLIC_URL is unset (PORT=0 has no port yet). Code needing the app origin must call deps.publicUrl() (http://localhost:<bound port> by default). The log allow-list has one addition to the spec list: port, needed for the harness 'listening' line.

scripts/seed.js embeds RS-FIX-1 as a constant; it was not cross-checked against test/fixtures/rs-fix-1.json (b2's file) because that file was not part of this task. The seed test asserts the brief table values.

The loopback-only guard used in ev:ev-mv1g7yel-017eb8cd is a scratch stand-in (.eccode/drafts/b1-net-guard.mjs) because test/helpers/net-guard.js belongs to b3; re-run these tests under the real guard once it exists.
The ES5 property of check-node.cjs is checked by a regex scan plus real runs on Node 20 and 21, not by an ES5 parser.

review.summary:
Re-review of phase B resubmission sub-mv1hokge-01004365, with the security reviewer's draft (phase-b-security-1.md) folded in. Every check below was re-run on the final tree after the resubmission.

PB-1, PB-2 and PB-3 are resolved:
- My strict race check passes with 0 failures in 20 sequential and 60 parallel runs (ev:ev-mv1hrnhg-017cd4f0).
- The new open-race and RS-14 busy tests pass 10 of 10 repeated runs (ev:ev-mv1hu6ju-01ddc12e).
- npm test passes 370/370 (ev:ev-mv1hqgk1-01c28d5d).
- Each task's declared command passes: b1 (ev:ev-mv1hul1f-017e688f), b2 (ev:ev-mv1hvui4-01910b1f), b4 (ev:ev-mv1hvurz-0103d44f), b3 with the clean checkout (ev:ev-mv1hwlgh-010ebdc4).
- The artifact list covers all 110 owned files (ev:ev-mv1hv48h-019aa8d3).
- My independent checks still pass (ev:ev-mv1hwly3-01ca7688).

I confirm the security reviewer's SEC-B-1 as major. I re-ran its planner sweep (ev:ev-mv1ii4ai-01f17e2d): with 100 bundles per supplier (a normal supplier PATCH) and a 10,000-cup request (inside the 1-100,000 range), plan() throws PLANNER_LIMIT after 170 ms. Yet supplier A alone covers the request: with maxPickups 1 the same input is feasible in 0.1 ms. PLANNER_LIMIT appears from availability 30 upward, and single calls hold the event loop for up to 305 ms. The exact planner, b2's deliverable, therefore returns no plan for ordinary, fillable requests. The submission's note that the cap is unreachable holds only at on_hand 1. This must be fixed in src/domain/planner.js before c2 exposes POST /api/requests/:id/plan.

Also confirmed:
- SEC-B-2 (minor): REPLACE bypasses the append-only triggers because recursive_triggers is off. Re-run: ev:ev-mv1iihtv-0176c6cd.
- SEC-B-3 (minor): deep nesting crashes canonicalJson into a 500 (security evidence ev:ev-mv1idwc0-01c3fc7c).

SEC-B-4..9 and PB-4 are info.

findings.title: Planner gives up (PLANNER_LIMIT) on ordinary, fillable requests and holds the event loop up to about 0.3 s
findings.detail:
From the security reviewer's draft, confirmed by my re-run of .eccode/drafts/sec-phb-planner-sweep.mjs (ev:ev-mv1ii4ai-01f17e2d; the security reviewer's run: ev:ev-mv1i9q9c-01ca3c24, ev:ev-mv1i9u6p-0136e358).
- The input is the seeded RS-FIX-1 catalog shape, with each supplier's onHand set to 100 (PATCH /api/supplier/inventory has no upper bound) and a request for 10,000 cups and 10,000 lids (the confirm range is 1-100,000), a large budget, no deadline and maxPickups 5.
- plan() throws PlannerLimitError after 169.8 ms, while the same request with maxPickups 1 is feasible (A, 301,000 cents) in 0.1 ms.
- Across the sweep, PLANNER_LIMIT appears from availability 30 per supplier, about 164 of 540 inputs refuse at availability 500 or more, and the worst call took 304.8 ms.
- Cause: the DFS enumerates every multiplicity vector up to min(availability, need/units) per offer (planner.js L27 MAX_SEARCH_NODES, the dfs, and up to 1 + survivors + 3 searches in plan()). That count grows exponentially in stock levels suppliers can legitimately set.
- The brief's planner is exact and the submission calls the cap unreachable, but that holds only at on_hand 1.
I disagree with the security reviewer's 'would not block'. The defect is in b2's delivered code, not in a later route: c2 will call it as is, and an approval cannot carry an open major. So it is major and fixed now.

findings.title: INSERT OR REPLACE / REPLACE INTO rewrites append-only audit_events and inventory_ledger rows
findings.detail: Confirmed by my re-run of .eccode/drafts/sec-phb-config-db.mjs on the reworked tree (ev:ev-mv1iihtv-0176c6cd; the security reviewer's run: ev:ev-mv1i7xgl-01c089fa). The connection has recursive_triggers=0, so REPLACE conflict resolution deletes without firing the BEFORE DELETE trigger. An audit row's action becomes 'REWRITTEN' and a ledger row's delta_on_hand becomes 500. With recursive_triggers=ON both rewrites are refused and plain appends still work. No current code issues REPLACE, so this is minor, but RS-38's append-only guarantee should not depend on statement style.
findings.recommendation: Owner: b1-foundation-core. Add PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON in openDb, with no migration change, and add a REPLACE case per append-only table to test/unit/db/triggers.test.js, named 'RS-38: ...' or 'SEC-B-2: ...'.

findings.title: A 40 kB deeply nested JSON body passes the body cap and makes canonicalJson throw: 500 instead of 4xx
findings.detail: From the security reviewer's draft (ev:ev-mv1idwc0-01c3fc7c, section H). readJsonObject has no depth limit (body.js L95), and canonicalJson is recursive (body.js L110-L116). A 20,000-deep body of 40,006 bytes, under the cap, overflows the stack when fingerprinted, which the reserve idempotency route (c3) will do. The process survives. Minor: no phase-B route takes a JSON body yet.
findings.recommendation: Owner: b1-foundation-core. Reject JSON nested deeper than a small limit (for example 32) in readJsonBody with 400 INVALID_JSON or 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, or make canonicalJson iterative with the same limit, and add a test named 'SEC-B-3: ...'.

findings.title: RS-14 busy-timeout-0 integration test must start the server before taking the lock
findings.detail: main.js applies the migrations at startup inside db.tx (BEGIN IMMEDIATE). With RS_DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=0, a server started while another process holds the write lock fails at startup; only openDb's pragmas are retried.
findings.recommendation: c6: in the rs14-db-busy test, start the server first, then have the lock holder take BEGIN IMMEDIATE, then call reserve. The delivery lead may add this to followups.md.

findings.title: Slow-connection timeouts act on the 30 s check interval; no maxConnections; timeouts answered 400 not 408
findings.detail: From the security draft (ev:ev-mv1ibkqk-015a9f85, ev:ev-mv1idq7i-019ac792, ev:ev-mv1hsot4-01da707f). Accepted as info: the README recommends a reverse proxy.
findings.recommendation: Optional, b1 or a later task: connectionsCheckingInterval 1000, maxConnections about 512, and 408 for ERR_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.

findings.title: Security info items SEC-B-5..SEC-B-9 (existing data/ mode, no lockfile, scrypt N and whitespace passwords, stale explain.js comment, c1 X-Forwarded-For validation)

Carried over from the security draft without change of severity:
- SEC-B-5: a pre-existing data/ directory is not tightened to 0700.

resolvedFindings.resolution: openDb reads the journal mode, then wraps the WAL switch and the opening pragmas in retryWhileBusy. The loop is bounded (budget max(busy timeout, 1 s)), backs off with jitter from 2 to 50 ms, retries only SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED, rethrows other errors at once, and closes the handle on failure. A regression test covers it with a 25 x 4-process stress run and a bounded give-up against a lock holder. My strict race check passes 0/80, the new timing tests pass 10/10, and npm test passes 370/370.
The six tests are renamed with their ids: ARCH-26, SEC-10, SEC-12, SEC-3 for the RS_TEST_HOOKS row, RS-14 and ARCH-25. They pass in the b1 run.

PB-1 (blocking), root cause: on a fresh database file, PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL needs an exclusive lock. When another process holds or awaits a write lock while this connection holds a shared one, waiting could deadlock, so SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately and never calls the busy handler, so busy_timeout does not help. Reproduced with the reviewer's script (ev:ev-mv1hf138-016b38f3: 3 of 40 sequential runs failed with 'database is locked'; the script always exits 0, so the counts are the result) and with a minimal probe (.eccode/drafts/b1-pb1-probe.mjs, error code 5 from the WAL switch, about 1 in 180 opens). New test/unit/db/open-race.test.js (all named PB-1): retry unit tests, bounded give-up against a real lock-holder process, success when the holder releases, and a stress of 25 rounds x 4 processes on a fresh file.
