This rework is pure planner code and never touches guard or root resolution; every owned write inside the nested record was allowed (no 'has no claimed task' or 'outside the ownership' denial of an owned file), so the wrong-root symptom did not occur.

handoff.objective: Rework the planner search so plan() stays exact and fast for large stock and quantities (phase B re-review finding SEC-B-1): no PLANNER_LIMIT on ordinary input, lexicographic objective and every per-candidate code, rejection, relaxation and blocking output unchanged.
handoff.context: Phase B re-review rev-mv1ijr52-01b2f4b6 (changes_requested) and the security draft SEC-B-1: the old search enumerated every multiplicity vector, exponential in stock, and refused a request one supplier could fill after about 170 ms. Reproduction: .eccode/drafts/sec-phb-planner-sweep.mjs (exit 1 before the fix). Reviewer's independent check: .eccode/drafts/tr-phb-checks.mjs (planner vs its own brute force). The first b2-domain work (modules, derive, states, explain, fixture, tests) is unchanged and was already handed off; this handoff covers only the planner rework.
handoff.expectedOutput: A planner that returns the exact optimum quickly on the API envelope, a named SEC-B-1 timing test, property tests on larger stock, and passing sweep and reviewer checks.
acceptanceCriteria: plan() returns the exact optimum quickly on the inputs the API can accept (seeded catalog shape, availability up to 100,000, quantities up to 100,000, maxPickups up to 5); objective (total, pickups, readyAt, supplier codes, vector) and all per-candidate codes, rejections, relaxations and blocking outputs unchanged
named timing test 'SEC-B-1: stock 100, 10,000 cups → A, under 50 ms' in test/timing
oracle property test extended to larger availability, plus a second property against a slow-but-exact reference on medium ranges
sec-phb-planner-sweep.mjs and tr-phb-checks.mjs exit 0
PLANNER_LIMIT kept only as a defensive guard with its bound stated
the plan's declared verification command passes
handoff.completedWork: Algorithm (new src/domain/search.js, used by planner.js): the search enumerates offer SUBSETS within the pickup cap, smallest first, and solves each subset's covering problem exactly by bounded depth-first search. Pickups, plan-ready time and the supplier-code string depend on the subset alone, so inside a subset only total and vector matter. Pruning is valid and exact: (1) only irredundant plans are enumerated (the optimum is always irredundant: dropping a bundle never raises total, pickups or ready time and gives a smaller vector; the forced offer of a cheapest-cover query is exempt); (2) multiplicities are looped only inside the window [kLo, kHi] that the remaining demand allows; (3) a fractional-knapsack lower bound per dimension (mandatory later bundles, prep fees of unused suppliers, tax-rate scaling less one cent of rounding per touched order) cuts subtrees above the budget or the K-th best plan; (4) ascending canonical vector order lets a subtree that can only tie the K-th best of the same subset be cut, which removes equal-cost plateaus; (5) when no supplier has two members, a dominance table keyed by (position, cups, lids) keeps the K cheapest prefixes per state. Subsets are pre-filtered by a cheap root bound (cover floor plus prep sums). For infeasible requests the cheapest unconstrained cover answers every offer it uses, and any other offer is searched with that cover plus one bundle as its starting incumbent. Results: reproduction (stock 100, 10,000 cups, budget USD 100,000, maxPickups 5) now returns A at 301,000 cents in 0.1 ms, same as maxPickups 1. Sweep: 5,400 inputs, no PLANNER_LIMIT, worst single call 21.5 ms (was 237-305 ms with refusals). Stress (draft b2-planner-stress.mjs): 8,000 seeded-shape inputs with availability up to 100,000, quantities up to 100,000, differing cup/lid quantities and tax: worst 9.7 ms, no limit; 3,000 random-priced 12-offer catalogs: worst 36 ms; 3,000 catalogs with several offers per supplier: worst 23 ms. Tests added: planner-oracle.property.test.js gains (a) brute-force oracle on larger stock (availability up to 7, 100 catalogs), (b) tie-heavy catalogs against the oracle (equal prices, prep fees, ready times, several offers per supplier, 120 catalogs), (c) identical tied offers of one supplier, (d) 250 medium catalogs (availability up to 12, up to 6 offers, quantities up to 3000) against the frozen slow exact reference test/unit/domain/helpers/reference-planner.js, comparing the whole output; planner-fixture.test.js replaces the old absurd-input test with 'SEC-B-1: huge stock and quantity are solved exactly' (12 offers of single cups, 100,000 each, solved in well under 1 s) and a guard test of the node cap through search(..., {maxNodes}); test/timing/planner-sec-b1.test.js has the named test, a 1,008-call grid over the seeded shape (stock 1..100,000, quantity 100..100,000, no PLANNER_LIMIT, each < 100 ms, p95 < 20 ms) and 150 random 12-offer catalogs (each < 250 ms). A mutation (pruning ties across different subsets) was caught by the reference comparison and reverted. The earlier suites (RS-06..RS-11, 500-catalog oracle property, derive totality, states, money, time, explain, NFR5) pass unchanged.
remainingIssues: PLANNER_LIMIT (2,000,000 nodes per search, about 150 ms) is still a real guard, not an unreachable one. It is not reached by the seeded catalog shape, by random-priced catalogs of up to 12 offers, or by catalogs with several offers per supplier within the API ranges (evidence above). It CAN still be reached, and calls can take 150-400 ms (up to about 800 ms when several searches hit it), by deliberately tie-laden catalogs: several suppliers whose bundles of different size cost the same per bundle, quantity of about 50,000 or more, and especially a non-zero tax rate (rounding noise defeats tie pruning); and by catalogs whose bundles hold different numbers of cups and lids (not reachable through the API, which only seeds equal counts) at quantity 100,000. Measured with the adversarial draft script b2-planner-stress.mjs: about 0.1-0.3 % of such inputs hit the cap (ev:ev-mv1jdvnv-01ed0f76 is that script's recorded run and shows one 58 ms call; it exits 1 by design because the script treats any call over 50 ms as a failure). A supplier can set equal prices through PATCH, so this is reachable in principle; exactness for those needs an integer DP over coverage that I did not build in this round. Recommended in c2 regardless: map PlannerLimitError (RangeError, code PLANNER_LIMIT) to a typed 422/503, and add the per-customer rate limit on POST /api/requests/:id/plan and on re-plan drains that the security draft asks for (item 3 of its resolution).
trace.enumerated now counts search nodes of the new method, so its values differ from the first version (no test or contract pins them).
tr-phb-checks.mjs part (1)-(3) (migrations, CSP, package.json) belong to b1 and passed in my run (failures: 0); they may change while b1 is reworked.

Third review of phase B (sub-mv1jn1fv-01d4cc9d, 116 artifacts), responding to rev-mv1ijr52-01b2f4b6. Every check below was re-run on the final tree after the submission.

Baseline:
- npm test passes 390/390 (ev:ev-mv1jozth-01485646).
- Each task's declared command passes: b1 188 (ev:ev-mv1jutcs-01febe09), b2 119 (ev:ev-mv1jv3k8-01ae4b0c), b4 9 (ev:ev-mv1jv3wd-01166e01), b3 390 plus clean checkout (ev:ev-mv1jvwq5-01042767).
- The artifact list equals the ownership set: 114 owned files, 0 missing (ev:ev-mv1jvx1j-0153189b).

SEC-B-1, the new exact subset search:
- It agrees with my independent brute force on 3000 random catalogs under the old seed and under a fresh one, on best plan, rejections, candidate codes and relaxations (ev:ev-mv1ju6ix-019711e2, ev:ev-mv1ju719-01803407).
- It agrees with the frozen reference planner on 1497 fresh-seed medium catalogs, comparing the full output (ev:ev-mv1jtj32-0105247e).
- The security sweep now passes: the 10,000-cup, stock-100 case answers A in 0.1 ms, and the worst call is 38 ms (ev:ev-mv1ju5yu-01993413).

The stated residual: deliberately tie-laden inputs. I probed it myself (ev:ev-mv1ju48g-01caf1f8):
- On the catalog version one can actually produce (the five seeded products, which suppliers can only re-price, re-time and restock), 1500 adversarial tie-laden calls never reach PLANNER_LIMIT; worst 96 ms, p99 11 ms. A supplier-reachable grid of 400 calls is also clean (worst 1.9 ms).
- The cap is reached only on catalogs no version-one route can create: 0.13 % with C confirmed compatible, and 9.4 % with 12 tie-priced offers. Even there it is bounded at 127-291 ms per call.
I therefore resolve SEC-B-1's major and keep the residual as a minor (SEC-B-1R) with RISK-19, FU-1 and FU-8.

Also resolved:
- SEC-B-2: REPLACE is refused with recursive_triggers=1 (ev:ev-mv1jrept-0107908e).
- SEC-B-3: bodies deeper than 32 levels get 422, and the HTTP canonicalJson refuses depth above 32 with TypeError. My independent probe and the hardening tests pass (ev:ev-mv1jyx54-01238917, ev:ev-mv1jyy8n-01a6c4f3). The security reviewer's HTTP probe (ev-mv1jrhzy-0128826d) exits 1 only on its obsolete RangeError expectation, so it is not cited as support.

findings.title: Residual: tie-laden catalogs beyond version one's reachable catalog still reach PLANNER_LIMIT, bounded at about 0.1-0.3 s per call
findings.detail:
My probe (ev:ev-mv1ju48g-01caf1f8) measured three catalog kinds:
- Seeded products, which is all that PATCH can produce: 1500 adversarial calls, 0 refusals, worst 96 ms.
- C confirmed compatible: 0.13 % refusals, worst refused call 127 ms.
- 12 tie-priced offers: 9.4 % refusals, worst 291 ms.
No version-one route can produce the last two. Products and offers come from the seed, and a PATCH only versions the existing offer of an existing product. No route writes compatibility rows. Random-priced 12-offer catalogs pass (the engineer's 150-catalog test, and the NFR5 generator).
My previous resolution condition asked for exact and fast results up to 12 offers. That holds for random prices but not for adversarial ties at 12 offers. I downgrade the remainder from major to minor for three reasons: it is unreachable through version one's API (verified); the cap bounds each call (at most about 0.3 s measured); and c2's typed 422 (FU-1) and per-customer planning rate limit (FU-8) plus RISK-19 cover it if the catalog ever grows.
findings.recommendation: Owners: c2-requests-plans-view (FU-1: PLANNER_LIMIT mapped to a typed 422; FU-8: per-customer planning rate limit, which f1 applies to re-plan drains), and the orchestrator (RISK-19). Any future route that creates offers or compatibility rows must first bring the planner to exact and fast on that larger envelope (for example an integer DP over coverage) or cap the catalog. Resolved when FU-1 and FU-8 are proven in phase C and RISK-19 is either closed or carries this condition.

findings.title: Two canonicalJson implementations; only the HTTP one has a depth limit
findings.detail: src/http/body.js exports a depth-limited canonicalJson (TypeError above 32 levels). src/domain/canonical.js exports a different recursive canonicalJson (used for planHash, offersHash and fingerprints per its header). It has cycle and type checks but no depth limit, and it encodes -0 as 0 while the HTTP one uses JSON.stringify. Neither has a caller in src/ yet. Request bodies cannot exceed 32 levels because readJsonBody refuses them first; my probe confirms the domain encoder handles that deepest accepted body (ev:ev-mv1jyx54-01238917).
findings.recommendation: c-phase route tasks (idempotency fingerprints, planHash) should use one canonical encoder, so the same body cannot produce two different fingerprints, and should only feed it values that passed readJsonBody's depth limit. No change needed in phase B.

resolvedFindings.resolution: The per-offer DFS is replaced by an exact subset search (search.js). It agrees with my brute force on 2 x 3000 random catalogs and with the frozen reference on 1497 medium catalogs, on full output. The security sweep passes: the stock-100, 10,000-cup case gives A in 0.1 ms, worst 38 ms. A named timing test was added (planner-sec-b1.test.js). On every catalog version one can produce, adversarial ties never reach the cap. The residual beyond version one's reachable envelope is tracked as SEC-B-1R (minor), RISK-19, FU-1 and FU-8.

openDb sets PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON. The security reviewer's probe on the final tree shows INSERT OR REPLACE and REPLACE INTO refused for audit_events and inventory_ledger, with plain appends still allowed. SEC-B-2 tests were added to triggers.test.js.

readJsonBody refuses JSON nested deeper than 32 levels with 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, using a non-recursive text scan before JSON.parse. The HTTP canonicalJson stays recursive but refuses depth above 32 with TypeError, so it cannot overflow the stack.
My independent probe passes:
- 20,000-deep and 33-deep text is refused, and 32 levels are accepted.
- Brackets inside strings are ignored.
- canonicalJson throws TypeError on 20,000-deep objects and arrays.
The hardening tests pass 7/7. The security reviewer's HTTP probe (ev-mv1jrhzy-0128826d) exits 1 only on its obsolete expectation that canonicalJson throws RangeError; that is consistent with the fix, but I do not cite it because it failed.
Recorded as FU-10 for c6: the rs14-db-busy test starts the server before the lock holder takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

The server uses connectionsCheckingInterval 1000 and maxConnections 512, and answers timeouts with 408. In the slowloris probe, slow-header connections close at 10-11 s and slow bodies at 30 s, all with 408. The SEC-B-4 hardening tests pass.

Resolved or routed:
- SEC-B-5: an existing data/ is tightened to 0700, with a test.
- SEC-B-9: FU-11 for c1.
- SEC-B-6 (lockfile): decision FU-12.
- The README notes go to FU-9 for g2.
- SEC-B-7 and SEC-B-8 stay info as accepted.

data.title: Phase C proceeds within the remaining recorded budget; the engine's BUDGET_EXCEEDED is the stop
data.decision: The user's instruction to continue is read as reaffirming the full 45-criterion scope without choosing between raising limits.maxRuntimeMinutes and descoping. Phase C dispatches proceed within the roughly 88 recorded minutes left under the 480-minute limit; when the engine refuses with BUDGET_EXCEEDED, work stops and the user is shown the exact terminal command for a limits.raise delegation rather than any workaround. This supersedes the precondition in dec-mv1fgdkd-01182466.
data.rationale: limits.raise is an engine action reserved for the user; the orchestrator neither edits config.json by hand nor bypasses the refusal. Continuing inside the remaining budget delivers the progress the user asked for while keeping the toolkit's own control as the hard stop.
data.alternatives: block all work until the user answers; descope without the user

handoff.objective: Authentication and authorization: sessions, CSRF, sign-in and register throttles, default-deny RBAC, admin bootstrap (ARCH-25, SEC-1, SEC-9, SEC-20, F-TR-17, RS-30, FU-6, FU-11).
handoff.context: Built against spec revision 3 (Authentication ARCH-25, RBAC matrix, Security T4/T6/T7/T8/T24, Rate limiting), the F-TR-17 review finding, followups FU-6 and FU-11, and b1's handoffs (router requires a policy; non-public routes were 401 until an authorize hook exists; seed hash format scrypt$16384$8$1$salt$key). Memory search for auth, throttle, scrypt, session returned nothing; the one lesson shown at claim (guard root resolution) is not about this task.
handoff.expectedOutput: Auth routes csrf/register/signin/signout/session, session store, CSRF, throttles, RBAC access hook wired into createApp, admin bootstrap from RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD, audit service, and tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Routes /api/auth/csrf, register, signin, signout, session as specified; cookie rs_sid HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age 43200, Secure on https; only sha256(id) stored; idle 60 min and absolute 12 h; rotation on sign-in and register (any incoming session destroyed, SEC-20); role always customer on register; RS_ALLOW_SIGNUP=0 -> 403 SIGNUP_DISABLED
CSRF: session-bound X-CSRF-Token on every non-GET route, pre-login HMAC token for signin/register, Origin check -> 403 CSRF_FAILED; POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey is exempt

SEC-1/SEC-9 throttle in SQLite: hard 429 at 5 failures per (username_key, IP) or 20 per IP in 15 min before the password check; cross-IP failures only delay (1-10 s), never refuse; username_key = lower(NFC(trim)); unknown usernames counted alike; identical 401 for unknown user and bad password with a dummy scrypt

F-TR-17: register is limited per IP per hour by RS_REGISTER_PER_IP_PER_HOUR (default 5); auth.test.js runs with the default and asserts the 6th registration from one IP -> 429 with details.limit register_ip

RBAC: every route module declares its policy next to each route; startup fails for a route without one; anonymous 401, wrong role 403, admin routes require role admin; admin account created or updated from RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD (>= 16 chars) as scrypt and disabled when unset (SEC-5)
auth.test.js names its cases with ARCH-25, SEC-1, SEC-9, SEC-13, SEC-20 and asserts no Access-Control-Allow-* header on any response
FU-6: password.js verifies the seed hash format and the dummy hash uses the same parameters; a test signs in a seeded account
FU-11: forwarded client IP validated with net.isIP; invalid falls back to the socket address; test named SEC-B-9
handoff.completedWork: ROUTES (src/routes/auth.js): GET csrf, POST register, POST signin (public; they run Origin + pre-login-or-session CSRF themselves), POST signout (policy session), GET session (public, uses ctx.auth.identify). Cookie rs_sid=<43 chars>; Path=/; Max-Age=43200; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (+Secure when RS_PUBLIC_URL is https); sign-out sends Max-Age=0. Sessions (src/auth/sessions.js): 32 random bytes, only sha256 stored, idle 60 min (last_seen refreshed at most once a minute, a busy DB on that refresh is ignored), absolute 12 h, disabled users do not resolve, disableUser deletes sessions. Sign-in and register destroy the incoming session in the same transaction that creates the new one (SEC-20); an attacker-planted id is never adopted. CSRF (src/auth/csrf.js): pre-login token nonce.hmac (nonce = 8-byte time + 16 random bytes, HMAC-SHA256 with meta csrf_key, 2 h, small future skew), session token compared in constant time, Origin must equal RS_PUBLIC_URL's origin or http(s)://<Host>. Throttle (src/auth/throttle.js): an attempt is counted when admitted, in the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE as the check (so parallel requests cannot overshoot); pair >=5 -> 429 signin_pair, IP >=20 -> 429 signin_ip, both before the password check; >=10 failures for the username across IPs -> delay min(10,(n-9)) s then the password is still checked; success deletes that pair's rows including its own reservation; unknown usernames take the same path and one scrypt against a dummy hash with the seed's parameters; 401 body is identical for unknown, wrong password and disabled. Register limit uses rate_events kind register, key ip:<addr>, reserved after validation and before hashing. Password (src/auth/password.js): async scrypt N=16384 r=8 p=1 key 64, accepts only that format, never throws on malformed hashes. Client IP (src/auth/client-ip.js, FU-11): socket address by default; X-Forwarded-For is ignored unless RS_TRUST_PROXY=1, then only the last hop and only if net.isIP accepts it (IPv4-mapped IPv6 collapsed, IPv6 lower-cased), else the socket address; an invalid value never becomes a throttle key. RBAC (src/auth/rbac.js): authorize(ctx, route) for non-public routes: policy signature is allowed only for POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey (no session, no CSRF) else 403; Origin check on non-GET first; no session -> 401; role mismatch -> 403 FORBIDDEN; then X-CSRF-Token must equal the session token (403 CSRF_FAILED). Admin (src/services/users.js ensureAdmin, called from main.js): scrypt hash from RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD, disabled row with an unusable hash when unset, password change or disable ends the admin sessions, a non-admin 'admin' row stops startup. Audit (src/services/audit.js): sanitised detail (ids and codes only) for auth.signin ok/failed/denied, auth.signout, auth.register ok/failed/denied. src/app.js: builds deps.auth, default access hook is the RBAC hook, an injected authorize still replaces it (b1's test double contract unchanged), ctx gains session/sessionId/identified, clientIp moved to src/auth/client-ip.js. TESTS: test/api/auth.test.js (52 cases) and test/unit/auth/* (67 cases). Criteria to evidence: all of them by ev:ev-mv2pf62t-01198c9f (119 tests pass under the net guard; the test names start with ARCH-25, SEC-1, SEC-9, SEC-13, SEC-20, SEC-B-9, F-TR-17, RS-30, FU-6, T6); failing state before any work ev:ev-mv2p31zi-01021921; full suite npm test 509/509 and NFR5 p95 92 ms ev:ev-mv2pg2ag-0141772a. Decisions: (1) X-Forwarded-For is not trusted by default (spec default is no proxy). (2) The access hook is only called for non-public routes (b1 contract, and b1's own tests register public POST routes), so the two public POST routes check CSRF inside their handlers. (3) Rejecting validation failures before the throttle: a 422 uses no register budget and no sign-in failure row.
remainingIssues: AUTHORIZE HOOK CONTRACT for c2/c3/e-tasks: do not pass an authorize to createApp. Declare the policy on router.add: 'customer' | 'supplier' | 'admin' | 'session' (any signed-in role). The hook runs before the handler and sets ctx.user = {id, username, displayName, role, supplierId, supplierCode}, ctx.session = {idHash, csrfToken, createdAt, expiresAt}, ctx.sessionId. Anonymous 401 UNAUTHENTICATED, wrong role 403 FORBIDDEN, bad Origin or missing/wrong X-CSRF-Token on any non-GET 403 CSRF_FAILED. Scope queries by ctx.user.id (customer) or ctx.user.supplierId (supplier) in SQL. toPublicUser(user) in src/services/users.js gives the contract User object.

Public routes that need the user (PayPal return/cancel 'anonymous -> 303 to sign-in' in the RBAC matrix, per e2) must be registered with policy 'public' and call ctx.auth.identify(ctx) (returns the user or null, never throws) or ctx.auth.requireRole(ctx, ...roles) (401/403). A policy 'customer' route cannot redirect an anonymous caller. A public state-changing route gets no automatic CSRF check: it must call checkOrigin and a token check itself (see guardPreLogin in src/routes/auth.js). test/unit/auth/rbac.test.js asserts that the only public non-GET routes are POST /api/auth/register and POST /api/auth/signin, so a task that adds another will see that test fail and must decide deliberately (update the list in that test, which is owned by c1 and would need a rework or a one-line change agreed with the orchestrator).

The webhook route (e3) must be registered as POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey with policy 'signature'; the hook skips session and CSRF for exactly that method and template and returns 403 for any other 'signature' route. Its own per-IP rate limit (60/min, 'webhook_ip') and ctx.clientIp() are the task's job.

ensureAdmin({db, config, clock}) runs in src/main.js startApp only. Tests that use test/helpers/app-harness.js do not get an admin account unless they call ensureAdmin themselves (see test/api/auth.test.js), and createApp does not provision it. The harness also does not run main.js, so no csrf_key row exists beforehand: createAuth creates it lazily with getOrCreateMeta.

The general per-user limit (300 requests/min, details.limit 'general') and the webhook/extract limits are not part of c1 and are not implemented here; rate_events kind 'general' exists in the schema. If no later task owns the general limit, the delivery lead should assign it (it would sit in the access hook after identification).

The cross-IP delay (1-10 s) uses a real timer (auth.sleep, injectable through createAuth), so API tests that exercise it take about 1 s each and pass record:false to keep NFR5 samples clean. Fixed-clock tests do not make it faster.

IPv6 clients can rotate through a /64 to get a fresh per-IP budget: the throttle key is the full address (the spec says per IP). Not changed; a /64 key would be a small change in src/auth/client-ip.js if the security reviewer wants it.
Registration reveals USERNAME_TAKEN (accepted in the spec as T24 note) and counts against the register budget, which is what limits enumeration.
Latency samples: the sign-in/register tests record their requests through the harness as usual (scrypt is about 50 ms); p95 over the whole suite was 92 ms in the full run.
The seeded RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD check is config's (>= 16 chars, placeholder refusal); ensureAdmin trusts config. The raw environment value is only held in the Secret and in the scrypt call.

inputs: src/domain/explain.js, src/domain/planner.js, src/domain/derive.js (read only, for texts, trace shape and enums)
handoff.expectedOutput: public/index.html, public/css/app.css, public/js/* (api, dom, format, router, store, poll, main, texts, errors, reserve-key, view-helpers), public/js/views/*, public/js/components/*; test/fixtures/contracts/*.json; test/scan/frontend.test.js; test/unit/frontend/format.test.js; test/unit/frontend/dashboards.test.js.
acceptanceCriteria: Hash routes #/signin, #/register, #/requests, #/requests/new (text only in this phase), #/requests/:id, #/supplier/orders, #/supplier/inventory, #/admin; one main#app, persistent #banner, aria-live #announcer

Request page sections 1-6 for the planning stages: status header with next step, 'What you need' with manual inputs for every core field, 'Why this plan' with trace comparisons, 'What was rejected' with blocking constraints, per-candidate codes and relaxation buttons, 'Total' from server cents with 'Test prices, not market prices', 'Supplier commitments' with Catalog offer and Supplier confirmed columns; Approve plan sends planHash and total; Reserve stores the Idempotency-Key in sessionStorage under reserve:<planVersionId>

api.js adds X-CSRF-Token, parses the envelope, aborts at 15 s; states loading, empty, error (message + requestId + Retry) and timeout render; text status indicators, never color alone; data-testid hooks as listed in the spec
DOM built with textContent and attribute setters only; test/scan/frontend.test.js asserts no innerHTML, no inline script or style attribute handlers, no secret-looking value in public/

test/fixtures/contracts/*.json hold example responses taken from the spec's contracts for every route the UI calls in this phase; format helpers tested in test/unit/frontend/format.test.js; dashboards.test.js checks the pure view-model functions of the request, supplier and admin views against the contract fixtures (section order, status text, relaxation buttons, Idempotency-Key reuse)
handoff.completedWork: Criterion 1: router.js parses and role-guards the eight hash routes; index.html has one main#app, #banner and aria-live polite #announcer, a skip link and landmarks; main.js moves focus to the h1 and announces the title on each route change (tests: 'RS-35: hash routes ...', 'NFR2: index.html ...', 'NFR2: each role reaches ...', main.js boot smoke test). Criterion 2: the request page is built from pure view models in components/* (status, fields-table, plan-card, rejections, totals, commitments, compensation, payments) in the order status, need, why, rejected, total, commitments, failure, actions; every field has a manual input (open by default when the extraction is degraded); trace comparisons are written from trace.comparisons ('A+B beats A+E: total $84.00 < $95.00'); rejections come from the planner's rejections array and show the server's template sentence for the code (fixed client template as fallback); infeasible runs show blocking constraints, per-candidate codes and one relaxation button per relaxation that re-confirms all values with the one constraint changed and re-plans; totals are formatted from server cents with the price notice; catalog offer and supplier-confirmed are separate columns; Approve plan sends planId, expectedTotalCents and planHash; Reserve takes its key from getReserveKey(sessionStorage, planId) stored under reserve:<planVersionId> and reuses it on retry/refresh (tests 'RS-16: ...'). Criterion 3: api.js is the only module that touches the network (one globalThis.fetch call site), adds X-CSRF-Token to non-GET calls, fetches the pre-login token when none is held, repeats once after CSRF_FAILED, parses the error envelope into ApiError, aborts at 15 s; notice.js renders loading, empty, error (message, action, request id, Retry) and timeout states; pills and badges always carry words. Criterion 4: dom.js builds nodes with createElement, createTextNode, textContent and setAttribute only and refuses on* attributes, style, srcdoc and non-http(s)/non-app URLs; the scan test asserts no markup parsing, no inline handlers or styles, no eval/Function/string timers, no external origin, no localStorage, no secret-shaped value, imports resolve, every button has a type, every control is built by the labelled form helpers. Criterion 5: 43 contract fixtures (list below), 95 frontend tests. Verification: baseline failed ev:ev-mv2p4dxf-01e156ae (test files absent); plan command passes 95/95; neighbours (http, health-config, all scan tests, frontend) 194/194. RS-34 labels: banner from config.labels (Simulated payments and/or AI, Test mode, single credential), Simulated and PayPal Sandbox badges on every payment element, Demo data badge on suppliers/offers/prices, price notice wherever prices show. FU-3 decision: SPEC_MISMATCH offers are NOT shown under 'What was rejected'; they are listed in the trace part of 'Why this plan' as 'Supplier F: Not a match for your cups (capacity or size)' (testid trace-skipped-<code>), rendered by template from trace.candidates[].skipped; test 'RS-35: FU-3 default ...'. SEC-7: only the server's template lines (explanation.lines, Question.question) are shown; Explanation.rephrased is never rendered. One guard refusal during the work: a command that cd'd and then wrote a relative path was refused; I redid the three edits with the Edit tool.
remainingIssues: FU-3 (for g1): decision recorded - SPEC_MISMATCH offers are shown in the trace list of 'Why this plan' (templated line 'Not a match for your cups (capacity or size)'), not under 'What was rejected'. g1 should verify this on the six-answer page; the planner has to keep writing skipped:'SPEC_MISMATCH' into trace.candidates for the line to appear.

Not run in a browser: this environment has no Playwright or Chromium. Everything is checked DOM-free (fake document) under node --test, including a boot smoke test of main.js. c6's browser suite should assert: no horizontal scroll at 360 px; visible 3 px focus; no CSP violation on load (module script, /favicon.svg, no inline style); focus on the h1 after each route change; the PayPal round trip (location.assign to the approval URL, then #/requests/:id?paypal=returned|cancelled&order=<id>); keyboard-only happy path; polling every 2 s while the status is transient and pause when hidden; the Retry and timeout states.

Fixture wrapper: each file is {route, status, variant?, headers?, request?, response}. c6's contract test should compare `response` by key set and field types, not by values. Success fixtures cover: GET /api/config (2 variants), GET /api/auth/csrf, GET /api/auth/session (customer, anonymous), POST /api/auth/signin|register|signout, GET|POST /api/requests, GET|DELETE /api/requests/:id (planned, reserved, infeasible, degraded views), POST extract|confirm|plan (feasible, infeasible), approve, reserve, paypal/create, execute (202 and 200 replay), abandon, receipt, GET /api/supplier/orders, supplier confirm|refuse|ready|handover, GET|PATCH /api/supplier/inventory, POST /api/admin/reset, POST /api/admin/faults, GET /api/admin/timeline, GET /api/admin/metrics; error envelopes: PLAN_CHANGED, RESERVATION_LIMIT, VALIDATION_FAILED, UNAUTHENTICATED, RESET_BLOCKED. Not covered because the UI does not call them in this phase: image upload/download, GET /api/health, PayPal return/cancel redirects, webhooks.

Contract gap (c2): the reserve button must explain 'You already hold stock for another request ... ' with a link to that request, but RESERVATION_LIMIT details carry only reservationIds, not a request id. The link therefore goes to #/requests. If c2 adds a request id to details, errors.js should link to it.

Contract gaps to confirm in c2/c3: (a) SupplierOrder.commitment is not typed in the spec; the fixture and UI assume the Order.commitment shape {bundles, readyAt, confirmedAt}. (b) GET /api/admin/timeline `cursor` is not typed; fixtures use integers and the UI passes the last cursor back unchanged as afterId. (c) Trace.candidates is object[]; the UI reads supplierCode and skipped only. (d) Request intakeStatus values draft|extracted|confirmed are taken from migration 002, not from the spec text.

The request page decides which action button to show from rescueStatus.nextStep.code (APPROVE_PLAN, RESERVE, APPROVE_PAYMENTS, RETRY_APPROVAL_OR_ABANDON, COMPLETE_PURCHASE, REPLAN, PLAN) together with plan and order state. c2's view service must keep those codes consistent with the plan state (for example APPROVE_PLAN only while the current plan is proposed); c6 should assert it.
Explanation.rephrased (opt-in AI rephrasing, off by default) is never rendered; if rephrasing is enabled later, a separately labelled 'AI-rephrased' block must be added and the SEC-7 test updated.
The scan test's secret patterns include a 40-character token regex; a future legitimate long literal in public/ would need an explicit allowance in the test rather than a weaker pattern.

handoff.objective: Requests, manual requirement confirmation, planning runs, plan approval and the request view with a derived rescue status (spec: Customer routes, Shared response objects, Rescue status derivation), with the plan follow-ups FU-1, FU-7 and FU-8.
handoff.context: Built against spec revision 3 (Interface Contracts > Customer routes, Error catalog, Data Design 002/003, Rescue status derivation, Supersession basics), b2's snake_case derive input (FU-7, header of src/domain/derive.js), c1's authorize contract (policy 'customer' on router.add, scope SQL by ctx.user.id) and the contract fixtures under test/fixtures/contracts. Memory search for 'planner limit', 'derive' and 'idempotency' returned nothing; the one lesson retrieved at claim (mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102) concerns a tool-call guard's root resolution and does not apply (see lessonDecisions). The orchestrator's snapshot commits landed mid-claim (src files and the first test file are already in HEAD); that is expected.
handoff.expectedOutput: src/services/{requests,plans,view}.js, src/routes/{requests,plans}.js, the createApp wiring in src/app.js, and test/api/{approve-guards,requests-plans,rescue-status,schema-no-rescue-status}.test.js.
acceptanceCriteria: Every customer query is owner-scoped in SQL; a foreign or archived id -> 404
POST /api/requests counts and inserts in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE (RS_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_CUSTOMER_PER_DAY, Asia/Amman day) -> 429 requests_per_day (SEC-2)
POST /api/requests/:id/confirm takes values only; without an extraction every confirmed field gets provenance manual; REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE for missing core fields; a new requirements version
POST /api/requests/:id/plan stores the planning run and a proposed version (plan_json, alternatives, planHash, trace, explanation) or an infeasible run with blocking, candidate codes and relaxations

RS-12: approve requires expectedTotalCents and planHash; mismatch -> 409 PLAN_CHANGED with current values; stored plan failing re-validation -> 409 PLAN_INVALID; approve with budget or deadline missing -> 409 MISSING_BUDGET / MISSING_DEADLINE (budget first)

RS-36: GET /api/requests/:id returns RequestView whose rescueStatus is computed by derive.js on each read with one query per table; schema-no-rescue-status.test.js finds no column named like rescue status and no status column on rescue_requests
Labels object on every response with seeded prices (priceNotice, demoData) and demo flags on supplier, offer and product objects
FU-1: a planner limit is a typed 422 VALIDATION_FAILED (plan / planner_limit), no run stored, status unchanged
FU-7: the view service builds deriveRescueStatus input in the snake_case shape of derive.js
FU-8: POST /api/requests/:id/plan is rate-limited per customer in rate_events with 429 RATE_LIMITED, details.limit plan, Retry-After
handoff.completedWork: ROUTES (policy 'customer'): GET /api/requests (newest 100, rescueStatus {status,nextStep}, totalCents of the current non-closed plan, labels), POST /api/requests (201 {request:{id,createdAt,language,intakeStatus:'draft'}}), GET /api/requests/:id (RequestView), POST /api/requests/:id/confirm (201 {requirements,rescueStatus}), POST /api/requests/:id/plan (201 {planningRun, plan|null, labels}), POST /api/plans/:id/approve (200 {plan, approvalsNeeded, labels}). A foreign, archived or deleted id is 404, checked before the body is read; malformed ids are 400. REQUESTS (services/requests.js): the Asia/Amman day count (rate_events kind request_create, key u:<id>) and the insert share one BEGIN IMMEDIATE; the 11th is 429 requests_per_day with Retry-After to local midnight; deleting requests does not reset the count. language is detected from Arabic/Latin letter shares. CONFIRM: only the nine values are read (a client provenance is ignored, SEC-8); provenance and originalWording are kept from the latest usable (schema_ok, not degraded) extraction only when the submitted value equals the extracted known value, otherwise manual; empty fields are unknown/none; core fields are productType, cupQuantity, lidQuantity, capacityMl, diameterMm, maxPickups (missing -> 422 REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE with details.fields, bad value -> 422 VALIDATION_FAILED); budget and deadline are optional here so the plan can be made but not approved (RS-04); a contradictory productType/quantity pair is refused (cups needs lidQuantity 0, lids needs cupQuantity 0, cups_and_lids needs both >= 1); every confirm is a new version; an executing/executed version -> 409 PLAN_IN_PROGRESS; a change of values supersedes proposed/approved versions (REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED) and queues a replan_queue entry (status replanning, row 4a) that the next plan removes. PLANNING (services/plans.js): runPlanningFor takes a catalog snapshot (bundle offers with cup and lid items, availability = on_hand - reserved, confirmed compatibility, suppliers that refused an order of this request excluded), runs the planner outside any transaction, then in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE re-reads the snapshot and refuses to store a result computed on a changed catalog (offers_hash and requirements version; up to 3 attempts, then 503 DB_BUSY); it stores the planning run (trace, rejections, candidate codes, relaxations, blocking, excluded suppliers, offers_hash) and, if feasible, a proposed version (plan_json = PlanBody, planHash = canonicalHash(body), alternatives, total, pickups, ready_at), supersedes earlier open versions (REPLANNED) and points them at the new one, deletes the replan_queue entry, audits. FU-1: PlannerLimitError/code PLANNER_LIMIT -> 422 VALIDATION_FAILED details.fields [{field:'plan',rule:'planner_limit'}]; nothing stored; the slot is still counted. FU-8: takePlanSlot counts per customer in rate_events (kind 'general', key 'plan:u:<id>'; 002_requests.sql CHECK has no 'plan' kind and migrations are outside this task) in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, default 10 per 10 minutes, 429 RATE_LIMITED details.limit 'plan' with Retry-After; only a request that would run the planner uses a slot (404 and no-requirements 409 do not). APPROVE: 404 -> body 422 (expectedTotalCents int, planHash 64 lowercase hex) -> superseded 409 PLAN_SUPERSEDED / non_executable 409 PLAN_NOT_EXECUTABLE (details.reason) / approved with same hash and total 200 unchanged / other states 409 INVALID_STATE -> MISSING_BUDGET then MISSING_DEADLINE (from the requirements version the plan was made for) -> server re-validation (hash of the stored body, cups/lids >= required, pickups <= max, totals consistent, budget, deadline) 409 PLAN_INVALID with details.reason -> hash/total mismatch 409 PLAN_CHANGED with details {currentPlanHash, currentTotalCents} -> CAS proposed->approved, plan_approvals row, audit; refused guards are audited as 'denied' with the code only. VIEW (services/view.js): loadRequestData does one SELECT per table for all requests asked for (images, extractions, requirements, planning_runs, plan_versions, reservations, reservation_items, supplier_orders, payment_operations, provider_calls, pickup_confirmations, replan_queue) in one read snapshot; deriveInput hands derive.js the snake_case rows and camelCase limits from config (FU-7); the rescue status is derived on every read (nothing is stored) and explained with explain.js templates; row 14 logs derive.fallback (code DERIVE_FALLBACK, requestRef). The RequestView carries request, extraction, requirements, planning (latest run of the current requirements version), plans (newest first), currentPlanId, reservation, orders, cancellingOrders (older versions with outstanding voids/refunds), rescueStatus with underlying, labels. app.js: createApp now takes planner (default domain planner(), read per request so a test can inject one), planRate ({limit, windowMs}; else config.planRateLimit/planRateWindowMin when present, else 10 per 10 min) and voidRule (c3's hook); resolvePlanRate is exported. TESTS: 65 cases in the four files under the net guard, named by criterion (RS-12, RS-04, RS-27, RS-36 (i)-(iv), SEC-2, SEC-8, PB-3/RISK-19, FU-1/FU-7/FU-8, RS-34, RS-09, RS-19, RS-30). Full suite 669/669, NFR5 p95 69.8 ms.
remainingIssues: FU-8 is only partly delivered: the limit is configurable through createApp({planRate}) and through config.planRateLimit / config.planRateWindowMin (app.js already reads them), but src/config.js and .env.example are outside this task's files, so no environment variable exists yet. Needs a small change by whoever owns them (delivery-lead to assign): RS_PLAN_RATE_LIMIT (integer 1-1000, default 10) and RS_PLAN_RATE_WINDOW_MIN (integer 1-1440, default 10) parsed into planRateLimit / planRateWindowMin, both listed in .env.example (test/scan/env-example.test.js checks the names). The new details.limit value 'plan' must also be added to the catalogued list in the spec (decision dec-mv1jopyn-01ba1096 per the dispatch).

rate_events.kind has no 'plan' value, so planning is counted under kind 'general' with user_key 'plan:u:<userId>'. The general 300/min per-user limit (c1's open item, still unassigned, NOT taken here) must key on 'u:<userId>' and must not count 'plan:' keys; if a later task wants a dedicated kind it needs a new migration (migrations are append-only).

The contract fixtures (owned by c5) show plan-create and plan-approve responses without `labels` and with supplierName 'Supplier A'. This task follows the spec's convention (any response with seeded prices carries labels) and so adds a top-level `labels` to POST /plan and POST /approve; supplierName is the planner default 'Supplier <code>'. If a contract test compares exact key sets, the fixtures or this choice need aligning.

Void-rule hook for c3: supersedeOpenVersions (services/plans.js) refuses with 409 PLAN_IN_PROGRESS when a version to supersede holds a live reservation (active, consumed, reconciling) and no ctx.voidRule is configured, so stock is never left reserved under a superseded plan. c3 must wire createApp({voidRule}) with voidRule(db, {planVersionId, reason}), called inside the superseding transaction and expected to release the reservation and cancel the operations; the status update to superseded is done by supersedeOpenVersions afterwards. f1 extends the same function for offer-change supersession.

Only bundle offers (a bundle product with a cup item and a lid item) are planned; single cup or lid offers are skipped. Order.commitment sums committed_qty_json as an array of {offerId, committedBundles|bundles} or an object of numbers (c3/e3 own that column's final shape). Order.presentation treats every order of a non_executable plan as cancelled_payment_incomplete unless refused, cancelled or refunded.

Not in this task: DELETE /api/requests/:id, image and extract routes, reserve/execute/abandon, the re-plan drain (f1) and the general rate limit. Status 'draft' is never written to plan_versions (versions are inserted as proposed).
The guard refused one attempt: an inline node program that rewrote part of a test file (writeFileSync); the same change was then made with the Edit tool.

handoff.completedWork:
RESERVE (services/reservations.js, route in routes/plans.js): one db.tx = BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Order: key row by (user,key) -> same fingerprint (sha256 of 'POST /api/plans/<id>/reserve\n'+canonical body) replays the stored status and body with Idempotent-Replayed: true, another fingerprint is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; no key row -> reservations by (customer,key): same plan replays the current reservation (200), another plan 422; then plan guards (PLAN_SUPERSEDED, PLAN_NOT_EXECUTABLE, ALREADY_RESERVED, INVALID_STATE, MISSING_BUDGET before MISSING_DEADLINE, PLAN_INVALID via revalidateStoredPlan); then the cap (count of the customer's active reservations >= config.maxLiveReservationsPerCustomer -> 409 RESERVATION_LIMIT details.reservationIds, not stored); then the reservation row, a conditional UPDATE per product (reserved+q<=on_hand) with a reserve ledger row, items, one supplier order (awaiting_supplier) and one created payment operation per supplier (merchant key DEFAULT in single-credential mode), audit, and the stored 201. A withdrawn or replaced offer counts as no stock. OUT_OF_STOCK (details.supplierCodes, newPlanVersionId null) rolls back; a second tx marks the plan non_executable (OUT_OF_STOCK) through the void rule, queues replan_queue and stores the 409; PLAN_*, MISSING_* and OUT_OF_STOCK refusals are stored under the key, RESERVATION_LIMIT, ALREADY_RESERVED, INVALID_STATE and 5xx are not. A UNIQUE violation is caught and re-resolved against what the winner committed. SQLITE_BUSY reaches the app's mapDbError (503 DB_BUSY, Retry-After 1). Refusals are audited as denied. Header Idempotency-Key: missing 400, malformed or repeated 422 VALIDATION_FAILED; a foreign plan is 404 before the header is read.

LEDGER (services/ledger.js): reserveStock, releaseStock, setOnHand (restock/adjust), resetInventory, closeReservation (active->released|expired, one release/expire row per item); one ledger row per change, so SUM(delta) = column holds (asserted in three test files).

VOID RULE (services/void-rule.js): createVoidRule({clock, provider}) returns voidRule(db,{planVersionId, reason, actor, requestId}), run inside the superseding transaction: releases an active reservation (release rows), cancels awaiting_supplier/confirmed orders, marks every non-terminal operation (cancel_requested_at, cancel_reason) and voids created / approved-without-authorize / approved-with-queued-authorize operations locally (queued calls -> cancelled), queues so:<id>:void:1 for authorized ones through provider.queueVoid(db,intent), and leaves authorization_pending, approved with a started or unknown authorize call, and unknown to the protocol. createApp now builds it by default (deps.voidRule) from the clock and createApp({voidProvider}) (default createNoopProvider(), a recorder that sends nothing); createApp({voidRule}) still overrides it.

SUPERSESSION (services/supersession.js): supersedeForOfferChange(ctx,{changes:[{offerId,reason}], drops:[{productId,newOnHand}], actor}) selects proposed/approved versions that use the old offer (json_each over plan_json lines) where the affected supplier's order is not confirmed or later, plus on_hand drops whose planned quantity exceeds on_hand-reserved+own reservation; approved ones get the void rule; each becomes superseded with the reason and the request is queued in replan_queue. markNonExecutable(ctx,{planVersionId,reason,detail,actor}) (approved->non_executable + void rule) and enqueueReplan are shared by refusal, expiry, OUT_OF_STOCK, reset.

SUPPLIER (services/orders.js, routes/supplier.js): list (status filter, 400 on an unknown status), confirm (COMMITMENT_INVALID: unknown/missing/duplicate offer, below planned, after deadline; identical repeat 200; reservation expired 409 RESERVATION_EXPIRED), refuse (order refused, markNonExecutable SUPPLIER_REFUSED with {supplierCode, refusal}, void rule, replan queued, ORDER_EXECUTED after the claim, repeat 200), ready and handover (HANDOVER_BLOCKED unless the plan is executed and no operation is unknown/capture_pending/refund_*, reservation not reconciling; pickup_confirmations row), inventory GET and PATCH (whole-PATCH ownership first: any foreign product 403, then unknown 404; per item a new offer version with the old row replaced, setOnHand with RESERVED_STOCK, supersession in the same tx, response items + superseded ids). Another supplier's order is 404 before the body is read. Refused transitions are audited as denied.

EXPIRY (reservations.js expireDueReservations(ctx,{limit})): CAS active->expired on expires_at<=now, expire rows, plan non_executable (RESERVATION_EXPIRED), void rule; second pass finds nothing; consumed rows never match. The reconciler (e4) calls it.

ADMIN (services/admin.js, routes/admin.js): reset (guard read inside the write tx, 409 RESET_BLOCKED with details.operations; approved plans -> non_executable DEMO_RESET through the void rule; operations and provider_calls archived, never deleted; requests tombstoned (raw_text null, archived_at, images/extractions/replan_queue deleted, originalWording nulled, image files unlinked after commit); catalog restored from the version-1 offers and the seed ledger rows with admin_reset adjust rows; fake_paypal_* tables, fault_flags, request_create and plan:* rate events cleared; own audit row carrying actor and reason; force needs reason 10-500; stranded listed when an operation is not terminal afterwards), faults (stock_depletion withdraws the active offers and supersedes via the same service as the supplier PATCH; supplier_refusal calls refuseSupplierOrder per open order; refund_order; fake_paypal / fake_model flags; clear; FAULTS_UNAVAILABLE with a real adapter; test-only faults need RS_TEST_HOOKS; each audited with actor and target ids), timeline (audit + ledger + provider_call + webhook, time order, requestId filter, afterId/limit paging) and metrics.

TESTS: 81 cases in six files under the net guard, named by criterion (RS-14, RS-15 (part), RS-16, RS-27, RS-28, RS-30, RS-13 offer-change half, RS-17 supplier half, RS-32 admin half, RS-37, SEC-2, SEC-11, F-TR-15), including a held write lock with busy_timeout 0 (server started first, FU-10 style) and key-set comparisons with the contract fixtures.
remainingIssues: 1. CONFLICT WITH A c2 TEST (the full suite is red by exactly this case, ev:ev-mv2r5ewg-01518bd8: 750 tests, 749 pass, 1 fail). test/api/requests-plans.test.js, case 'confirm: an executing or executed plan version is 409 PLAN_IN_PROGRESS; a live reservation without the void rule is refused too' asserts the old fail-closed stopgap: a requirements change over an APPROVED plan holding an ACTIVE reservation is refused 409. With the void rule wired by default (the spec: a requirements change supersedes proposed/approved versions, void rule) that confirm now succeeds (201), supersedes the plan (REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED), releases the reservation with release rows and queues a re-plan. The executing/executed half of that case is unchanged. The file is c2's, outside my globs, so I did not edit it. Fix (c2 rework or the orchestrator): in that case replace the 'live' assertions with status 201, plan status superseded with supersede_reason REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED, reservation released, and keep the 'running' (executing) assertion at 409 PLAN_IN_PROGRESS. The alternative (not wiring the rule by default) would leave refusal, expiry, offer changes and the reset without the rule.

2. Re-plan drains are not done here (f1/e4): supersession, refusal, OUT_OF_STOCK and stock_depletion put the request in replan_queue and the request reads 'replanning'; the customer re-plans with POST /api/requests/:id/plan, which removes the entry. RS-32's replacement journey needs the drain (or that click).

3. Provider voids: only the port exists. With the default no-op recorder an `authorized` operation gets cancel_requested_at and a recorded intent but no provider_calls row. e2 must pass a provider whose queueVoid does INSERT OR IGNORE into provider_calls (key so:<supplierOrderId>:void:1, status intent, started_at NULL) via createApp({voidProvider}) and add the resolution hook and void-result handling; sending is the caller's/reconciler's job. The forced reset (spec steps 1-2: send voids, bounded read-resolve pass) is therefore only partly delivered: it queues through the port, archives, and lists every non-terminal operation in `stranded` and in the audit event.
4. refund_order is minimal: it moves captured -> refund_requested under an executed plan and queues so:<id>:refund:1 (INSERT OR IGNORE, status intent). The saga/reconciler (e4) must send it.

5. Conventions e1/d-phase consumers should follow: fault_flags rows are name '<kind>:<fault>' ('fake_paypal:authorize_denied', 'fake_paypal:lost_response:authorize', 'fake_model:timeout'), value = supplier code or '', remaining = count or NULL (until cleared). metrics reads meta keys reconciler_last_tick_at and reconciler_last_tick_ms (null until e4 writes them).

6. Contract-fixture mismatches (fixtures are c5's; I followed the spec): (a) supplier-order-confirm.json shows canMarkReady true right after confirm with the plan only approved; the brief (state table confirmed->ready: plan executed and no unsettled operation, else HANDOVER_BLOCKED) and this task's criterion make it false until the plan is executed, so the fixture should show false (or an executed-plan variant). (b) plan-reserve.json has no `labels`; the reserve response carries labels (spec Labels convention: seeded prices), as c2's plan responses do. (c) admin-timeline.json shows integer cursors; the cursor is an opaque STRING '<atMs>.<sourceIndex>.<rowId>' (a stable merge key across four tables), so any contract test that types cursor from the fixture must accept a string, or the fixture must change. (d) admin-reset.json is consistent: `stranded` is present only when non-empty. SupplierOrder.commitment {bundles, readyAt, confirmedAt} and RESERVATION_LIMIT details.reservationIds match the fixtures as assumed. Supplier-order and inventory item key sets equal the fixtures' (asserted in supplier-orders.test.js).

7. Spec ambiguity decided: the Conventions say the stored status and body are replayed (so a replay of the first answer is 201 with Idempotent-Replayed: true) while the route table says '201 (new) or 200 (replay)'; I replay the stored status from the key row and answer 200 for the purged-key path (reservation row as guard), as the Conventions word it. If the reviewer wants 200 everywhere, it is one line in resolveExisting/replayStored.

8. The reset's audit row is written directly (not through recordAudit) because recordAudit drops free text and the spec wants the operator's reason recorded; the reason is admin-typed 10-500 characters, never request data.

9. The two-OS-process RS-14 tests belong to c6; reserve is correct for them (check and insert in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, OUT_OF_STOCK not a lock error); FU-5 regression watch: any 'database is locked' at open in those tests is a regression of src/db/connection.js. The general 300/min per-user limit is still unassigned (c1's open item).

REQUESTS (services/requests.js): the Asia/Amman day count (rate_events kind request_create, key u:<id>) and the insert share one BEGIN IMMEDIATE; the 11th is 429 requests_per_day with Retry-After to local midnight; deleting requests does not reset the count. language is detected from Arabic/Latin letter shares. PLANNING (services/plans.js): runPlanningFor takes a catalog snapshot (bundle offers with cup and lid items, availability = on_hand - reserved, confirmed compatibility, suppliers that refused an order of this request excluded), runs the planner outside any transaction, then in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE re-reads the snapshot and refuses to store a result computed on a changed catalog (offers_hash and requirements version; up to 3 attempts, then 503 DB_BUSY); it stores the planning run (trace, rejections, candidate codes, relaxations, blocking, excluded suppliers, offers_hash) and, if feasible, a proposed version (plan_json = PlanBody, planHash = canonicalHash(body), alternatives, total, pickups, ready_at), supersedes earlier open versions (REPLANNED) and points them at the new one, deletes the replan_queue entry, audits. FU-1: PlannerLimitError/code PLANNER_LIMIT -> 422 VALIDATION_FAILED details.fields [{field:'plan',rule:'planner_limit'}]; nothing stored; the slot is still counted. FU-8: takePlanSlot counts per customer in rate_events (kind 'general', key 'plan:u:<id>'; 002_requests.sql CHECK has no 'plan' kind and migrations are outside this task) in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, default 10 per 10 minutes, 429 RATE_LIMITED details.limit 'plan' with Retry-After; only a request that would run the planner uses a slot (404 and no-requirements 409 do not). APPROVE: 404 -> body 422 (expectedTotalCents int, planHash 64 lowercase hex) -> superseded 409 PLAN_SUPERSEDED / non_executable 409 PLAN_NOT_EXECUTABLE (details.reason) / approved with same hash and total 200 unchanged / other states 409 INVALID_STATE -> MISSING_BUDGET then MISSING_DEADLINE (from the requirements version the plan was made for) -> server re-validation (hash of the stored body, cups/lids >= required, pickups <= max, totals consistent, budget, deadline) 409 PLAN_INVALID with details.reason -> hash/total mismatch 409 PLAN_CHANGED with details {currentPlanHash, currentTotalCents} -> CAS proposed->approved, plan_approvals row, audit; refused guards are audited as 'denied' with the code only. VIEW (services/view.js): loadRequestData does one SELECT per table for all requests asked for (images, extractions, requirements, planning_runs, plan_versions, reservations, reservation_items, supplier_orders, payment_operations, provider_calls, pickup_confirmations, replan_queue) in one read snapshot; deriveInput hands derive.js the snake_case rows and camelCase limits from config (FU-7); the rescue status is derived on every read (nothing is stored) and explained with explain.js templates; row 14 logs derive.fallback (code DERIVE_FALLBACK, requestRef). review.summary:
First technical review of phase C (sub-mv2y7tlh-017e22c9, 139 artifacts). I read the code (not the summaries) and re-ran every declared check after the submission, on the final tree.

Baseline:
- npm test: 804 tests, 788 pass, 10 skipped, 6 todo, 0 fail; NFR5 p95 125.6 ms over 1612 calls (ev:ev-mv2ybl0f-013c354c).
- npm run test:browser: 3/3 (ev:ev-mv2ybx3o-01f85564).
- Each task's declared command passes: c1 119 (ev:ev-mv2yk2rh-01c06905), c2 65 (ev:ev-mv2ykgn0-01adbf47), c3 81 (ev:ev-mv2ykous-01b934a1), c5 95 (ev:ev-mv2ykpdu-0144a41b), c6 npm test + browser (ev:ev-mv2ylocq-01972c4e).
- Artifacts: every file changed since c1's base c1614468 under phase-C ownership is listed, every listed sha256 equals the file now, nothing listed outside the ownership (ev:ev-mv2yu4qy-019d189e).

Independent probes:
- RS-14/RS-16 across processes: c6's two-process and DB_BUSY tests three times over (ev:ev-mv2ym79u-01cb8774), and my own race with four customers per round plus one customer's same key sent to both processes at once, pair first or last, 14 rounds: always one active reservation, every loser 409 OUT_OF_STOCK, the same-key pair agrees (201 + replay, or 409 + replay), A reserved 1 of 1, one reserve ledger row per item, loser plans non_executable, no lock error in either log (ev:ev-mv2ymhqs-01a776ec, ev:ev-mv2yn0fs-01877ed0).
- A seeded random walk through the live API (3 x 800 steps: create/confirm/re-confirm, plan, approve and tampered approve, reserve/replay/key on another plan, supplier confirm/refuse/ready, every inventory PATCH kind, clock jumps with the expiry pass run twice, admin stock_depletion/supplier_refusal/reset). After every step: reserved equals the active reservations' items, ledger sums equal on_hand and reserved, reserved <= on_hand, no active reservation, open order or created operation under a superseded or non_executable version, one reserve and one release/expire row per item, no 5xx, no derive.fallback, no view in row 14, the second expiry pass is a no-op (ev:ev-mv2yoajb-01a1e3b6). No path left stock reserved, an order open on a closed plan, or a ledger row missing.
- RS-36 (i)-(iv) on the live endpoint, including (iv) through the real supplier refusal route; the schema has no rescue-status column (ev:ev-mv2ypyue-019d3b1a).
- RBAC over the live route table x 4 actors, CSRF (token and Origin) on every protected non-GET, the 'signature' policy refused on any route but the webhook, no CORS header (ev:ev-mv2yqv56-01c827cf).
- Throttles against T8, SEC-1, SEC-9 and F-TR-17 (ev:ev-mv2ys7g8-01cffb10).
- Security review folded in (phase-c-security-1.md: no blocking or major; ev:ev-mv2z05jg-016641ca, ev:ev-mv2yb2r4-016452c4). I re-ran its hoarding reproduction (ev:ev-mv2z9jtb-01c883bb). I also showed the bound myself (ev:ev-mv2z9kns-01a0430f): the hold survives the TTL because nothing calls the expiry pass yet, and one pass releases it with expire rows, after which cafe1 plans A+B again. I confirmed SEC-C-4's URL acceptance (ev:ev-mv2z9kvi-01c52506).

Decision: approve. Every open item is minor or info, and each has an owner and a resolution condition.
Severities, my own judgement:
- SEC-C-1 is minor. RS-FIX-1 has one bundle per supplier, so even a legitimate canonical reservation takes two of the five. The design accepted 30-minute holds under a count cap. Once e4 runs the pass, the hold is bounded by the TTL, as I demonstrated.
- SEC-C-2 (merged with my TR-C-5) and SEC-C-3 (merged with my TR-C-1) are minor. Neither is an acceptance criterion of any phase-C task, and the general limit was never assigned in the approved plan, which my own plan review missed. Both go to the FU-15 rework before phase E.
- FU-8's environment names (TR-C-2) go to the FU-14 rework before phase D.
For SEC-B-1R (phase B), FU-1 (typed 422 planner_limit) and FU-8's route limit are now delivered and tested; only FU-14's environment names remain.

criteria.description: Sessions, CSRF, sign-in and register throttles, default-deny RBAC, admin bootstrap, no CORS (ARCH-25, SEC-1, SEC-5, SEC-9, SEC-13, SEC-20, F-TR-17)
criteria.notes: Hook order: signature policy (POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey only, else 403) -> Origin on state-changing calls -> session (401) -> role (403; unknown policy denied) -> session CSRF token. Origin precedes identification, so an anonymous call with a foreign Origin gets 403 CSRF_FAILED rather than 401; the spec fixes no order and both refuse. The two public POST routes guard Origin and the pre-login token themselves; they are the only public non-GET routes. Probe: 6th attempt with the correct password from the same IP 429 signin_pair (Retry-After 900); another IP 200; 12 cross-IP failures delay the real user about 3 s and never refuse; Admin/' admin '/ADMIN share one key; unknown and wrong-password 401s are identical; the 21st attempt from one IP 429 signin_ip; the 6th registration 429 register_ip.

criteria.description: Requests with the daily cap, value-only confirmation, planning runs with the offers_hash re-check, approval with hash and total (RS-12), RequestView deriving the rescue status on each read (RS-36), labels, FU-1, FU-7, FU-8 (route)
criteria.notes: Approve re-validates the stored plan (hash, cups and lids against the requirements of the planning run, pickups, totals, budget, deadline) before comparing hash and total; a tampered total answered 409 in every walk step that tried it. deriveInput hands derive.js the persisted snake_case rows its header documents, with latestRun scoped to the current requirements version. RS-36 (i)-(iv) held on the live endpoint in my own setups. The planner node cap is a typed 422 planner_limit (FU-1); planning is limited to 10 per customer per 10 min (FU-8 route half).

criteria.description: Reserve in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE with (user, key) idempotency, F-TR-1 fallback, live-reservation cap, conditional stock update; supplier orders and inventory with supersession; expiry pass; admin reset/faults/timeline/metrics; ledger and denied-audit rows
criteria.notes: Order inside the transaction: key lookup (user, key) -> reservation by (customer, key) when purged (another plan -> 422) -> plan guards -> live cap (not stored, so the key may be retried) -> reservation row -> conditional UPDATE per product with its reserve row -> one order and one created operation per supplier -> stored 201. A unique violation from a concurrent same key is re-resolved after rollback. OUT_OF_STOCK rolls back, then a second transaction marks the plan non_executable, queues a re-plan and stores the 409. The expiry pass is a compare-and-set on status and expires_at; a second pass is a no-op (asserted every walk step). The void rule releases the active reservation, cancels open orders and voids created operations in the caller's transaction. The cap counts reservations, not stock (SEC-C-1). That is the design's SEC-2 as written, and is bounded by the TTL once e4 runs the pass.

criteria.description: SPA shell, request page sections, supplier and admin dashboards, api.js (CSRF, 15 s abort), textContent-only DOM, contract fixtures and view-model tests
criteria.notes: dom.js refuses on* attributes, style and srcdoc, and href/src/action/formaction values other than app paths, hashes or http(s); text goes through textContent only, and the scan test asserts no innerHTML. The reserve key is stored under reserve:<planVersionId> and reused. Fixture defects (TR-C-3), the 360 px column (TR-C-6) and actions on unregistered routes (TR-C-4) are minor and routed. The URL guard lets /\host and /<TAB>/host through to another host (SEC-C-4, info: no such value is rendered today).

criteria.description: RS-14 two-process and DB_BUSY tests, HTTP contract test, browser harness with a fresh database and customer per journey, RS-33 journey at 360 and 1280 px
criteria.notes: The 6 todo results are fixture defects (live API follows the spec); I accept them as todo for this phase (TR-C-3). The 10 skips are routes that do not exist yet; 'every registered route has a scenario' fails if a route lands without one. The extract-404 tolerance is narrow (exactly that route and one console line per call) and must go once d3 lands (TR-C-4).

criteria.description: Phase C goal and its criteria RS-12, RS-14, RS-16, RS-28, RS-30, RS-33, RS-36, the auth contract, SEC-2, F-TR-17, the HTTP contract, npm test and npm run test:browser pass
criteria.notes:
RS-12, RS-14, RS-16, RS-28, RS-30, RS-33 and RS-36 are proved by named tests that pass in my runs and, for RS-14/16/30/36 and RS-12's tamper half, by my own probes. Deviations judged:
- Planning counted as rate_events kind 'general', key plan:u:<id>: acceptable, since migrations are append-only. FU-15's general limit must exclude these keys.
- Replay status 201: accepted (TR-C-7).
- Forced reset and refund_order minimal until phase E: acceptable; no operation can reach a provider state in phase C, and RS-37 is claimed in F.
- IPv6 full-address keys: SEC-C-2 (I ask for the /64 key, with the security reviewer).
- The other deviations follow the spec's intent.
Process notes: the DIRTY_OWNERSHIP refusal and the lockfile handling were correct. c3 completing with the suite red (one stale c2 case, fixed by c2's one-case rework) is acceptable because the fix is evidenced. The budget raise is a user commit (4300fb9) recorded as dec-mv2xlzls-01709639.

criteria.description: Every phase-C task's not-applicable decision on mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102 holds
criteria.notes: No phase-C task designs or changes a hook or guard. The installed guard is the repaired version (sha256 d43f4b54...). The guard refused none of my writes during this review; every draft and probe went to the nested record's draft areas as expected.

findings.title: One reservation can hold every compatible bundle (the SEC-2 cap counts reservations, not stock), and nothing runs the expiry pass in a live server until e4
findings.detail:
Security's reproduction, which I re-ran (ev:ev-mv2z9jtb-01c883bb):
- One self-registered customer asks for 500+500 with maxPickups 5 and a large budget.
- The approved plan uses A, B, D and E (C's lids are 95 mm), and its single reservation holds all of them, within the cap of 1.
- cafe1's canonical request then has no feasible plan.
- 35 minutes later the hold is still active, because src/ calls expireDueReservations nowhere (reservations.js#L271; the reconciler is e4).
My bound probe (ev:ev-mv2z9kns-01a0430f): one call of the pass expires the reservation, writes 4 expire rows, brings reserved back to 0, and cafe1 plans A+B for 8400 again.
I judge this minor:
- RS-FIX-1 has one bundle per supplier, so any reservation takes a large share of the stock.
- The design accepted 30-minute holds under a count cap.
- Once e4 runs the pass every tick, the impact is bounded by the TTL.
This finding also carries the expiry half of my earlier TR-C-8.

findings.title: Throttle keys use the full IPv6 address, so one /64 gives unlimited fresh pair and per-IP budgets (merged with TR-C-5)
findings.detail:
normalizeIp returns the whole lower-cased IPv6 address, and throttle.js keys on it.
- Security's probe: 8 failures from 8 addresses of one /64 never hit a limit, and the correct password then gives 200 (ev:ev-mv2z05jg-016641ca S3).
- Mine: 6 failures from 6 addresses of 2001:db8:1:1::/64, all 401 (ev:ev-mv2ys7g8-01cffb10).
Per-IP signin_ip and register_ip become per-address for IPv6 clients. The per-username cross-IP delay sleeps per request, so concurrency dilutes it. Seeded accounts (96-bit passwords) and the admin (16+ characters, scrypt) are not at practical risk. Self-registered customers (10-character minimum) are bounded only by scrypt CPU. The default deployment is localhost.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the orchestrator, folded into the FU-15 rework (backend-engineer, src/auth/**). Resolved when IPv6 addresses are mapped to their /64 for the sign-in and register throttle keys (IPv4 and ::ffff: unchanged), and a named test shows 5 failures spread over 5 addresses of one /64 making the 6th attempt get 429. This must land before phase E is dispatched.

findings.title: The general per-user limit (300 requests/min) is absent and was never assigned in the approved plan, and an unchanged confirm still writes a new requirements version (merged with TR-C-1)
findings.detail: Spec Security > Rate limiting and Conventions > Limits require the general limit; no plan task owns it (FU-15; my plan review missed the gap). Security measured 300 confirms in one minute writing 300 requirements versions and 300 audit rows, none limited, and 600 RequestView reads unthrottled (ev:ev-mv2z05jg-016641ca S9). confirmRequirements inserts a version even when the values equal the latest one; sameRequirements gates only supersession (requests.js#L215-L236). The expensive call (planning) has its own limit (FU-8), and the specific limits hold.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: the orchestrator (the FU-15 rework, backend-engineer; it must also own src/services/requests.js for point 2). Resolved when, before phase E is dispatched:
1. The access hook counts every signed-in call per user in rate_events (kind general, key u:<id>, check and insert in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE), answers 429 RATE_LIMITED with details.limit general and Retry-After, and never counts plan:u:<id> keys. A named test shows the 301st call in a minute refused, and NFR5 p95 stays under 300 ms.
2. A confirm whose values equal the latest version returns that version without inserting a row.
This may be merged with FU-14.

findings.title: FU-8's environment variables are not delivered; the planning limit is configurable only through createApp({planRate})
findings.detail: The limit itself works (10 per customer per 10 min, 429 details.limit plan) and is tested. RS_PLAN_RATE_LIMIT and RS_PLAN_RATE_WINDOW_MIN need src/config.js and .env.example together, and no later task owns both (FU-14).
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator (FU-14 rework, which may be merged with FU-15). Resolved when, before phase D is dispatched, both names are parsed with bounds (1-1000 and 1-1440, defaults 10 and 10) into planRateLimit/planRateWindowMin, listed in .env.example, covered by a RISK-19 test, and the env-example scan stays green.

findings.title: Six contract fixtures disagree with the live API and are reported as todo
findings.detail: Labels are missing at the top level of four plan/approve/reserve fixtures, canMarkReady is true before execution, and the timeline cursor is typed as an integer. In each case the live API follows the spec. The UI reads these values from live responses, not fixtures: the cursor is passed through as an opaque string (public/js/api.js#L187), and buttons follow the live canMarkReady. So the defects affect only test data used by c5's view-model tests. Marking them todo keeps them visible; fixing them now would need a c5 rework for test data only.
findings.recommendation: Owner: d4-frontend-extraction (fixtures), then d5-extraction-contract-browser (removes KNOWN_FIXTURE_DEFECTS), per FU-13. Resolved when phase D's npm test shows 0 todo from contracts.test.js and the six scenarios pass as normal tests. The 10 skips are resolved per FU-18 when each route lands.

findings.title: The UI calls or offers routes that do not exist yet: POST /extract (404 tolerated by the journey) and 'Delete request' (DELETE /api/requests/:id, 405)
findings.detail: The request page calls extract after creating a request and ignores the 404. RS-33's journey tolerates exactly that 404 (withoutUnregisteredExtract). The request page also shows a 'Delete request' button (public/js/components/payments.js#L43); its route is not registered, so a click answers 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED. FU-16 has no owner yet.
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator. It must assign FU-16 (a one-file test-engineer rework after d3, or g3), and the phase-D task that registers DELETE /api/requests/:id. Resolved when both routes exist, the tolerance helper is removed, and a journey asserts no 404/405 from any UI action.

findings.title: At 360 px the 'Original wording' column of 'What you need' is clipped (header reads 'Or')
findings.detail: Seen in test/browser/out/journey-infeasible-360.png from my browser run. The page has no horizontal scroll, but the column can be read only by scrolling inside the table.
findings.recommendation: Owner: d4-frontend-extraction (FU-17), verified by g1. Resolved when every column of the table is readable at 360 px without scrolling inside the table, asserted in a 360 px journey.

findings.title: Idempotent replay answers the stored 201 (the route table says 200 for a replay)
findings.detail: Conventions > Idempotency says the stored status and body are replayed, and the route table says '201 (new) or 200 (replay)'. c3 follows Conventions: it replays the stored 201 with Idempotent-Replayed: true, and answers 200 on the purged-key path. I accept this. Conventions is the normative rule; a byte-identical replay is the safer client contract; and clients detect a replay by the header.
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator. At the next spec touch, align the route table row to 'stored status (201) with Idempotent-Replayed, 200 after the key purge'. e6's contract fixtures assert that.

findings.title: Nothing drains the re-plan queue yet (by plan: e4 wires the call, f1 builds the drain)
findings.detail: After a supplier refusal the request reads "replanning" (row 4a, nextStep WAIT), and the page offers no Plan button until a drain stores a new run. A requirements change self-heals, because the UI plans right after confirm. The expiry half of this item moved to SEC-C-1.
findings.recommendation: Owner: e4-saga-reconciler (drain calls) and f1-supersession-refusal-expiry (the drain). Resolved when phase-F tests show a refused request reaching a new proposed version without a customer action.

findings.title: dom.js isAllowedUrl accepts /\host and /<TAB>/host, which browsers resolve to another host
findings.detail: Confirmed: setAttr accepts "/\evil.example/x", "/\t/evil.example/x" and "/\n/evil.example/x", which WHATWG URL resolves to evil.example; "//evil.example/x" is refused (ev:ev-mv2z9kvi-01c52506, ev:ev-mv2z05jg-016641ca S11). There is no exposure today: every href in public/** is a constant or a numeric hash route. Any absolute https URL is accepted by design anyway.
findings.recommendation: Owner: the first of d4-frontend-extraction or e5-frontend-payments to touch dom.js, and in any case before e5 renders a server-supplied URL. Resolved when values containing a backslash, whitespace or a C0 control are refused (or are resolved with new URL and required to be same-origin unless absolute http(s) is intended), with a unit test.

findings.title: Proxy trust is all-or-nothing and set by the operator
findings.detail: Behind a proxy with RS_TRUST_PROXY=0, every client shares the proxy address, so 20 failures lock everyone out for 15 minutes (signin_ip). Without a proxy and with RS_TRUST_PROXY=1, clients choose their own key. README line 84 tells proxied deployments to set the flag (ev:ev-mv2z05jg-016641ca S3).
findings.recommendation: Owner: e1-payment-adapters (config) or g2 (docs). Resolved when a startup warning is logged for https RS_PUBLIC_URL with RS_TRUST_PROXY=0 and the README states both failure modes, or the owner records why not.

findings.title: The webhook route reaches its handler with no session and no CSRF; e3 must verify the signature before any write and apply 60/min per IP
findings.detail: The signature policy works as the routing contract says (ev:ev-mv2z05jg-016641ca S5; my RBAC probe ev:ev-mv2yqv56-01c827cf shows any other signature route refused).
findings.recommendation: Owner: e3-webhooks; the phase-E reviewers re-check it. Resolved when e3's tests show the cheap pre-checks, signature verification before any write, and 60 requests per IP per minute (429, no row written).

findings.title: Phase-B carry-overs: SEC-B-2 and SEC-B-4 remain remediated; SEC-B-7 (scrypt N = 2^14) unchanged, as accepted
findings.detail: recursive_triggers is ON and the server timeouts and maxConnections are in place (code reading by security; I verified both by probe in phase B, rev-mv1k04zq-01814d87).
findings.recommendation: Owner: none. No action. SEC-B-7 stays an accepted demo setting.
