lessonDecisions.note: appliesWhen concerns a hook or guard mapping file writes to a project root in a repository with several records; this task changes application code (config, access hook, throttle keys, confirm service) and writes no guard or root-discovery logic, and the guard here resolved the nested record correctly for every write.

handoff.objective: Close the phase C review rev-mv2zb2wy-019ac65d findings TR-C-2 / FU-14 (planning-limit environment names), SEC-C-3 / FU-15 (general 300/min per-user limit, unchanged confirm writes no version) and SEC-C-2 (IPv6 /64 throttle keys) before phase D.
handoff.context: Review findings TR-C-2, SEC-C-2, SEC-C-3 in gate phase:c-core-flow; security draft .eccode/reviews/drafts/phase-c-security-1.md; followups FU-14, FU-15; c1 ho-mv2pgzqg-0145c52b (throttle design, rate_events kinds); c2 ho-mv2q84ku-01502a13 (createApp reads config.planRateLimit/planRateWindowMin). The general limit is wired through the existing access hook (createAccess in src/auth/rbac.js, built by createAuth in src/auth/index.js, which createApp already uses by default); src/app.js and src/routes/** were not touched.
handoff.expectedOutput: Config and .env.example carry RS_PLAN_RATE_LIMIT, RS_PLAN_RATE_WINDOW_MIN, RS_GENERAL_RATE_LIMIT, RS_GENERAL_RATE_WINDOW_SEC; the access hook enforces the general limit; IPv6 clients are keyed by /64; an unchanged confirm writes nothing; each finding has a named failing-first test.
acceptanceCriteria: TR-C-2: RS_PLAN_RATE_LIMIT (1-1000, default 10) and RS_PLAN_RATE_WINDOW_MIN (1-1440, default 10) are parsed into planRateLimit/planRateWindowMin, listed in .env.example, and the env-example scan is green

SEC-C-3: the 301st call of a signed-in user in a minute gets 429 RATE_LIMITED with details.limit general and Retry-After; rows are kind general, key u:<id>, in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE; plan:u:<id> keys are neither counted nor deleted; NFR5 p95 under 300 ms
SEC-C-3: a confirm with the same values and provenance as the latest version returns it and inserts no requirements, audit or re-plan row
SEC-C-2: IPv6 sign-in and register throttle keys are the /64; 5 failures over 5 addresses of one /64 make the 6th get 429; IPv4 and ::ffff: mapped addresses are unchanged

handoff.completedWork: src/config.js now parses RS_PLAN_RATE_LIMIT, RS_PLAN_RATE_WINDOW_MIN, RS_GENERAL_RATE_LIMIT (1-100000, default 300) and RS_GENERAL_RATE_WINDOW_SEC (1-3600, default 60) into planRateLimit, planRateWindowMin, generalRateLimit, generalRateWindowSec, refusing out-of-range values by variable name; all four are in .env.example with their defaults. New src/auth/general-limit.js counts every non-public, authenticated call in rate_events (kind general, key u:<id>) inside one db.tx (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) together with the delete of expired rows, refuses the call over the limit with 429 RATE_LIMITED {limit: general} and Retry-After, and does not insert a refused call; createAccess calls it right after authentication (anonymous 401 and the signature webhook route are not counted); createAuth builds it from config. src/auth/client-ip.js gained throttleKey(): IPv6 becomes its /64 (2001:db8:1:1::/64), IPv4 and ::ffff: mapped addresses (dotted or hex form) collapse to IPv4; clientIp uses it for the socket address and the trusted last X-Forwarded-For hop. confirmRequirements in src/services/requests.js returns the latest version without inserting a requirements row, audit row or re-plan when the values and the derived field provenance equal the latest version (still HTTP 201, intake_status kept at confirmed). Tests: limits.test.js (TR-C-2 x2, SEC-C-3 config), client-ip.test.js (SEC-C-2 x2), general-limit.test.js (SEC-C-3 limiter, one-transaction check, access hook), rate-limits.test.js (301st call, p95, plan key separation both ways, public routes uncounted, configurable), auth.test.js (SEC-C-2 sign-in 6th gets 429, register /64), requests-plans.test.js (SEC-C-3 unchanged confirm), env-example.test.js (four new defaults). Failing state first: ev:ev-mv2zhs1c-019dd6ab (18 failures). Three existing assertions had to follow the new behaviour: two in test/api/requests-plans.test.js counted every kind-general rate_events row (now they count only plan:% rows, since every signed-in call now adds a u:<id> row) and one asserted u:<id> was 0 (now asserts > 0 and distinct from the planning key); three in client-ip.test.js / auth.test.js expected a full IPv6 address as key (now the /64).
remainingIssues: The general limit counts every authenticated call including a 403 role refusal and a CSRF-token failure of a signed-in user; only anonymous calls (401), public routes and the signature-authenticated webhook route are outside the per-user count. The webhook route keeps its own 60 per IP per minute limit, which a later payment task owns.

Every authenticated request now writes one rate_events row (at most 300 per user per minute, expired rows deleted on the next call of that user). Rows of users who stop calling stay until their next call; the admin reset in src/services/admin.js deletes only request_create and plan:% rows, and no retention sweep of old u:<id> rows exists.

A confirm is treated as unchanged only when the derived fields JSON (values plus provenance and wording) equals the latest version, not just the columns; a confirm that changes only provenance because a newer extraction exists still writes a new version.

review.summary:
Technical review of rework-1 (sub-mv2zoxlo-019effce: 14 changed files plus the submission and followups.md), against the resolution conditions I wrote in rev-mv2zb2wy-019ac65d for TR-C-2, SEC-C-2 and SEC-C-3. Every check below ran after the submission, on the final tree (no project file changed since: 14 files differ from the claim base 4bfc13a1, exactly the listed artifacts).

Baseline:
- npm test: 821 tests, 805 pass, 10 skipped, 6 todo, 0 fail; NFR5 p95 54.8 ms over 2578 calls (ev:ev-mv2zrmza-016c0e05).
- npm run test:browser: 3/3 (ev:ev-mv2zrq4r-01ae051a).
- Artifacts equal the changes since 4bfc13a1, every sha256 matches, all inside the rework's ownership (ev:ev-mv2zv70k-01ca6173).
- The tests falsify: copied onto the pre-rework source they fail 19 times (TR-C-2 2, SEC-C-2 4, SEC-C-3 8 named failures) and pass 123/123 on the final tree (ev:ev-mv2zwsx9-012d555f).

My probes:
- General limit (ev:ev-mv2zt14w-01460430). The 301st call gets 429 general with Retry-After 60, and a refusal writes no row. Public routes and anonymous 401s are not counted. Plan and general keys are separate both ways (11 plan calls: plan rows +10, the 11th 429 plan while general passes). Only u:<id> and plan:u:<id> keys exist. With busy_timeout 0 and a held write lock, the answer is 503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After 1, never 500. The config bounds are refused by name and take effect.
- Across two processes: 120 concurrent calls of one user against limit 50 give exactly 50 passes, 70 refusals and 50 rows, in 3 rounds (ev:ev-mv2zxqy5-012a72ba).
- The phase-C probes still hold on this tree:
  - throttles, where the /64 is now one key and the 6th failure is refused (ev:ev-mv2ztesg-01b08c7d);
  - the RBAC matrix (ev:ev-mv2ztfq3-01364574);
  - the two-process reserve race (ev:ev-mv2ztoiz-01964725);
  - the 3 x 800-step random walk, where the limit broke no step (ev:ev-mv2zuvqn-014b7da3).

Error order is now Origin -> session (401) -> general limit (429) -> role (403) -> CSRF token (403). I accept the 429 between authentication and authorization: it keys on the user and bounds a signed-in client's probing. The signature-policy route returns before the limiter.

The security review (rework-1-security-1.md: no blocking or major) is folded in with its ids: SEC-R-1 minor, SEC-R-2..4 info; I agree with each severity. Decision: approve.

States: idle, creating, uploading (names the file and size, indeterminate progress element, Cancel), extracting (Cancel), error (message, what to do, request id, Retry, and a link to the request page), cancelled (Try again, open the request), then it navigates to the request page, which shows the success or degraded result. No real model call is made; every result below comes from the deterministic fake provider and is evidence of the harness and the pipeline, NOT of model quality (the live-model suite is LIVE-M1, not part of this task). src/ai imports only src/domain (AppError, localDay, buildQuestions) and node built-ins; the DB and the clock are injected into the gate. The provenance enum on the wire is the spec's user_text|image|none (manual is assigned by the confirm step, SEC-8).
handoff.expectedOutput: src/ai/{provider,schema,prompt,fake,gate,rephrase}.js and test/unit/ai/{schema,prompt,fake,gate,rephrase}.test.js, passing under the net guard.
acceptanceCriteria: EXTRACTION_WIRE_SCHEMA exactly as spec (questions are field names only, SEC-7); validateExtraction enforces the local rules (exact keys, enums, deadline patterns, budget <= 2 decimals by string arithmetic, value null iff provenance none) [schema.test.js]
prompt.js PROMPT_VERSION x1: fixed system prompt; data block between random 16-hex delimiters with safeJson escaping [prompt.test.js]

fake.js (simulated: true) parses English and Arabic (both digit scripts, dual form) with exact-substring quotes; images by sha256 through an injectable image map (default test/fixtures/extraction/fake-image-map.json; unknown image -> all fields none plus questions); faults timeout, invalid_json, schema_invalid, error [fake.test.js: RS-01, RS-02, RS-03, RS-05]

gate.js in integer micro-dollars: rate check and insert in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, per-customer concurrency 1, per-customer daily share default 0.2 with details.scope customer|global, spend + cap <= budget, reservation before the call and settlement or refund after [gate.test.js: NFR6, SEC-10]

Provider selection: always fake when RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1; default model haiku [fake.test.js, gate.test.js: NFR6]
handoff.completedWork: schema.js: EXTRACTION_WIRE_SCHEMA (deep-frozen, the Anthropic-compatible subset), validateExtraction/parseAndValidate (strict keys, enums, deadline patterns, budget cents by string arithmetic, null iff none, 200 code point wording cap, question set of field names; optional grounding: a user_text quote must be a substring of the NFC/digit-folded text and its number must occur in the quote, an image number must be among the image's legible numbers; errors carry paths and codes only), renderQuestions (server templates from domain/explain.js, budgetUsd mapped to the budget question). provider.js: ProviderError and the four codes, assertExtractionProvider, selectProvider (fake whenever config.testOffline, labelled fallback when an adapter is missing), toDegraded. prompt.js: fixed SYSTEM_PROMPT, safeJson, random 16-hex markers, buildExtractionPrompt (text block then optional image block; no parameter exists for catalog text), buildRephrasePrompt. fake.js: lexicon parser for English and Arabic, instruction sentences masked before parsing and only setting addressedToAssistant, image map by sha256, faults supplied by an injected faults() callback, optional rephrase method, self-validation through the same parse-and-validate path a real adapter uses. gate.js: toMicroUsd and share arithmetic in integers/BigInt, takeRate, reserve (concurrency, global, customer), settle, refund, settleStale, run, gateLimitsFromConfig. rephrase.js: guardRephrased (foreign numbers in both digit scripts, foreign supplier codes, number words, links, length), buildRephraseInput (code + sentence only), createRephraser through the same gate with purpose rephrase. 111 tests in the five files pass. A mutation check (budget boundary changed to >=) made 4 gate tests fail (ev:ev-mv30idlj-0141efc8), then the code was restored. Full npm test (ev:ev-mv30jdb5-01a1c105): 971 tests, 960 pass, 10 skipped, 1 FAIL that is not in src/ai: test/api/contracts.test.js 'NFR6: the route table covers each fixture file exactly once' reports test/fixtures/contracts/request-extract-degraded.json and request-image-upload.json (added by d4 in commit 5e1df73) as fixtures without a scenario; the test-engineer's d5 owns that scenario table. The suite is therefore not green and is not cited as passing.
remainingIssues: npm test is red by one test outside this task: test/api/contracts.test.js has no scenario for the d4 fixtures request-extract-degraded.json and request-image-upload.json (d5 test-engineer, or the owner of contracts.test.js, must add them).

Contract notes for d3 (src/services/extraction.js and src/main.js): (1) gate = createGate({db, clock, limits: gateLimitsFromConfig(config)}); the gate reads config fields modelDailyBudgetMicroUsd, modelCallCapMicroUsd, fakeModelCostMicroUsd (integers, preferred) and falls back to the existing modelDailyBudgetUsd, modelCallCapUsd, fakeModelCostUsd; modelCustomerDailyShare is already parsed (default 0.2). d3 may add the three micro fields to config.js with toMicroUsd(raw env string), or leave config.js unchanged; both work. (2) Call order: gate.takeRate(customerId) on every image upload; extraction = gate.run({customerId, requestId, call: () => provider.extract({text, image, signal})}) which takes the rate, reserves the cap, calls outside any transaction, settles with usage.costMicroUsd (or costUsd) and refunds on a thrown error. A refusal throws a domain AppError (429 RATE_LIMITED details.limit extract_upload|model_concurrency with headers['Retry-After'], or 503 MODEL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED details.scope global|customer) that the HTTP layer adopts via adoptAppError; d3 stores the degraded row in a separate transaction. (3) The fake takes faults: () => null|'timeout'|'invalid_json'|'schema_invalid'|'error' (a 'fake_model:' prefix is accepted); d3 must read and decrement the fake_model:* row of fault_flags and return the fault name, because adapters never touch service tables. (4) createFakeProvider({costMicroUsd}) takes integer micro-dollars: pass toMicroUsd(config.fakeModelCostUsd). (5) On ProviderError use toDegraded(err) for {schemaOk:false, degraded:true, errorCode, output: all unknown}. (6) validateExtraction(output, {text, imageNumbers}) rejects ungrounded output (provider adapters should call parseAndValidate with the request text); the spec's post-validation normalisation (downgrade to unknown, ranges, image wording stripping, non-USD budget) stays in services/extraction.js and is not implemented here. (7) renderQuestions(output.questions) gives the server-templated Question[].

Contract notes for d2: the fake image map is keyed by sha256 hex of the image bytes (not by an image id); entry shape {fields:{<name>:{value,wording}}, visibleNumbers?:number[], questions?:string[], addressedToAssistant?:boolean, imageText?:string, language?:string}; imageText is only scanned for instructions, never copied into a field. A missing default file test/fixtures/extraction/fake-image-map.json means an empty map (every image is unknown), a malformed file is an error. Providers may implement an optional rephrase({system, content, input, signal}) -> {output:{text}, usage}; the fake does. usage may carry costMicroUsd (integer, preferred by the gate) beside costUsd. User content order in prompt.js is the text block then the image block; the API adapter spec lists image first, so d2 should reorder if the API requires it. ProviderError(code, {usage}) is the only error type the gate and toDegraded understand beyond a generic Error.

The fake parser is a lexicon, not a language model: it handles the documented English and Arabic forms (digits in both scripts, thousands commas, ml/mm, 'by'/'قبل الساعة' with minutes or am/pm, $ / dollars / دولار, pickups / نقطتي) and leaves anything else unknown with a question; a bare hour ('by 11'), Arabic number words other than the dual, and decimals in integer fields are deliberately unknown. EXT-1 corpus texts written in d2 may need lexicon additions in fake.js, which is owned by this task.

The rephrase guard compares against the template sentences, so it cannot catch a reordered comparison or a negation (accepted residual, spec); a capital 'A' or 'I' used as an English article counts as a supplier code and causes a discard (fails safe).

Lesson mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102 (guard root resolution) did not apply: this task builds no hook or guard. The guard itself refused one Bash call (an evidence label containing a greater-than-or-equal sign was read as a redirect to the relative path '='); the label was reworded and the command rerun.
No ECCODE_EVAL line is printed by this task; the fake-mode EXT-1 eval belongs to d2 (test/eval/extraction-fake.test.js).

NOTES FOR THE REVIEWER: (1) request ids come from INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, so after a hard delete of the highest id the next request reuses it, and audit rows of the deleted request share the id with the new one (found by my own test; a new migration with AUTOINCREMENT would fix it, migrations are not d3's). (2) A refusal by the budget or the rate limit stores a degraded row, as the spec says, and it is then the newest extraction: the page shows 'Automatic reading unavailable' even if an earlier extraction of the same request succeeded, and a later confirm treats every value as manual. (3) Uploads count toward the 10 per 10 minutes even when later refused by size or magic bytes (the count happens after the owner and header checks, before the body is read). Technical review of rework-2 (sub-mv31tlv1-01663c96: test/api/requests-plans.test.js plus the submission). Both artifact sha256 values match the submission (file 72be8760...). The rework's ownership is that one file, and it is the only file the rework changed: +3/-1 since the claim base c83d80b2, landed in commit ae7c763, with no uncommitted change (ev:ev-mv32a4fr-01fc4e1f).

The change, in the case 'RS-34: GET /api/requests/:id carries labels and the planned shape of the contract fixture' (L778-L780):
- 'capabilities' is added to the exact, sorted top-level key list. It is still compared with deepEqual, so any other new key still fails.
- Two new assertions: Object.keys(v.capabilities) deep-equals ['deleteRequest'], and typeof deleteRequest is 'boolean'.

This matches the producer, src/services/view.js L494-L496 (capabilities: { deleteRequest: true }). data.title: FU-23: request ids are never reused
data.decision: Option 1: an app-only migration rebuilds rescue_requests with AUTOINCREMENT, with a test named RS-39 showing that an id is never reused after a hard delete. Done as a one-task rework (owner backend-engineer, files src/db/migrations/** and the test) opened after rework-3 is approved and before phase E's e4; the phase D reviewers may raise its severity.
data.rationale: Audit rows of a hard-deleted request would share an id with a later request that may belong to another customer. The fix is a migration and one test; accepting the reuse would leave the admin timeline ambiguous.

data.title: FU-24: a budget or rate refusal becomes the newest extraction
data.decision: Accepted for version one as d3 built it: the refusal stores a degraded row, the page shows the degraded notice and the manual form, and a later confirm treats every value as manual.
data.rationale: It follows the spec's wording, the customer can always finish by hand, the notice is hidden once requirements exist (d4's reset), and the alternative (keeping an earlier successful extraction current) would mix provenance across extractions. Reversible by a rework of src/services/extraction.js.

data.title: FU-25: explanation rephrasing is not wired in version one
data.decision: Rephrasing (src/ai/rephrase.js) stays an unwired, unit-tested capability. e1 (owner of src/config.js in phase E) removes the RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE parsing and g2 removes it from .env.example and documents that explanations are deterministic and rephrasing is not wired. The verification report counts RS-05's rephrasing clause as unit-level only.
data.rationale: A configuration variable with no effect is a placeholder presented as a feature. The deterministic explanations meet the user-facing need; wiring a model call to every plan view would add spend and latency without LIVE-M1 evidence.

- Nothing else in the journey changed: the steps, selectors, database checks and screenshot are byte-identical to the base.
- No .js file outside node_modules mentions withoutUnregisteredExtract or EXTRACT_ROUTE_MAY_BE_MISSING (ev:ev-mv3351jw-0188869e).

Why the unfiltered assertion catches a 404 on the extract route. I read the harness: newJourney pushes 'HTTP <status>: <method> <url>' for every response with status >= 400 (harness.js L66-L67), plus every console error. The journey's text-only path calls POST /api/requests/:id/extract (request-new.js L205-L211). It reaches waitForURL only when that call succeeds, or when it fails with a degraded 429 or 503 (L218-L220). In that degraded case the >= 400 response would itself be in problems and fail L97. A passing journey therefore proves the extract call answered below 400.

The frontend no longer tolerates a 404 either. classifyExtractFailure (request-new.js L45-L50) returns 'retry' for a 404, so the page stays on the error state with Retry. The unit rows for FU-16 pass (extraction.test.js L431 and L672-L682, 36/36, ev:ev-mv33481c-0186bea7). The engineer's first scratch run, ev:ev-mv32eef8-01a1865d, shows the same behaviour in the browser: a 404 on the page's own call stops the journey at waitForURL.

My checks ran after the submission, all on one tree (644325026d5e...):
- npm run test:browser: 8/8 pass, 3 suites (ev:ev-mv3336jn-01854cbc);
- the journey file alone: 3/3 (ev:ev-mv333e72-01e37f9b);
- the frontend extraction unit file: 36/36 (ev:ev-mv33481c-0186bea7);
- npm test: exit 0, 1216 tests, 1208 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped (ev:ev-mv336kwi-018b30c5);
- scope and diff: ev:ev-mv3351jw-0188869e.

I tried to reproduce the injected-404 case myself with a scratch probe in the session scratchpad. The tool-call guard refused the write ('technical-reviewer reviews/designs but does not edit project files; ...'). I did not work around it. I rely on the engineer's two logs together with my reading of the harness and of the assertion. See TR-RW3-1 for why that is enough.

Decision: approve. There are three info findings and none blocks.

criteria.description: FU-16: remove the extract-route 404 tolerance from the phase C browser journey
criteria.notes:
I checked each of the handoff's acceptance criteria.
(1) Any 404 on POST /api/requests/:id/extract during a journey is a failure. The helper and all filtering are gone, and L97 compares the raw problems list with []. The harness records every response >= 400 (harness.js L66-L67), so a 404 on that route, or on any route, fails the row. The page now also stops at waitForURL on such a 404, which gives a second failure point (ev:ev-mv32eef8-01a1865d).
(2) A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it. With the same injected 404, the strict assertion fails and lists exactly the extract 404 and its console line (ev:ev-mv32evim-01a6a1d8, an intended failure, cited in TR-RW3-1 because the engine does not accept a failed check as support for a met criterion). The old helper passes and prints the two entries it hid (ev:ev-mv32exvz-01f53643). That is a valid before/after contrast on the assertion that changed. Because the scratch file was deleted, its source cannot be inspected. I accept the logs for the reason given in TR-RW3-1.
(3) The existing checks still pass. Browser suite 8/8, journey 3/3, npm test 1208 pass / 0 fail / 8 skipped of 1216, all on the final tree.
Scope: the diff since e011e54 changes the owned file only by +1/-18. The journey's steps and its other assertions are unchanged (ev:ev-mv3351jw-0188869e).

criteria.description: c6's test/browser/journey-infeasible.test.js tolerates a 404 on POST /api/requests/:id/extract through withoutUnregisteredExtract() because the route did not exist in phase C. d3 added the route and d4's reset removed the frontend tolerance (ho-mv32b3pf-011eac5d). Phase C is approved and no phase D task owns the file, so a rework removes the helper: any 404 on that route during a journey is a failure.
criteria.notes:
The rework's purpose is met. The test side and the app side now agree that the extract route exists and that a 404 on it is a failure:
- Test side: the journey's assertion has no filter (L97).
- App side: d4's reset removed EXTRACT_ROUTE_MAY_BE_MISSING. classifyExtractFailure sends a 404 to 'retry', so there is no navigation and the page shows the error with Retry (request-new.js L45-L50). The FU-16 unit rows pin this behaviour, and they pass in my run (ev:ev-mv33481c-0186bea7).
The full browser suite passes 8/8 on the final tree (ev:ev-mv3336jn-01854cbc). The triggering run ev:ev-mv3226jz-0198f037 passed only with the tolerance in place. The same journey now passes without it.
The two degraded-extraction journeys (phase D) already assert an unfiltered deepEqual(problems, []) (degraded-extraction.test.js L181 and L241). No browser journey keeps a filter now.

criteria.description: The rework's not-applicable decision on mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102 holds
criteria.notes:
I read the lesson with memory search --check-env. It applies to a hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record or root in a repository with several records. The --check-env result 'APPLIES' checks only the environment (node >= 18.17), not the scope.
This rework deletes a test helper and changes one assertion in a browser test file. It designs or changes no hook, guard or root discovery (ev:ev-mv3351jw-0188869e), so not-applicable holds.
The engineer's two guard denials were for scratch writes outside its claimed file. Those are the role and claim rules working, which the lesson's 'Not applicable when' list covers. My own scratch probe was refused with the role message for a target outside the record's draft areas (the session scratchpad), not inside the nested record's draft area. That is also outside the lesson's wrong-root case. My draft write into this record's .eccode/reviews/drafts/ was allowed.
The decision matches rework-1 and rework-2, which I accepted.

findings.title: The failing-first proof is a deleted scratch test; the evidence logs suffice and no permanent regression test is required
findings.detail:
The record's output says 'a regression test that fails without it', and its criterion says 'a regression test fails before the fix and passes after it'. Here the fix is the removal of a filter inside a test, so the regression test is the journey itself. Its unfiltered L97, together with the harness collector at harness.js L66-L67, fails on any >= 400 response.
The engineer showed the contrast on the changed assertion with an injected 404: the strict assertion fails (ev:ev-mv32evim-01a6a1d8) and the old helper passes (ev:ev-mv32exvz-01f53643). The logs record the command, the exit code and the exact problem entries. The scratch source was deleted, so only its output can be inspected.
I considered requiring a permanent test, for example a test/browser/extract-404-guard.test.js owned by test-engineer that injects a 404 through page.route and asserts that the journey's problem collection carries it. I do not require it, for three reasons:
(a) It would test the harness, not the journey. A filter re-added to journey-infeasible.test.js would not make it fail, so it does not protect against the regression in question.
(b) It would add little. The collector is a few page.on handlers that all three browser journeys share, and the FU-16 unit rows already pin the app-side 404 handling (extraction.test.js L431, L672-L682).
(c) The engineer's ownership was the journey file only, and the submission discloses this.
My own attempt at an independent browser probe was refused by the guard (scratch file write), so I could not re-run the contrast. My conclusion rests on reading the harness and the assertion.
findings.recommendation: No action required for this gate, and no follow-up. If the orchestrator wants scratch-test proofs to be inspectable in future reworks, the engineer could record the scratch source with 'evidence file' before deleting it. That would be a workflow note, not a condition of this gate.

criteria.description: Extraction core: provider contract, wire schema and strict validator, prompt with random delimiters, deterministic bilingual fake, budget/rate/concurrency gate, opt-in rephrase
criteria.notes:
The wire schema is byte-for-byte the spec's (deep-frozen), and validateExtraction enforces exact keys, enums, deadline patterns, budget decimals by string arithmetic and null <=> none.
- Its optional text context also checks that a number occurs in the quote. That is the check d3 does not use: TR-D-1.
- The gate works in integer micro-dollars:
  - the rate count and insert run in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE;
  - concurrency, global budget and customer share are checked in one transaction before the call;
  - spend + cap = budget passes;
  - unreadable usage is charged at the cap.
- My budget-boundary mutant (>=) is killed by d3's API tests too, not only by d1's unit tests.
- selectProvider returns the fake whenever RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1.
- Rephrase is built and unit-tested but not wired (FU-25, dec-mv330t7a-017a2211). I agree: an inert switch is not a feature, and the decision has e1 and g2 remove or document it.

The rest holds, by code reading, the plan command, my mutants and security's U and X probes:
- Upload order: owner check, declared type, Content-Length, rate, streamed cap and deadline, magic bytes, then write to .tmp and rename with mode 0600. The magic-bytes mutant is killed.
- Extract: the gate runs first and the provider is called outside any transaction. The watchdog charges a timeout at the cap.
- Refusals store a degraded row and never call the provider. The mutant that calls the provider is killed.
- Every provider failure becomes a 200 degraded response. A provider-level PROVIDER_BUSY also does, per my probe P1; it has no test of its own (TR-D-2).

findings.title: Grounding admits model-invented numbers when the quote has no digits (merged with security SEC-D-1, which security rates minor)
findings.detail:
Where:
- extractRequest calls validateExtraction(answer.output) without context.text, "structure only" (src/services/extraction.js L510). d1's number check (schema.js NUMBER_NOT_IN_INPUT, numberGrounded) therefore never runs on a real answer.
- d3's per-field rule (L374-L381) accepts a numeric user_text value when the quote merely is a substring: `ok = written.size === 0 || written.has(value)`. A quote without digits grounds any number.

Reproduced (ev:ev-mv337a71-01b57e0c, P2) on the RS-FIX-1 text:
- cupQuantity 777 with originalWording "cups" is stored {value: 777, status: known, provenance: user_text};
- maxPickups 5 with originalWording "two pickups" is stored the same way;
- schema.js validateExtraction with the text refuses both with NUMBER_NOT_IN_INPUT.
Security reproduced the same with 99999, 777 and 5 (ev:ev-mv33e5qp-017ba56b, E1).

Impact:
- The UI shows a model-invented quantity as "From your text" with the buyer's own words beside it.
- confirm keeps provenance user_text when the buyer accepts it unchanged (SEC-8 works as designed).
- The planner and the payment amounts then use that number.
- d3's own test names this rule ("the quote does not contain the number"), but only with a digit-bearing quote.
- The fake can never trigger it, which is why the suite is green.
- It matters as soon as a real adapter runs. `npm start` selects the CLI whenever `claude` is on PATH, and it is on PATH here (2.1.296).

Why major and not minor: grounding is the only server-side defence between a hallucinated number and its provenance label (the spec's T9 mitigation), the phase claims 'grounding and provenance', and the stricter check already exists unused. The confirmation boundary and plan approval still hold, so no money moves without the buyer, and I do not rate it blocking.

Security rates it minor but also requires it to land before the verification gate.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer (src/services/extraction.js and test/api/extract.test.js; a d3 reset or a one-task rework), with ai-engineer if schema.js must export numberGrounded.

Resolved when all of the following hold:
(1) normaliseExtraction downgrades a numeric user_text field unless its value occurs in the quote, as digits of either script or as a number word or dual form. Reuse schema.js's numberGrounded and word list (export it) rather than a second copy.
(2) A named SEC-7 API test shows each of these stored unknown, with a question: "cups"->777, "two pickups"->5, security's E1 cases ("need cups"->99999, "lids for the weekend"->777), and a quote with an unrelated digit ("200 cups"->300, already tested).
(3) The same test shows these stay known: "two pickups"->2, "نقطتي استلام"->2, "٢٥٠ مل"->250.
(4) A mutation of the new condition is shown red.
(5) npm test and the d3 plan command pass.
(6) I re-run my probe P2 and it shows both values unknown.

findings.title: FU-23: ids are reused after a hard delete, wider than recorded (requests, plan versions, images); I agree with dec-mv330std-0165d9be if its scope grows
findings.detail:
rescue_requests uses INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, so a hard delete of the highest id lets the next request take it.

Security's reproduction (ev:ev-mv33e5qp-017ba56b, section F):
- Y's request and plan version get X's deleted ids.
- Y sees nothing of X, and X gets 404.
- The admin timeline of Y's request lists X's extraction.run, requirements.confirm, plan.create, plan.approve, void_rule.apply, plan.non_executable and request.delete events.

The scope is wider than the decision:
- plan_versions ids are reused through the same cascade, and images ids follow from it;
- both appear in audit_events.entity_id, and plan-version ids feed the timeline scope.
AUTOINCREMENT on rescue_requests alone would leave X's plan.approve rows attributed to Y's plan.

I add one point: model_spend.request_id has no foreign key, so X's model-spend rows also re-attach to Y's id.

The reach is limited: the highest ids only, hard deletes only (no supplier order ever), and no customer-facing disclosure. The audit rows hold ids and codes only. I do not raise its severity.

findings.title: The eleven documented design deltas: all acceptable additions or justified deviations, three with caveats to carry
findings.detail:
Each delta (followups.md, 'Documented design deltas') judged against the approved spec.

Acceptable additions:
- (1) Extraction.addressedToAssistant. The spec requires the notice but omitted the field from Extraction. It is stored under the __meta key, hidden on read, and confirm ignores it.
- (2) RequestView.capabilities.deleteRequest. Additive, but always true, so the UI offers Delete in states where DELETE answers 409 PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS. The UI handles the 409. Either make it status-dependent or document it as a route-availability flag.
- (3) 400 BAD_REQUEST for a missing Content-Length and for UPLOAD_TIMEOUT. The catalog has no better code. Caveat: with the default server requestTimeout of 30 s, the route's 60 s UPLOAD_TIMEOUT branch cannot fire in production; only tests reach it, with an injected deadline (see TR-D-7).
- (4) The refusal rows' errorCode, BUSY or UNAVAILABLE. Both values are inside the spec's enum.
- (5) A degraded row replaces the newest degraded row. The table stays bounded. The audit row per extraction.run and model_spend keep the history.
- (6) Content-Disposition: inline. Harmless next to CSP sandbox and nosniff; security's polyglot run in Chromium confirms it (ev:ev-mv33nzz8-010dae0c).
- (7) The sweep also purges rate_events and settles stale reservations. An interim owner, with FU-22 requiring one owner.

Justified deviations:
- (8) Client limits of 65 s and 45 s. The spec's blanket 15 s contradicts its own 30 s model timeout, so the deviation is necessary.
- (10) RS_LIVE_MODEL_CEILING_USD. Safer than the spec; FU-21 covers the docs. Its parsing is TR-D-10.
- (11) Internal micro-dollar fields. No external contract.

Deviation from d2's criterion:
- (9) labels/*.txt with a 5x7 bitmap renderer instead of labels/*.html with Chromium. The labels are legible (I viewed i06), but they are English capitals only. No image carries Arabic text, so LIVE-M1 will say nothing about reading Arabic packaging.

None of the eleven is a spec violation that needs code rework.

findings.title: FU-2 and the timeout chain: I agree with dec-mv31kbrz-012381a1, with two notes for the verification report (merged with security SEC-D-8, info)
findings.detail:
Upload:
- Node's requestTimeout of 30 s cuts a slow body before the route's 60 s deadline. Security measured 408 at 30.95 s for a 1 KiB/s upload (ev:ev-mv33mul3-01ddae55, T2).
- That 408 is the server's bare clientError reply from src/http/server.js, with no JSON envelope and no requestId (NFR6 says every response carries one).
- The client waits 65 s, then shows the error with Retry.

Extract:
- RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS (default 30 s) bounds the watchdog, the CLI timer and the Anthropic deadline. Node's requestTimeout does not bound the handler: security's T1 got a 200 after 35 s with the variable at 40 s.
- The client allows 45 s, so the default chain is consistent.
- config accepts RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS up to 600000. Above about 44 s the client aborts first, while the server still holds the connection and the customer's model slot, stores the row and charges the call.

1.4 Mbit/s for 5 MB is acceptable for version one.
findings.recommendation:
Owners: delivery-lead and g2, or e1 (owner of src/config.js in phase E) for the clamp.
- The verification report lists the 408 without envelope or requestId as an NFR6 exception.
- RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS is clamped to at most 40000, below the client's 45 s (security suggests 60000; 40000 also keeps the client consistent), or g2 documents the bound.
No phase D code change.

findings.title: Security info items SEC-D-3..SEC-D-9 folded in; FU-24 and FU-25 decisions agreed
findings.detail:
Folded from the FINAL security draft, all info:
- SEC-D-3: the server is not the injection backstop for a real model; the flag, the buyer and the approval are.
  - An obeying model that quotes the injected sentence itself passes grounding (budget $99,999 from ti01-en).
  - Any in-range image-provenance number is accepted; there is no OCR.
  - Suggestion: when addressedToAssistant is true, ask the buyer to re-check every known field (product decision).
- SEC-D-4: five self-registered accounts from one IP spend the default USD 1.00 daily budget (SEC-10 residual, measured). Suggestion: the README recommends RS_ALLOW_SIGNUP=0 or a smaller share for public deployments.
- SEC-D-5: anthropic.js buffers a chunked body whole before the 1 MiB check (48 MiB read, RSS +157 MiB). Only the pinned host can send it.
- SEC-D-6: extract has no per-request idempotency; a double-click is one extra billed call, bounded by the rate limit and concurrency 1.
- SEC-D-7: photos, including EXIF location, are stored and forwarded to the provider byte-for-byte. The README privacy statement (T23) should say so, or metadata is stripped.
- SEC-D-8: merged into TR-D-7.
- SEC-D-9: d5's secrets scan covers the log channel well. Responses, database rows and an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the separate-process run are gaps, planned for g3 (RS-29).

On the open decisions:
- FU-24 (dec-mv330t0g-0175d52b): I agree. It follows the spec text, avoids mixing provenance across extractions, and the customer can finish by hand.
- FU-25 (dec-mv330t7a-017a2211): I agree. An inert RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE must be removed or documented, and RS-05's rephrasing clause counts as unit-level only.
findings.recommendation: FU-24: none. FU-25: per the decision, e1 and g2. SEC-D-3..SEC-D-7 and SEC-D-9 go into the verification report's risk list (owner delivery-lead). The README items (SEC-D-4, SEC-D-7) go to g2; SEC-D-5 (streamed byte cap) goes to the ai-engineer when anthropic.js is next touched.

findings.title: A detached CLI child outlives its parent: a server restart or a killed live run leaves a billed model call unsupervised (security SEC-D-2, minor)
findings.detail:
Where:
- src/ai/cli.js spawns the child with detached: true, in its own process group. Only the adapter's timer, the abort signal or the stdout cap kill it, and all three die with the parent.
- main.js stop() calls process.exit(0) without stopping in-flight provider calls.
- test/live/run-live-model.js has no SIGINT or SIGTERM handling.

Reproduced by security against a stub (ev:ev-mv33mul3-01ddae55, C7): after the parent's SIGTERM, and again after SIGKILL, the child keeps running. I read the same code: runOnce keeps no registry of children and the provider has no close().

Impact:
- Each orphaned call still bills, up to --max-budget-usd (USD 0.05): at most 2 per server process, plus one per killed live run.
- A hanging CLI leaks a process.
- Accounting survives: the reservation stays 'reserved' and the sweep settles it at the cap.

findings.title: The live runner silently rounds the ceiling it was given (5.0000001 becomes 5.000000 and is accepted); it started a real run during the security review (RISK-21)
findings.detail:
evaluateLaunch parses RS_LIVE_MODEL_CEILING_USD with toMicroUsd, which rounds half-up at the sixth decimal, and only then checks the result against the 5.00 maximum. So the value 5.0000001 is accepted as exactly USD 5.00.

The money cap itself holds. The enforced ceiling is never above 5.00, and security confirms that every value over 5.00 is refused (ev:ev-mv33mul3-01ddae55, section L).

The defect is silent coercion of a spend limit typed by a person. A ceiling that means 'just over five' should be refused, not reinterpreted.

The incident:
- During the security review this value, together with RS_LIVE_MODEL=1 and a logged-in `claude` on PATH, started a real run for up to 30 s (RISK-21).
- The runner then had no SIGTERM handling, so a killed run could leave its CLI child alive (TR-D-9).
- Whether a call was billed is unknown; the worst case is bounded by --max-budget-usd 0.05 per call.

The primary cause was the probe enabling the live switch on a machine with a logged-in CLI, which is not the runner's fault. Two runner properties widened it:
- a single env switch suffices to start a billed run;
- the run does not print and confirm its provider and worst case first. `--dry-run` exists but is optional.

Existing guarantees unchanged: pinned argv, --tools "", --safe-mode, allow-listed env, 8 MiB cap, concurrency 2, process-group SIGKILL on timeout, one attempt

handoff.completedWork: TR-D-9: src/ai/cli.js tracks every started child (per-adapter registry plus a module-level set). The adapter now exposes close() and liveChildren(). close() marks the adapter closed, sends SIGTERM to each child's process group, SIGKILLs after killGraceMs (new option, default 1000 ms, CLI_KILL_GRACE_MS), sweeps the group once the leader exits, rejects the in-flight calls with PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, removes their temp cwd and resolves when all runs have settled; it is idempotent and later calls reject PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE without spawning (a close() that lands while the temp cwd is being made also stops the spawn). A single process 'exit' hook SIGKILLs the groups still registered, which covers process.exit() in main.js stop(). The timeout, abort and cap paths still SIGKILL the group immediately, as before. TR-D-10: test/live/run-live-model.js parses the ceiling with parseCeilingMicroUsd: the regex ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,11})(?:\.([0-9]{1,2}))?$ on the raw string (no trim, no sign, no exponent, no leading zero), compared in integer cents, 1..500, before any conversion; toMicroUsd is no longer used for the ceiling. The runner prints a 'cli: claude <version>' line after the plan lines and before the first call, installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers once the provider exists (close the adapter, say 'interrupted', no report, exit 130/143 through an injectable exit), and closes the adapter in a finally on every return path. Test fixtures: stub-claude.mjs gains child.pid in hang mode and a stubborn mode (ignores SIGTERM); cli-orphan-driver.mjs is the process.exit() driver. FINDING -> CHANGE -> TEST -> EVIDENCE. TR-D-9 / SEC-D-2 -> src/ai/cli.js registry, close(), exit hook; runner closes the adapter on SIGINT/SIGTERM and on every return path -> cli.test.js 'close() and the exit hook leave no CLI child behind' (6 tests: group kill, SIGTERM-ignoring child, closed adapter, other adapter untouched, process.exit() driver, registry empty after calls) and live-runner-refusal.test.js 'SIGINT and SIGTERM close the adapter' (in-process) plus 'the runner process kills its CLI child on SIGINT and SIGTERM' (real runner process, stub claude, exit 143 / 130, pids dead, no report); all red before the change (6 red in cli.test.js: close is not a function and three stub children were left running; 3 red in the refusal file) -> ev:ev-mv34amer-0143b344 (plan command, 107/107, ECCODE_EVAL 200/200 fake) and ev:ev-mv34bp0u-01821bb8 (npm test). TR-D-10 -> parseCeilingMicroUsd, badCeiling message, CLI version line before the first call -> live-runner-refusal.test.js 'NFR3: the ceiling is a decimal with at most two fraction digits, from 0.01 to 5.00, checked BEFORE any rounding (TR-D-10)': 38 refused values in evaluateLaunch, 6 through the real process (exit 2, empty stdout, fixed message), 5, 5.00 and 0.50 accepted through --dry-run; red before the change -> same two evidence ids.
remainingIssues: Decision: '05' and '005.00' are refused (a leading zero is non-canonical for a spend limit); '5.0' and '0.5' are accepted (one fraction digit is within 'at most two'). close() is idempotent and terminal. The timeout, abort and 8 MiB cap paths keep the immediate process-group SIGKILL (existing guarantee); SIGTERM then SIGKILL applies to close().

A parent killed by SIGKILL (or by SIGTERM with no handler) cannot run any hook, so its CLI child is still orphaned in that case; the child is bounded by --max-budget-usd and the reservation sweep settles it. The server and the live runner both handle SIGTERM/SIGINT and close the adapter, so only an uncatchable kill leaves a child. The exit hook runs on process.exit() and on a normal end.

FU-21 for g2 (not my files): RS_LIVE_MODEL_CEILING_USD is the exact variable name in test/live/run-live-model.js. It is missing from .env.example and README.md. Suggested text: 'RS_LIVE_MODEL_CEILING_USD: the most you are willing to spend on one live model run (npm run test:live-model); required together with RS_LIVE_MODEL=1; an exact decimal from 0.01 to 5.00 with at most two decimals (for example 0.50 or 5); anything else, including 5.0000001, 1e0 or 05, is refused with exit 2.'
Not in my ownership: the README or docs line that says the live runner prints the worst case first can now also mention the CLI version line.
LIVE-M1 (the real run) is still not performed and is not claimed; all results here come from the stub claude and the fake provider and are not evidence of model quality.

data.title: Live-runner ceiling refuses a leading zero
data.decision: The ceiling must be written as 0, or a non-zero whole part without a leading zero, with at most two decimals (0.01 to 5.00). 05 and 005.00 are refused.
data.rationale: One exact form per value keeps the check unambiguous; the refusal message states the rule. ai-engineer asked (d2 reset handoff ho-mv34d3dh-01f6abfa). Reversible by widening the pattern.

findings.title: With a photo attached, provenance image is accepted for every field, so a model bypasses the TR-D-1 grounding for budget, pickups, quantities and deadline (security SEC-D-12, which security rates minor)
findings.detail:
Where: normaliseExtraction accepts `f.provenance === 'image'` whenever `hasImage === true` (src/services/extraction.js L389-L391) and applies only the range checks. The spec's rule 'use provenance image only for values legibly printed on the image', and 'never infer a budget, deadline or pickup limit that is not stated', exist only in the prompt.

Reproduced (ev:ev-mv35carz-014fc788):
- P5a, normaliseExtraction with a photo: budget 99999 USD (9999900 cents), maxPickups 5, cupQuantity 99999, deadline 06:00 and capacity 1999 are all stored known, provenance image. Without a photo, all of them are unknown.
- P5b, through the route after a real upload of EXT-1's injection image i06: cupQuantity 99999, capacity 1999, deadline 2026-10-20T06:00, budget 9999900 cents and maxPickups 5 are all stored known, provenance image.
Security reproduced the same (ev:ev-mv353ywi-01d41ace, G7 and G9).

Why major (I raise security's minor, as I did for SEC-D-1):
- It defeats the resolution of TR-D-1, a major I required, with a one-word change in the model's answer.
- It works on exactly the channel T9 names as the injection vector: packaging text in the photo. EXT-1 itself carries injection images.
- It covers fields no package can carry: the budget (it changes which plans are feasible), the pickup limit, the quantities and the deadline.
- The phase claims 'grounding and provenance'. Server-side grounding is the spec's T9 mitigation, and the RS-02 photo journey is a primary flow.

The confirmation boundary still holds: the badge reads 'From the photo', the buyer confirms every field and approves the plan, and amounts never come from model output. That is why I do not rate it blocking. The same was true of TR-D-1.

(2) A named SEC-7 test shows, through the route after an upload, that the P5b claims (budget 99999, maxPickups 5, cupQuantity 99999, deadline 06:00) are stored unknown with their questions.
(3) RS-02 (capacity 250 and diameter 90 from the clear image, provenance image) stays green, and the EXT-1 fake eval stays 200/200.
(4) A mutation of the new field allow-list is shown red.

findings.title: A quote that is the tail of a longer number grounds the smaller value: 200 from '1,200 cups', 50 ml from '250 ml' (security SEC-D-11)
findings.detail:
The quote rule is a plain substring test after normalisation (extraction.js L385; schema.js validateExtraction does the same), and numbersIn reads only the quote. Nothing checks that the quote's digit runs are whole numbers of the text.

Reproduced (ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7, P3b) with the text 'I need 1,200 cups and 1200 lids, 250 ml, 90 mm.'. These are stored known, provenance user_text, with the shown wording looking like the buyer's own:
- cupQuantity 200 quoted '200 cups';
- lidQuantity 200 quoted '200 lids';
- capacityMl 50 quoted '50 ml'.
Security adds 250 from '2500', budget 120 and 12 from '$1200', and 1 from '11:30' (ev:ev-mv353ywi-01d41ace, G2 and G9).

Impact: a tenfold understatement of a quantity or a budget, or a wrong cup size, shown as 'From your text'. Dropping the thousands is exactly what the EXT-1 t03-thousands case tests for in a real model. It is narrower than TR-D-1, because the value must be the literal tail of a written number, and the buyer still confirms. It is a gap in d1's rule, not a regression of the TR-D-1 fix.

findings.title: A user_text deadline is never grounded: 06:00 quoted 'for the weekend' is stored known, 'From your text' (security SEC-D-10)
findings.detail:
validateExtraction applies NUMBER_NOT_IN_INPUT only to kinds int and num, and the deadline is a string. normaliseExtraction calls numberGroundedInQuote only for numbers (L387). A user_text deadline therefore needs only a quote that is a substring of the text.

Reproduced (ev:ev-mv35carz-014fc788, P5c) with the text 'We need cups for the weekend, by 11:30 please.'. These are stored known, provenance user_text:
- '06:00' quoted 'for the weekend';
- '23:59' quoted 'by 11:30';
- '2026-10-21T06:00' quoted 'for the weekend'.
The genuine '11:30' quoted 'by 11:30' is correctly known. Security reproduced the same through the route (G9).

This is TR-D-1's class for a string field, and I missed it in iteration 1. The deadline constrains the planner and can make a plan infeasible or wrong. The buyer confirms it.

Resolved when a named SEC-7 test shows that a non-numeric user_text field whose quote is not in the text (for example material 'plastic' quoted 'plastic cups', and a deadline quoted 'by noon' that the text does not contain) is stored unknown with its question, and when my M2 mutant is red.

findings.title: A call ended by close() is settled at 0, while a timeout is charged at the cap: the TR-D-9 fix turned a conservative ledger into an under-count (security SEC-D-16, which security rates info)
findings.detail:
Before the fix, an orphaned call's reservation stayed 'reserved', and the sweep settled it at the cap. Now terminate() rejects with ProviderError('PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE') and no usage (cli.js L175-L188). gate.run then refunds it at microUsdOfUsage(undefined) = 0, although the killed CLI call may already have been billed up to --max-budget-usd. callProvider's own reasoning ('a call that timed out may still have been billed', extraction.js) applies equally here.

Reproduced (ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7):
- P3c in-process: the reservation is 50000 while the call runs, then {actual 0, settled} after close().
- P4, a real server on SIGTERM: the same row is {reserved 50000, actual 0, settled}. After SIGKILL, by contrast, the row stays reserved at the cap.
Security: S1-S3 in ev:ev-mv3549s6-014f5d35.

Bound: at most 2 x USD 0.05 per server shutdown with calls in flight. It is rare and cannot be triggered by a customer. It still matters to the phase's claim of budget controls in integer micro-dollars, so I rate it minor rather than info.
findings.recommendation: Owner: ai-engineer (src/ai/cli.js, test/unit/ai/cli.test.js). The fix is one line: terminate() rejects with `{ usage: { costMicroUsd: callCapMicroUsd } }`, like the watchdog, and a test asserts the cap on the close() path. If d2 is not reset in this iteration, the orchestrator records a decision that adds this to FU-28 (or a new follow-up with an owner), and the verification report lists it as a ledger under-count residual. It does not block approval on its own.

findings.title: FU-28 is wider than recorded: SIGHUP, and a second SIGTERM during the grace period, still orphan the child (security SEC-D-15)
findings.detail:
main.js registers `process.once('SIGINT', stop)` and `process.once('SIGTERM', stop)` (L183-L184), and the runner's INTERRUPT_SIGNALS holds SIGINT and SIGTERM only. So:
- SIGHUP (a closed terminal) kills the server or runner with no hook;
- a second SIGTERM during close()'s grace period hits the default disposition, because `once` has already been consumed.
Security reproduced both (S4, S5, D3 in ev:ev-mv3549s6-014f5d35). I confirmed the SIGKILL residual itself on a real server (P4: child and grandchild alive, row reserved at the cap; ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7). The bound is unchanged.
findings.recommendation: If d3 is reset: main.js uses process.on for SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP, and `stopping` swallows repeats. The runner's SIGHUP (exit 129) goes with any later d2 change. Either way, FU-28's text and g2's runbook name SIGHUP and the double signal.

- SEC-D-13: grounding is lexical, not semantic. A quote that belongs to another field grounds its number ('90 mm lids' -> lidQuantity 90), as does a buyer's SKU or phone fragment, or an idiom ('no one'). The shown quote reveals each of these, and the buyer confirms. Security suggests unit tokens for capacity, diameter and budget.
- SEC-D-14: SEC-D-3 stands for capacity and diameter from the photo, which still have no OCR; TR-D-11 does not change that.
- SEC-D-17:
  - the exit-hook paths leave empty temp cwds behind;
  - d2's cli.test.js sandbox appends the caller's PATH after the stub directory, so on a developer machine a logged-in claude could sit behind it. The RISK-21 class: pass `command:` as the absolute stub path.
I checked SEC-D-17's PATH point by reading: sandbox() builds `PATH: ${bin}${delimiter}${process.env.PATH}`. It is safe as long as the stub is written first, which it is.

findings.detail:
- SEC-D-3, SEC-D-5, SEC-D-6, SEC-D-7 and SEC-D-9 are in carry item 6.
- SEC-D-4 and SEC-D-7 are in FU-29 (g2 README).
- SEC-D-5 is FU-26 (a).
- SEC-D-9's DB rows and the key in a separate process are named as gaps for g3.
- FU-24 is dec-mv330t0g-0175d52b; FU-25 is dec-mv330t7a-017a2211.
The security suggestion attached to SEC-D-3 (re-check every known field when addressedToAssistant is true) is left undecided, which is acceptable for an info item. TR-D-11 removes the worst part of SEC-D-3 for the non-product fields.
findings.recommendation: As mapped.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
Resolved; this is also security's SEC-D-1. normaliseExtraction no longer accepts a digit-free quote: the `written.size === 0 ||` branch is gone. A numeric user_text value must pass numberGroundedInQuote (extraction.js L355-L359), which runs d1's validateExtraction with the text on a single-field probe, so d1's NUMBER_NOT_IN_INPUT rule decides.

Routing instead of export: I accept it. It meets 'reuse rather than a second copy', d1's files stay untouched, and the probe makes every failure attributable to one field. The cost is at most nine small validations. A future whole-object rule in validateExtraction could only downgrade, which is the safe direction.

The six conditions:
(1) Met as above.
(2), (3) Met by the named tests at extract.test.js L220 and L323: 'cups'->777, 'two pickups'->5 and 'a cafe'->250 are unknown with questions; 'two pickups'->2, 'نقطتي استلام'->2, Arabic and English words, Arabic-Indic digits and '1,200'->1200 stay known. Security's E1 strings are not literally in the test, but the class is the same. My P3a shows 'need cups'->99999 and 'lids for the weekend'->777 unknown through the route on HEAD (ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7), and so does security's section E (ev:ev-mv34vttl-015b579b).
(4) Mutants M6 (forced true), M7 (old rule restored) and M8 (probe without the text) are red (ev:ev-mv357tfj-0191a2c4).
(5) npm test and the d3 command pass (ev:ev-mv34x92o-01fef48e, ev:ev-mv34yqr2-01de799d).
(6) My P2, re-run by path, shows cupQuantity and maxPickups unknown, and schema.js still gives NUMBER_NOT_IN_INPUT for both (ev:ev-mv35098k-018beba3).

The bypasses found afterwards are new findings: TR-D-11 (image provenance), TR-D-12 (digit suffix) and TR-D-13 (deadline).

Resolved; this is also security's SEC-D-2. All three conditions hold.
(a) cli.js keeps a per-adapter registry and a module-level set of live children. close() sends SIGTERM to each process group, SIGKILLs it after killGraceMs, rejects the in-flight calls, removes their cwd, and is idempotent and terminal. One exit hook SIGKILLs any group still registered.
(b) main.js close() awaits provider.close() after the retention stop and before app.close(), inside a try/catch that logs by code. The runner's SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers close the adapter, write no report and exit 130/143, and a finally closes it on every path.
(c) Security's C7, inverted, is covered by tests.

The tests pass after the submission:
- the six cli.test.js tests (L325);
- the three stop() tests (uploads-retention.test.js L719);
- the two runner tests with an injected signal target;
- the two real-runner-process tests with a stub claude, SIGTERM->143 and SIGINT->130, child and grandchild gone (live-runner-refusal.test.js L264).
Runs: ev:ev-mv34yg5i-0152378d, ev:ev-mv34yqr2-01de799d.

My own end-to-end check, which the submission lists as not tested (P4, ev:ev-mv35ahlo-01407cf7): a real server process (src/index.js with RS_MODEL_PROVIDER=cli; /api/config reports cli; the stub claude in hang mode first on PATH), with an extract in flight. On SIGTERM it exits 0 after stop(), the stub child and its grandchild are gone, and the in-flight request gets 200 degraded PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE.

Residuals, recorded as new items: TR-D-16 (SIGHUP and the double signal; FU-28) and TR-D-15 (the ledger settles the killed call at 0). The SIGKILL residual is FU-28 and I confirmed it (P4 SIGKILL: the child survives, the row stays reserved at the cap). No stray process was left after my runs.

Resolved. parseCeilingMicroUsd matches the raw string against ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,11})(?:\.([0-9]{1,2}))?$ (no trim, sign, exponent or leading zero; the leading-zero refusal is dec-mv34dqsr-0163a6d9, which is stricter than my pattern and which I agree with). It compares in integer cents, 1..500, before any conversion, and toMicroUsd is no longer used for the ceiling.

The named NFR3 test (live-runner-refusal.test.js L62) refuses 37 values, which I counted from the source; the submission is right and the handoff's 38 is wrong. They include 5.0000001, 5.001, 4.999 and 1e0. It accepts 10 values, including 5, 5.00 and 0.50, and 6 refusals and 3 acceptances also go through a real process.

My probe (ev:ev-mv35auyr-010b9d52) passes 21 values the test does not list, all as expected: '4.995', '5.000', '5e-1', '٠.٥', '１', '5.0\r' and '000000000000005' refused; '3.33' accepted as 3330000. It also checks the order: the switch first, an empty value gives noCeiling, a bad ceiling is refused before the guard check, and a non-string is refused.

The pre-call print of provider, model, per-call cap, worst case, ceiling and `cli: claude 2.1.296` is asserted in the real-process test, which passes (ev:ev-mv34yg5i-0152378d).

RISK-21's possible spend is recorded as an upper bound of USD 1.10 (run.corrected on run-mv330tea-0177469c). Security confirms this with no residual.

handoff.objective: Close TR-D-12 (= SEC-D-11) in the extraction validator: a quote that starts or ends inside a longer number must not ground a smaller value. Third and last review iteration of phase D.
handoff.context: Review rev-mv35hyoj-01e0a18c, finding TR-D-12 (minor), security SEC-D-11. numberGrounded in src/ai/schema.js read only the quote, and the quote rule was a plain substring test, so 250 grounded from '2500 cups', 200 from '1,200 lids'/'1200 lids', 50 ml from '250 ml', 1 from '11:30', $12 from '$1200'. d3 (src/services/extraction.js) routes every numeric user_text field through validateExtraction, so the fix here covers its normaliseExtraction too, with no change in d3's file. Work stayed inside d1's files. d3 and d2 are being reset by others; I did not touch their files.
handoff.expectedOutput: validateExtraction(raw, { text }) refuses (NUMBER_NOT_IN_INPUT on fields.<f>.value) a numeric user_text value whose quote sits in the text only inside a longer number, keeps every legitimate form, and re-checks that every user_text quote (numeric or not) is in the text (NOT_QUOTED), so d3 can rely on it for TR-D-14.
acceptanceCriteria: 250 from '2500 cups', 200 from '1,200 lids' and '1200 lids', 50 ml from '250 ml', 1 from '11:30', $12 and $120 from '$1200' are refused
1,200 -> 1200, 250ml -> 250, $120.50 -> 120.5, Arabic-Indic digits, Arabic thousands separator, English and Arabic number words and the duals are still accepted
tests failing first, a mutant of the alignment shown red and reverted
d1 plan verification command passes; npm test has no failure in d1-owned files
handoff.completedWork: src/ai/schema.js: (1) quoteAlignedInText/alignedAt: the quote must have at least one occurrence in the normalised text that does not start or end inside a number. A number continues over ',' '.' ':' when a digit follows; Arabic-Indic digits and the Arabic thousands/decimal separators are folded to ASCII before the comparison by the existing normalizeForCompare, so they are handled the same way. (2) numberGrounded masks clock times (HH:MM[:SS]) in the quote before reading its numbers, so '11:30' grounds neither 11 nor 30 for a numeric field. The deadline field is a string kind and is not number-grounded in the validator, so the deadline is unaffected (its own grounding is TR-D-13, d3). (3) The doc comment of validateExtraction states the rule. TR-D-14: validateExtraction already checked quote presence (NOT_QUOTED) for every user_text field of every kind, because the substring test sits before the numeric branch; what was missing was a test. I added one (productType, material, deadline: quote not in text -> NOT_QUOTED; present -> ok; case difference and an injected tail -> NOT_QUOTED). d3 may rely on it; the mutant that removes d3's own substring check is now killed by the validator call it already makes, as long as d3 calls validateExtraction with { text } for non-numeric fields too (today numberGroundedInQuote is only called for numeric values: d3 should call the validator for every user_text field). 43 tests added to schema.test.js (18 refused cases, 18 accepted cases, 2 edge tests, 5 TR-D-14 tests). Red run before the fix: 18 of 71 failed (ev:ev-mv35lwdy-01f8cf33), all 18 the refused cases; the 5 TR-D-14 tests passed already. Mutants, all reverted: M1 alignment disabled 16 red (ev:ev-mv35mhaq-0186b5db); M2 separator-then-digit before the quote ignored 4 red (ev:ev-mv35mmi1-01bb91e9); M3 clock masking removed 2 red (ev:ev-mv35mtcw-016cdd03). Green: d1 plan command 154/154 (ev:ev-mv35n0po-013c3a04); npm test 1276 tests, 1268 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped, ECCODE_EVAL 200/200 (ev:ev-mv35nywb-01431134).
remainingIssues: Table words inside a longer word (quote 'one' from 'Someone', SEC-D-13) and a quote that grounds the number but belongs to another field (SEC-D-13) are unchanged: info level, not part of TR-D-12.
The deadline field has no grounding in the validator (TR-D-13 / SEC-D-10); it is d3's task. A d3 deadline check can reuse HH:MM extraction from the quote.
d3 should pass non-numeric user_text fields through validateExtraction too (numberGroundedInQuote is called only when value is a number) so TR-D-14's mutant is killed in d3's own tests.
Evidence run results are on the real code; no model provider is involved (fake/deterministic unit tests), so they say nothing about model quality.
handoff.nextAction: reviewer: verify TR-D-12 with the P3b and G2 probes against HEAD; backend-engineer (d3): call validateExtraction for every user_text field and land TR-D-11/13/14 in the d3 reset.

handoff.objective: Third review iteration of d2: fix TR-D-15 / SEC-D-16 (a call ended by close() was settled at 0 while a timeout is charged at the cap) and SEC-D-17 (cli.test.js sandbox PATH may reach a real claude; empty temp cwds left by the exit hook), inside d2 ownership only.
handoff.context: Review rev-mv35hyoj-01e0a18c, drafts phase-d-2.json TR-D-15 and phase-d-security-2.md SEC-D-16/17. The gate (src/ai/gate.js, d1) refunds a rejected call at microUsdOfUsage(err.usage) and at 0 when err.usage is absent; the service watchdog (src/services/extraction.js callProvider, d3) rejects PROVIDER_TIMEOUT with usage { costMicroUsd: cap }. The shared provider contract test (test/unit/ai/provider-contract.test.js) requires any attached err.usage to have the FULL usage shape (model, costUsd, integer costMicroUsd, token counts, latencyMs), so the adapter marker is the full shape with costMicroUsd = the per-call cap rather than the bare watchdog object; the gate reads only costMicroUsd, so the charge is identical. No real model, no claude binary and no network were used; every command ran with PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin and RS_LIVE_MODEL was never set. The CLI adapter tests use only the repository stub (stub-claude.mjs) in a temp bin directory.
handoff.expectedOutput: An adapter whose killed-started-child rejections (close(), SIGKILL after grace, timeout, abort, output flood) carry the per-call cap as usage so the gate charges the cap; an exit hook that also removes the temp cwd; a cli.test.js sandbox that can never reach a real claude.
acceptanceCriteria: After close() with a call in flight the rejected call carries usage with costMicroUsd equal to the per-call cap, like a timeout
An unchanged call still settles at its reported usage; a failed call that reported usage keeps it
Through a real gate the ledger row of a close()-ended call is settled at the cap, not 0
The cli.test.js child PATH is the stub directory alone and every provider uses the stub's absolute path as command
The exit hook leaves no empty rs-cli-* temp cwd
The d2 plan verification command passes and npm test is green

data.title: FU-32: the adapter charges the cap for any started call it kills
data.decision: Accepted: a CLI call killed by the adapter's own timeout, an abort or the output flood after a child has started is charged at the per-call cap, like a call killed by close() or by the service watchdog.
data.rationale: Once a child has started, the real spend is unknown and bounded only by the cap; charging the cap keeps the ledger conservative and consistent across all kill paths (TR-D-15's principle). Reversible by ai-engineer under FU-26.

data.decision: For version one, a user_text deadline is grounded on its time only (the date part is not checked), and Arabic am/pm markers are not read (such deadlines become unknown and are asked). Both stay listed as residuals in the verification report; they ride FU-23's rework-4 if the user authorizes it, owner backend-engineer.
data.rationale: The buyer confirms every deadline before planning and approves the plan before any payment; an unread marker fails in the safe direction. No task after d3 owns the extraction service and the rework limit is reached (dec-mv341ap0-010209d2).

data.title: SEC-D-13: grounding stays lexical
data.decision: The unit-or-currency-token requirement for capacity, diameter and budget quotes is not adopted in version one. Grounding is lexical (presence, whole-number alignment, field-specific rules for the deadline and image provenance).
data.rationale: The remaining cases (a quote that belongs to another field, codes, idioms) show the mismatch in the quote displayed next to the value, the buyer confirms the fields, and the plan is approved before payment. Reversible; owner backend-engineer with ai-engineer if adopted later.

findings.title: Two mutants of the d2 adapter survive: M19 (the cap in terminate() is pre-empted by the close handler) and M21 (the 'never started is not charged' branch of fail() is untested)
findings.detail:
From my mutation run (ev:ev-mv36q12a-0122343d, which fails by design because my driver fails on any survivor).

- M19: removing the cap from terminate()'s rejection (src/ai/cli.js L198) leaves cli.test.js 38/38 green. When the child exits, Node emits 'close' right after 'exit' once stdio is closed, so the close handler of a terminated run (L246), which also carries unknownAtCap(), settles first. finish() is idempotent, so terminate()'s own rejection never wins in these runs. M19b (L246 only) and M19c (both sites) are killed (ev:ev-mv36r8lf-01323bb3), so the close() charge is pinned by tests. M19 is an equivalent mutant in practice, and L198 is a redundant backstop.
- M21: changing fail() to `usageHint ?? unknownAtCap()` (L206), which charges calls that never started a process, also leaves 38/38 green. The d2 test 'TR-D-15: a call that never started a process ... is not charged' (cli.test.js L467) covers two cases, and neither goes through fail():
  - a provider closed before call(), which is refused at the provider level;
  - a missing binary, which arrives as the child 'error' event.
  The fail() branches without a child are untested: close() while the temp cwd is being made, a signal aborted before the spawn, and a synchronous spawn throw. If that code were wrong, the error would over-charge, which is the conservative direction.

Neither affects the ledger behaviour I verified through the route (P10a, P10b, P10c) and on a real server (P11, P4).
findings.recommendation: Owner: ai-engineer, with the FU-26 adapter change (no later task owns src/ai/cli.js); not required for this phase. Add a test that reaches fail() without a child and asserts err.usage is undefined, for example close() raced against the mkdtemp, or a signal aborted between the call and the spawn. Either drop terminate()'s duplicate usage or comment that the close handler normally settles first. delivery-lead may note it under carry item 8.

handoff.objective: Payment UI for the SPA: PayPal approvals per supplier with provider badges, try-again and abandon after a cancel, complete purchase, receipt, supplier ready and handover, cancelled presentation, polling, with fixtures and a pure view-model test.
handoff.context: Phases C and D already shipped most of the payment screens (components/payments.js, status.js, commitments.js, compensation.js, banner.js, supplier-orders.js, poll.js, api.js methods for the seven phase E routes) and the seven phase E contract fixtures. E5 closed the remaining gaps against the spec: the single-credential notice next to the approvals, no approval button and 'Cancelled — payment did not complete' for orders of a non_executable plan (also in Supplier commitments), a RESERVATION_LIMIT message with a link to the other request, a loading then success then error state for every payment action (success only after a 2xx answer), aria-disabled on buttons while an action runs, a pure nextDelay(elapsed, {hidden}) schedule, and polling while a payment is in flight. Payment view-state fixtures live in test/fixtures/contracts/payments/ (a subdirectory on purpose: test/api/contracts.test.js requires every top-level *.json in test/fixtures/contracts to have a route scenario, and e6 owns that table). No backend file was touched.
handoff.expectedOutput: e2 and e4 serve the answers the fixtures show; e6 enables the seven skipped contract scenarios. If e2/e4 differ from the contract assumptions below, the UI changes are small and local to public/js/components/payments.js and public/js/poll.js.
acceptanceCriteria: 'PayPal approvals: 1 of 2 — Supplier A — Approve with PayPal' with location.assign to the approval URL (no form post), badge Simulated or PayPal Sandbox — no real money, single-credential notice
After a cancel: Try approval again and Abandon purchase; Complete purchase when every supplier confirmed; Record receipt; RESERVATION_LIMIT message with a link to the other request
Orders of a non_executable plan read 'Cancelled — payment did not complete' with supplier actions hidden; the supplier view marks ready and records handover
poll.js: 2 s while transient, 10 s after 2 min, paused when hidden; textContent only; contract fixtures for the payment routes
test/unit/frontend/payments.test.js checks the pure view-model against the payment fixtures
handoff.completedWork: All five criteria are met and covered by test/unit/frontend/payments.test.js (23 tests) and five new scan tests in test/scan/frontend.test.js. Verification command passed (164 tests). npm test passed (1316 tests, 1308 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped; the 8 skips are the contract scenarios that wait for the phase E routes and are not mine). npm run test:browser passed (8 of 8). Separately, an ad-hoc Chromium check (scratch script, not in the repo, API mocked from the fixtures) loaded the seven payment states at 360 px and 1280 px: no horizontal overflow, every button at least 46 px high, approval text, badges and the single-credential notice as specified. That check is not a recorded evidence run and does not exercise the real server or the real approval round trip; e6 owns the browser journey for that.
remainingIssues: CONTRACT ASSUMPTION 1 (e2): RESERVATION_LIMIT details carry only reservationIds, which are not request ids, so the UI cannot link to the other request from the error alone. It calls GET /api/requests and links to every request whose rescueStatus.status is stock_reserved or payment_authorized (other than the current one); it falls back to a link to #/requests when none is found. If e2 adds details.requestIds (ids only, allowed by the envelope rule) the UI uses it first with no change. Not required.

CONTRACT ASSUMPTION 2 (e2/e4): after the buyer returns from PayPal the payment is approved or authorization_pending until the reconciler or return handler reads the authorization. The UI polls on any order payment in approved, authorization_pending, capture_pending, unknown, refund_requested or refund_pending, and on nextStep WAIT, in addition to the spec's list of transient rescue statuses. It relies on Order.payment.status exposing those machine states in RequestView.orders.

CONTRACT ASSUMPTION 3 (e2): Order.presentation is 'cancelled_payment_incomplete' for an order of a non_executable plan whose fulfilment is still 'confirmed' (F-TR-11), and SupplierOrder.can* are all false for it. The UI also hides actions on its own for that presentation, but does not infer the presentation from the plan status.

CONTRACT ASSUMPTION 4 (e2): POST /api/orders/:id/paypal/create returns approvalUrl (http or https); the UI follows it with location.assign only after isNavigableUrl. The fake approval listener URL is http://127.0.0.1:<port>/..., which passes. A non-http(s) link is refused with an error and never followed.
CONTRACT ASSUMPTION 5 (e4): POST /api/plans/:id/execute answers 202 {claimed:true} or 200 {claimed:false}; the UI says 'Purchase started' (never 'paid') and then relies on polling for the outcome.

The Complete purchase button follows nextStep.code COMPLETE_PURCHASE from the server; the client does not re-check that every order is confirmed (the server's execute check order is authoritative and a refusal is shown as an error).

Test-only RS_PAYMENT approval round trip through a real browser (approve at the fake listener, return, poll to payment_authorized) is not covered by e5; it belongs to e6's journey test. The 360 px layout was checked on mocked data only.

test/helpers/paypal-stub.js, test/helpers/webhook-signer.js and test/unit/payments/ were present as untracked files from the test-engineer's e0 work; they are not mine and they passed inside npm test.
