(2) webhook-signer.js: HMAC-SHA256 over id|time|sha256(raw body bytes), signEvent/buildEvent/tamperBody/verifySignature, FAKE_PAYER and PAYER_MARKERS. (3) provider-contract.js: runProviderContract({name, createAdapter, timeoutMs}) with identity, per-method ok shapes and rejections, replay, a method x Outcome-class table (rejected 422, retryable 429, unknown http_5xx, timeout, network, bad_body, with same-requestId retry converging on one effect), status variants, verifyWebhook (signed, tampered, wrong secret, missing headers, byte-exact bodies), OAuth failures, wire mapping, and the no-leak check (log sink, stdout/stderr, Outcomes). (4) paypal-stub.test.js: 160 tests including the stub's own behaviour, the signer, the raw-span scanner, and a REFERENCE adapter defined in the test file (not src/payments/sandbox.js) that runs the whole contract suite against the stub; a deliberately leaky variant proves the leak check fires. Verification command: 160 tests, 160 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (three repeat runs identical). npm test: 1476 tests, 1468 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped (the 8 are contract scenarios waiting for phase E routes, not from this task); p95 54.8 ms.
remainingIssues: FOR E1, FACTORY CONTRACT (full text in the header of provider-contract.js): createAdapter(ctx) with ctx = {merchantKey:'DEFAULT', timeoutMs, log, clock} returns {provider, expectations:{id,simulated,sandbox}, approve(orderId), supports(fault), inject(fault,{count}), clear(), webhookSecret, sensitive(), wire, close()}. ctx.clock is the time source of the SIMULATED side (fixed 2026-10-20T06:00:00Z): pass it to startPaypalStub({clock, appOrigin}) and to the fake. log is a src/log.js logger whose sink the suite captures; the adapter must log only through it. wire is {calls(kind), clear()} over stub.callsOf/clearCalls for the Sandbox harness and null for the fake (wire block then SKIPPED with a reason). For the Sandbox harness: startPaypalStub, build sandbox.js with baseUrl = stub.baseUrl and credentials from stub.merchants.DEFAULT ({clientId, clientSecret, webhookId}), approve = stub.approve, supports = parseFaultName succeeds, inject = stub.fault, clear = stub.clearFaults, sensitive = [...stub.issuedTokens(), clientId, clientSecret, webhookId]. A working harness is createReferenceHarness at the end of test/unit/payments/paypal-stub.test.js. A fault the fake cannot inject makes supports() return false and the test is SKIPPED, never passed: the fake should support at least authorize_denied, authorize_pending, capture_declined, capture_pending, refund_pending, refund_failed, void_fail, auth_expire, lost_response:<kind>, timeout:<kind>, http_500:<kind> (the spec's fault list); the http_<NNN> classes other than 5xx and bad_body are optional for it.

INTERPRETATIONS THE SPEC LEAVES OPEN, to confirm or change in review (the suite and stub pin them): (a) verifyWebhook({merchantKey, headers, rawBody}): headers are an object with lower-case names (as Node's req.headers), rawBody is a Buffer of the exact received bytes. (b) The fake's HMAC scheme is not specified: webhook-signer.js defines signature = base64(HMAC-SHA256(secret, `${transmissionId}|${transmissionTime}|${sha256hex(rawBody)}`)), auth algo header 'SHA256withRSA' (label only), cert url on api.sandbox.paypal.com; src/payments/fake.js verifyWebhook should call verifySignature from the same definition (re-implement it identically, production code cannot import test helpers) and e3's tests sign with signEvent. (c) Missing signature headers: the suite accepts ok{verified:false} or rejected, never verified true. (d) lost_response maps to unknown reason 'network', timeouts to 'timeout' (OAuth included), a 200 with an unparsable body to 'bad_body', 401/403/429 to retryable. (e) A capture of an authorization already CAPTURED answers rejected with issue AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED and a second full refund CAPTURE_FULLY_REFUNDED (spec, 005 semantics); other issue names in the stub (ORDER_NOT_APPROVED, ORDER_ALREADY_AUTHORIZED, AUTHORIZATION_VOIDED, AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, AUTHORIZATION_CANNOT_BE_VOIDED, REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDED, REQUEST_ID_KIND_MISMATCH, MISSING_REQUEST_ID) are stub conventions, not pinned by the suite. (f) getOrder maps capture.authorizationId and refund.captureId from the links rel 'up' of the capture and refund objects, and the stub omits payments.* arrays that are empty (the adapter must default to []). (g) Replay: only 2xx answers are stored; a mutating call without PayPal-Request-Id is 400 (option requireRequestId); the same id on another kind is 422. (h) The stub verifies the webhook signature over the RAW span of the webhook_event member of the request JSON, whitespace before and after the value excluded, so the adapter must splice the received bytes unchanged (the suite asserts stub.lastCall('verify_webhook').webhookEventRaw equals the original body). (i) The approval link is {stub.baseUrl}/checkoutnow?token=[REDACTED] with rel payer-action (option approvalLink {rel, base} produces rel approve or a foreign host to test APPROVAL_HOST_INVALID).

FOR E2/E3/E4/E6: stub.callsOf(kind) / stub.counts() give the per-kind record (requestId, headers, parsed body, status, replayed, fault, merchantKey) for RS-19 body assertions and request-id checks; stub.appOrigin is settable once the app port is known; signEvent({event|rawBody, secret, transmissionId, transmissionTime}) builds the five paypal-* headers for webhook tests, buildEvent({withPayer:true}) plants PAYER_MARKERS to prove payer data is never stored or logged; the stub is in-process only (e6's two-process test counts fake_paypal_calls, which belongs to the DB-backed fake, not to this stub).

LIMITS: the suite proves the adapters agree with this simulation and with the spec's Outcome classes; it does not prove how the real Sandbox behaves (OQ-D5 stays open until test:live-paypal). The timeout cases use a real 500 ms AbortSignal bound (about 5 s total), the only wall-clock dependence; everything else uses the injected clocks. The leak check covers the log sink, process.stdout/stderr writes during one scenario, and every Outcome; it cannot see a leak through a channel the adapter was not given (for example a file). The suite was run only against the reference adapter in the test file, not yet against e1's adapters.
No package-lock.json was created and nothing outside the four owned files was written.

lessonDecisions.note: The lesson applies when designing a hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record or root in a repository with several records; this task designs no hook, guard or root discovery, so its 'Applies when' list does not hold. The guard accepted every nested write here and correctly refused an inline python file writer, asking for the Edit tool.

handoff.objective: Give phase E the payment adapters: the DB-backed fake with faults and the replay model, the fake approval listener with its own CSP, the PayPal Sandbox REST v2 adapter (stub-verified only) and the merchant mapping, all behind the PaymentProvider port, with the shared contract suite run against both adapters.
handoff.context: Built against spec revision 3 (PaymentProvider and Outcome, PayPal Sandbox wire mapping, 005_fake_paypal.sql semantics, fake approval listener SEC-12 and F-TR-14, SEC-3 approval host, SEC-5 webhook key) and e0's handoff ho-mv37ojw0-01fb7411 (stub, signer, contract suite and its factory contract). LIVE-DEPENDENT: sandbox.js is verified only against test/helpers/paypal-stub.js and injected fetch functions; no Sandbox host was contacted, no credential exists, RS_LIVE_MODEL and RS_LIVE_PAYPAL were never set; issue names, link rels and status sets stay the spec's guesses until test:live-paypal runs (OQ-D5 open). Follow-ups: FU-25 (decision dec-mv330t7a-017a2211) and FU-27 done in src/config.js; FU-19 conventions used (fault_flags rows fake_paypal:<fault>, value = supplier code or empty, remaining = count or NULL). The one verified lesson shown at claim does not apply (see lessonDecisions).
inputs: .eccode/artifacts/design/spec.md (Internal module contracts, PayPal Sandbox wire mapping, 005_fake_paypal.sql, Fake approval listener, Admin routes faults, Provider call protocol, Secrets handling)
src/http/headers.js, src/http/host.js, src/http/server.js, src/services/admin.js (fault_flags writer), src/services/void-rule.js (provider port), src/db/migrations/005_fake_paypal.sql
handoff.expectedOutput: src/payments/{provider,fake,listener,sandbox,merchants}.js and the five test files, ready for e2 (payment flow routes), e3 (webhooks), e4 (saga and reconciler), e6 (two-process tests).
acceptanceCriteria: fake.js: state in fake_paypal_*, (merchant_key, request_id) replay with replayed = 1, AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED, CAPTURE_FULLY_REFUNDED, expiration 29 days unless auth_expire, every call counted in fake_paypal_calls, all faults of the spec including lost_response, timeout and http_500 per kind and the RS_TEST_HOOKS-only freeze_after_capture_apply, freeze_before_capture_apply, capture_lands_after_void_intent; payloads labelled simulated: true; fake webhook key generated once into meta

listener.js: second node:http listener on RS_FAKE_APPROVAL_HOST (127.0.0.1 outside test mode), refuses paypal-sandbox, Host check, app security headers except CSP plus exactly one approvalPageCsp(appOrigin), three routes, redirects only to stored URLs

sandbox.js: wire mapping, OAuth cached per merchant until expires_in - 60 s, one AbortSignal timeout covering OAuth, outcome classification, approval host www.sandbox.paypal.com (loopback only with the test flag), credentials never logged
merchants.js maps suppliers to merchant keys and reports per-supplier or single-credential

provider-contract.test.js runs e0's suite against the fake and against the Sandbox adapter with paypal-stub, supports() false for faults a harness cannot inject (skipped, not passed); fake-approval-headers.test.js pins the CSP string and the Location of approve and cancel and checks the app pages still send form-action 'self'
handoff.completedWork: (1) src/payments/provider.js: the port (PROVIDER_METHODS, CALL_KINDS, Outcome constructors ok/rejected/retryable/unknown, toPayPalValue, checkArguments, webhookInput, assertPaymentProvider) and createPayments({config, db, clock, log, appOrigin}) -> {provider, listener, close} which imports the adapter named by config.paymentProvider. A bad argument is a rejected 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT before anything is sent or stored. (2) fake.js: createFakeProvider({db, clock, log, testHooks, webhookSecret, approvalOrigin, pid, freeze}); each call is ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (fault take, replay or effect, fake_paypal_calls row), so processes agree and counts are exact; merchant-scoped lookups; faults read from fault_flags (scenario faults, lost_response/timeout/http_<4xx|5xx>/bad_body per call kind incl. reads and verify_webhook, hooks only with testHooks); approveFakeOrder, loadFakeOrder, takeFakePaypalFault, parseFakeFault, fakeWebhookSignature exported; verifyWebhook is the HMAC scheme of webhook-signer.js; the default freeze sends SIGSTOP to the process (checked in a scratch two-process run: stopped after the capture commit, result returned after SIGCONT). A busy database is a retryable 429 FAKE_DB_BUSY Outcome. (3) listener.js: startApprovalListener({db, clock, config, log, appOrigin}) -> {server, host, port, origin, close}; the three routes, 303 only to the stored URLs (token and PayerID set with URL), one CSP header from approvalListenerHeaders(appOrigin) plus Cache-Control no-store, Host check on its own host and port (421), 404/405/409/413 pages with the same headers, refusal for paypal-sandbox and non-loopback hosts, an unusable app origin still sends one restrictive CSP and a 500 page. (4) sandbox.js: createSandboxProvider({baseUrl, merchants, timeoutMs, testOffline, log, clock, fetch}); constructor refuses any base URL but the Sandbox API (loopback only with testOffline); one AbortSignal.timeout per call over OAuth, API call and body reads; redirects never followed; 1 MiB response cap; issue names reduced to upper-case tokens (no provider text is copied); 401 drops the cached token; approval link check (APPROVAL_HOST_INVALID / APPROVAL_LINK_MISSING); verifyWebhook proves the body is exactly one JSON object (strict UTF-8, BOM kept) and splices the received bytes; ok payloads carry provider paypal-sandbox and sandbox: true. (5) merchants.js: SUPPLIER_MERCHANT_KEYS, merchantMode, activeMerchantKeys, isActiveMerchantKey, merchantKeyForSupplier, merchantCredentials (Secret values), sandboxMerchants, describeMerchants (secret-free). (6) src/config.js: RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE parsing and config.explainRephrase removed (FU-25); RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS bounded to 1..40000 (MAX_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS), default 30000 (FU-27). (7) Tests: fake.test.js 41, sandbox.test.js 35, merchants.test.js 14 (incl. 'TR-D-7: RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS above 40000 is refused ...' and the FU-25 test, placed here because test/unit/config/limits.test.js is outside e1's ownership), provider-contract.test.js runs e0's suite twice (216 tests: 209 pass, 7 skipped), fake-approval-headers.test.js 18. Defects found by the tests and fixed before completion: the fake's verifyWebhook opened a nested transaction when it had to create the SEC-5 key (contract suite); the Sandbox adapter returned bad_body for an authorization the double reports already EXPIRED (contract suite, auth_expire); the fake counted a verifyWebhook call with an unusable body (fake.test.js); TextDecoder stripped a leading BOM from a webhook body, so the spliced bytes were not the received ones (sandbox.test.js). A mutation (a second CSP header appended in the listener) was caught by 5 header tests and reverted. Verification command: 484 tests, 477 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped (the 7 are the fake harness's OAuth and wire scenarios, skipped because supports() is false or wire is null, not passed). npm test: 1800 tests, 1781 pass, 4 fail, 15 skipped; the 4 failures are the direct consequence of FU-25 in files outside e1's ownership (see remainingIssues 1); the 15 skips are the 7 above plus the 8 contract scenarios waiting for phase E routes.
remainingIssues: FU-25 BREAKS 4 TESTS OUTSIDE E1'S OWNERSHIP (npm test: ev:ev-mv38e6wu-01748302 and ev:ev-mv38bsgw-01e94ad3, 4 fail): test/unit/config/defaults.test.js asserts c.explainRephrase false (line 38) and true with RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE=1 (lines 84 and 124); test/unit/config/limits.test.js 'boolean switches accept only 0 or 1' lists RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE (line 76); test/scan/env-example.test.js has RS_EXPLAIN_REPHRASE in its DEFAULTS table (line 65) and .env.example still lists it (line 93, g2 per the decision). Whoever owns those files (g2 or the orchestrator) must drop those lines; the replacement assertions already exist in test/unit/payments/merchants.test.js ('FU-25: ...'). Until then npm test is red by exactly these 4. Comments in src/ai/provider.js:11 and src/ai/rephrase.js:1 still mention the variable (not e1 files).

FOR E2 (construction): after app.listen(), call createPayments({config, db, clock, log, appOrigin: () => app.deps.publicUrl()}) and assign app.deps.payments = payments.provider (ctx is spread from deps per request, so late assignment works); close() on shutdown. Pass voidProvider to createApp separately: its queueVoid(db, intent) must INSERT OR IGNORE so:<supplierOrderId>:void:1 into provider_calls (c3 port, FU-19). The listener is started inside createPayments only for the fake and is null for the Sandbox; its origin is what createOrder returns as approvalUrl (default port 0, so tests read listener.port). merchantKeyForSupplier(config, supplierCode) gives the merchantKey for every provider call (fake: the supplier code; Sandbox: per merchant mode); isActiveMerchantKey(config, key) is the webhook route's 'configured key else 404' check. The return handler's crash hook is takeFakePaypalFault(db, 'crash_after_return_commit', {merchantKey, testHooks: config.testHooks}).

FOR E2/E3/E4 (Outcomes): ok values are the port shapes plus provider and simulated (fake) or provider and sandbox (Sandbox). authorizeOrder status is CREATED, PENDING or DENIED (an authorization already EXPIRED when PayPal answers is reported CREATED with its past expirationTime). Definitive rejections to expect: INVALID_ARGUMENT (400, nothing sent), MERCHANT_NOT_CONFIGURED, APPROVAL_HOST_INVALID and APPROVAL_LINK_MISSING (createOrder: the order exists at PayPal but is unusable), WEBHOOK_ID_MISSING (verifyWebhook without a webhook id; the route decides its answer), REQUEST_ID_KIND_MISMATCH, ORDER_NOT_APPROVED, ORDER_ALREADY_AUTHORIZED, AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED / _VOIDED / _EXPIRED / _PENDING / _DENIED / _AMOUNT_EXCEEDED, AUTHORIZATION_CANNOT_BE_VOIDED, CAPTURE_FULLY_REFUNDED, CAPTURE_NOT_COMPLETED, REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDED. The fake alone also answers retryable 429 FAKE_DB_BUSY. verifyWebhook returns ok {verified:false} (never an error) for missing or malformed signature headers or a body that is not one JSON object.

FOR E3/E4/E6 (fake behaviour): a fake PENDING authorization, capture or refund never settles by itself; tests move it with SQL on fake_paypal_* (there is no settle helper). verify_webhook calls are counted in fake_paypal_calls (kind 'verify_webhook'), approval-page requests are not. fake_paypal_calls.resource_id is the id of the resource a call created, else the one it addressed. Faults are consumed inside the call's own transaction; a fault row whose value is a supplier code applies only to that merchant key. The test-only faults are ignored (and stay armed) unless createFakeProvider got testHooks: true (createPayments passes config.testHooks). Fault kinds beyond the admin list work too (every call kind, http_<400-599>, bad_body) for tests that insert fault_flags rows directly. freeze_* default to process.kill(pid, 'SIGSTOP') (POSIX only); a unit test can inject freeze.

SPEC GAPS RESOLVED (to confirm in review): (a) order status of the fake after authorize is COMPLETED and after a void VOIDED; (b) the fake stores only ok answers in fake_paypal_requests, like the stub; (c) a void is allowed on CREATED and PENDING authorizations; (d) fake auth_expire stores expiration_time = now and reads show EXPIRED (persisted lazily as status EXPIRED); (e) the fake approval page lists a merchant label 'Merchant <key> (simulated)' and has no stylesheet because style-src 'self' with exactly three routes leaves nowhere to serve one; (f) the listener adds Cache-Control: no-store to the app's headers; (g) argument validation limits: ids [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}, request id [A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,108}, amountCents 1..999999999, USD only, return/cancel URLs http(s) without credentials up to 2048 chars, webhook body 1..65536 bytes; (h) whitespace OUTSIDE the webhook JSON object is not covered by the Sandbox path, because the double (and PayPal's parser) verify the member span, which excludes it, while the fake signs every byte.

LIMITS: the Sandbox adapter proves agreement with the simulation and the spec's Outcome classes only; the real issue names, link rels (payer-action vs approve), status sets, the 29-day expiry, token lifetime and the verify-webhook request shape are unconfirmed until test:live-paypal runs. The timeout cases use real 400-500 ms AbortSignal bounds (about 5 s in the contract suite). The approval listener's behaviour in a real browser (form-action across the 303 chain) is not re-tested here; fake-approval-headers.test.js pins the bytes, the earlier Playwright run is ev:ev-mv1dsh6c-019c5a8d.
Process note: the tests were written after the code; each defect listed in completedWork was found by a test and fixed before completion, not by a failing test written first.

Log: one webhook.received line per request with provider, code and httpStatus (allow-listed keys only). (2) src/routes/webhooks.js: router.add POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey policy signature. (3) test/api/webhooks.test.js: 96 tests, all passing: access (policy signature, no cookie/CSRF/foreign Origin, 404 for Z F a AA, GET 405), body limit (65,536 accepted, 65,537 -> 413), 38 pre-check cases (each header missing/empty/overlong, id shapes, algo, five time shapes, ten cert URL shapes, eleven body shapes) each asserting 400, one invalid row with the flag_reason, payload_json NULL, sha256 of the bytes and ZERO fake_paypal_calls, the accepted edges (64-char id, 14:59 either way, +03:00 offset, paypal.com and api.sandbox.paypal.com:443) and zero net-guard blocked attempts, RS_PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ALGOS, forged-id poisoning (T13), RS-24 (tampered body, wrong secret, garbage signature, altered headers, re-serialised body, unreachable with http 500/429/422 faults then the retry applied, WEBHOOK_ID_MISSING, throwing and missing adapter), RS-23 (replay x3, different payload under a used id, five concurrent copies -> one applied + four duplicate + one hook call), 21 event/transition cases plus id fallbacks, id mismatches, no-match, SEC-16 (other merchant URL, other provider, archived, with a positive control), the hook (real void port: one so:<id>:void:1 row, replay and second event add none; recorder port; unknown and denied-capture paths; rollback of move, row and audit when the hook throws, then the retry applies), byte-exact raw body (BOM, whitespace/CRLF outside the object, BOM + raw non-ASCII + escapes, odd layout with duplicate keys: the adapter receives Buffer-equal bytes, stored sha256 matches, the five headers arrive lower-case), SEC-6 (61st request -> 429 with Retry-After, no row, no provider call, counter not incremented, 404 for an unknown key, admitted after the window; per-client budgets with RS_TRUST_PROXY=1 and an IPv6 /64 shared), T13 privacy (payer data, amounts, notes and shipping never in webhook_events, audit_events, payment_operations, any log line or any answer; refused/unverified/failed requests leak neither the signature nor the shared secret; log lines carry requestId and only allow-listed keys), and one Sandbox-adapter test against paypal-stub.js (verify_webhook received the merchant's webhook id; forged -> 400; a BOM body is never sent to the stub). Failing-first: the tests were written after the code (not test-first); each named behaviour was then pinned by mutation (scratch edits, file restored byte-identical, cmp verified): dedupe over all rows (7 tests fail), no merchant/provider/archived scoping (SEC-16 test fails), hook disabled (5 fail), body trimmed before verification (5 fail incl. the Sandbox test), rate limit removed (2 fail), CAS/state-table check bypassed (7 fail), cert host by substring (2 fail), time window one-sided (1 fails), full event stored as payload (privacy test fails). Test-code defects found and fixed while writing: the 200 body carries requestId (split off by the helper, pinned once), audit_events is append-only (tests use a per-test id floor), the fake reports a rejected verification with its own issue code. No production defect was found by a failing test.
remainingIssues: npm test is RED by one test, outside my files and expected: ev:ev-mv3a96vq-0142da7d (FAILED, 1964 tests, 1948 pass, 1 fail, 15 skipped, 0 cancelled). test/api/contracts.test.js 'NFR6: every registered route has a scenario in the table' now lists THREE registered routes without a scenario: GET /api/paypal/return, GET /api/paypal/cancel (e2) and POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey (e3). e6 (test-engineer) adds `route:` rows (no fixture is needed or exists for the webhook route; a scenario would sign with webhook-signer.js and the fake's secret from RS_FAKE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and expect 200 {outcome} plus requestId, and 400 WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID for an unsigned body). rbac.test.js and every other test pass: the route is policy signature, not public, so the by-design rbac failure did not occur and no edit to that test is needed.

SPEC CONFLICT (decision needed from the orchestrator): the Webhooks pre-check says the body must have a MAPPED event_type (failure -> invalid row, 400) while the event list says 'Unknown types -> ignored'. I followed the task's acceptance criterion: an unmapped type is a pre-check failure (invalid row EVENT_TYPE_NOT_MAPPED, 400), because it is the only reading that keeps SEC-6's 'no provider call for junk'. Consequence: a PayPal webhook subscribed to extra event types gets 400 and PayPal retries those until it gives up; the README/runbook must say to subscribe the webhook to the seven mapped events only. If the orchestrator prefers 'ignored', it is a one-line change in precheck() (keep a well-formed string, drop the mapped check, let applyEvent return ignored) and the test table in 'SEC-6: ... event_type that is not mapped'.

src/config.js does not parse RS_PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ALGOS and .env.example does not list it (both outside my files; the spec names the variable). webhookAlgos(config) reads config.paypalWebhookAlgos if the configuration provides an array, otherwise process.env.RS_PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ALGOS at request time, otherwise SHA256withRSA. The owner of src/config.js should add `paypalWebhookAlgos: r.list(...)` (and the .env.example line, which test/scan/env-example.test.js checks against config.js), after which the env fallback can go.

A body with a leading BOM is accepted by the route (parsed without it, verified as the exact bytes). The fake adapter verifies it (HMAC over the bytes); the Sandbox adapter answers ok {verified:false} for it (JSON.parse refuses a BOM), so on the Sandbox such a body is an invalid row and 400 without a provider call (tested). PayPal does not send a BOM, so this affects only a hand-made request. Whitespace outside the object is passed through unchanged; the Sandbox double verifies the member span, so a whitespace-wrapped body signed over all bytes would not verify there (e1's note (h)); not tested at the stub.

Not covered by e3 tests (not mine or not reachable here): the real PayPal event shapes and names (OQ-D5, LIVE-DEPENDENT: PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED/VOIDED, PAYMENT.CAPTURE.*, the supplementary_data.related_ids and the 'up' link used for fallback matching are PayPal-doc conventions verified only against my own fixtures); a webhook-driven end-to-end run through the real fake approval, return and capture flow (operations are put into a state with SQL set-up, as the stated state is what the route reacts to); two real OS processes racing one transmission id (the single-process concurrency test and the partial UNIQUE index catch are covered; the index race branch is not exercised by a test); retention of invalid/unverified rows after 7 days (retention.js, not mine).

Rate counter rows: an admitted request inserts one rate_events row (kind webhook, key ip:<key>); the route deletes that key's expired rows on each request, and retention.js purges rate_events older than 24 h. A flood from many distinct IPv6 /64 prefixes leaves one row each until retention runs (bounded by 60 per key per minute).
handoff.nextAction: orchestrator: (1) decide the pre-check/ignored conflict above and send it back if 'ignored' is preferred; (2) assign src/config.js + .env.example for RS_PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ALGOS; (3) e6 (test-engineer): add the three missing route rows to test/api/contracts.test.js (npm test is red by exactly that test); (4) give e4 the notes below; (5) send e3 to review. NOTES FOR e4/e6. e4 (reconciler, saga): a webhook can move an operation without the reconciler: authorization_pending|approved|unknown(prev ok) -> authorized (+ provider_authorization_id, authorization_expires_at, the resolution hook), authorized -> voided, authorized|capture_pending -> captured (+ provider_capture_id), authorized -> capture_pending, capture_pending -> authorized (denied), refund_pending -> refunded (+ provider_refund_id). It clears unknown_since when it moves an unknown operation, leaves prev_status as it was and does NOT touch provider_calls rows: an open unknown/intent call row of that operation stays for the reconciler, which must therefore treat 'the operation is already past that state' as a resolved call (CAS on status, no error), exactly like recordCall's authorize/void mappers already do. A capture event moves an operation outside the saga lease; the saga must re-read the operation status after its capture call and accept captured as done. Webhook rows never reach the reconciler; it keeps polling (webhooks are secondary). The admin timeline already reads webhook_events (source 'webhook', detail outcome/signatureStatus/flagged). Flagged rows (outcome flagged, flagged = 1, flag_reason) are the operator's list; nothing else reads them yet. e6: the route answers 200 {outcome: applied|ignored|flagged|duplicate, requestId}; errors 400 WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID (no details), 404 NOT_FOUND, 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, 429 RATE_LIMITED details.limit webhook_ip + Retry-After, 503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE + Retry-After 30 (and 503 DB_BUSY). Tests sign with signEvent({event|rawBody, transmissionTime: <harness clock ISO>}) and the harness env must set RS_FAKE_WEBHOOK_SECRET to FAKE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (the fake otherwise generates a random key in meta). The harness clock is fixed at 2026-10-20T06:00:00Z, so the signer's default new Date() transmission time is outside the 15-minute window: always pass transmissionTime.

lessonDecisions.note: The lesson applies to hooks or guards that map file writes to a project record or root. This task changes a SQL migration, the application's general limiter and tests; it contains no hook, guard or root discovery, so none of the 'Applies when' conditions holds.

handoff.objective: FU-23 / TR-D-3: ids of rescue_requests, planning_runs, plan_versions and images are never reused after a hard delete, and model_spend.request_id is a foreign key; SEC-R-1: the general per-user limit fails open for GET and HEAD on a busy write lock and stays fail-closed for everything else.
handoff.context: Phase D review rev-mv33xoyz-0143dd56 (TR-D-3), security draft phase-d-security-1.md section F (probe ev:ev-mv33e5qp-017ba56b, decision dec-mv330std-0165d9be) and rework-1 review rework-1-1.json (SEC-R-1). Migration 006 is app-only. The runner (src/db/migrate.js) applies a file inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE with foreign_keys = ON, which cannot be switched off inside a transaction, so the rebuild uses defer_foreign_keys = ON and TEMP staging tables. DROP TABLE runs an implicit DELETE that fires ON DELETE CASCADE, so extractions, requirements, replan_queue and plan_approvals are staged and put back with their ids; non-cascading children (reservations, supplier_orders, payment_operations, provider_calls) stay and are satisfied again when the parent ids are re-inserted; a parent that does not come back fails the COMMIT on the deferred foreign key and rolls everything back. Tables are recreated under their own names, so no RENAME rewrites other tables. The SEC-B-2 triggers sit on audit_events and inventory_ledger, which are not touched. CHOICE for model_spend.request_id: FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES rescue_requests(id) ON DELETE SET NULL. The row is the budget ledger (gate.js sums every row of the day), so it must survive a hard delete of its request, and SET NULL drops only the pointer so it can never name another request; an insert naming a request that does not exist is refused. A CHECK cannot look at another table, and a tombstone reference would add a second source of truth to keep. Rows that already point at a deleted request are copied with NULL. SEC-R-1: take(userId, { method, log, requestId }) in src/auth/general-limit.js; GET/HEAD busy error -> return uncounted plus one warn line rate_limit.busy_open (requestId only), reads wait readBusyWaitMs (default 50 ms) instead of the connection busy timeout and the timeout is restored; other methods and a call with no method rethrow the busy error unchanged (the app maps it to 503 DB_BUSY); 429 over the limit is unchanged.

handoff.completedWork: (1) src/services/saga.js (new): processExecutorId (<hostname>:<pid>:<8 hex>), claimExecution (check order: plan status, reservation active and not past expiry, pending/approved/unknown-prev-approved -> AUTHORIZATION_PENDING, any operation not authorized -> AUTHORIZATION_MISSING, any order not confirmed -> COMMITMENT_MISSING, stored expiry <= now + margin -> AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED with the void rule committed before the 409; one BEGIN IMMEDIATE; conditional UPDATE; reservation consumed with consume ledger rows written locally because ledger.js has no consume; one capture intent per order; audit ok / denied), createSaga (begin/start/idle/stop, autoRun flag, runs keyed by plan and epoch), step 2 (getAuthorization per operation under G with a lease renewal before each read; a failed read pauses), step 3 (sequential, startCall with a guard = G(now) + operation authorized + earlier operations captured + lease_epoch stamped on the call; recordCall with apply = capture mapping and fence = epoch; pause when the first non-captured operation is capture_pending/unknown or a retryable answer is backing off; the saga re-reads after the call and accepts captured by a webhook), step 4 (executed, lease_until NULL), step 5 compensation (one transaction under G: CAPTURE_FAILED | AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, reservation consumed -> reconciling, cancel_requested_at on every open operation, queued captures cancelled, voids and refunds queued, then sent), queueRefundWhenCancelled (the compensation hook for captured), releaseIfSettled (reconciling -> released with restock rows; escalation REFUND_FAILED, VOID_FAILED, UNKNOWN_TOO_LONG, PENDING_TOO_LONG). (2) src/services/reconciler.js (new): the nine steps in spec order, createReconciler (tick joins a running tick, start/stop, meta reconciler_last_tick_at / _ms), resolution by reading for authorize, capture, void and refund (unknown) with the resolution hook and compensation hook in the same transaction, polls with the 5-minute back-off, takeover (never while an operation is capture_pending/unknown or the next capture backs off) that starts the saga with the new epoch, backstops (queued authorize of a cancelled operation -> voided locally; captured + cancelled -> refund; authorized + cancelled without a void -> void), drainReplanQueue, housekeeping. (3) src/routes/plans.js: POST /api/plans/:id/execute (202 {claimed:true,plan} / 200 {claimed:false,plan,rescueStatus}). (4) src/app.js: deps.saga, executorId option, app.close() stops the saga. (5) src/main.js: voidProvider real port, reconciler started after the startup retention pass, returned as reconciler / reconcilerStarted / payments; close() stops the reconciler first; d3's close order and signal handling untouched. (6) Tests: execute.test.js 28, lost-response.test.js 9, authorization-pending.test.js 6, void-rule-lost-authorize.test.js 6, reconciler.test.js 21 = 70 passing (ev:ev-mv3tkpcw-015107ae). Failing-first: the tests were written AFTER the code, not before. Mutation proof (scratch copy of the project under the session scratchpad, real tree never mutated; no ev id because the runs were plain node --test in the copy): lease guard without lease_until (1 test fails), result fence removed (killed only after adding the test 'the epoch is a fence of its own'; before it the mutant survived because the send_token fence also refused), stale-intent step disabled (4 fail), CAPTURED treated as CREATED so a capture is sent again (7 fail), takeover ignoring capture_pending/unknown (3 fail), resolution hook removed from the authorize read (1 fail), poll back-off removed (1 fail), webhook purge 7 days -> 1 hour (1 fail), check order MISSING/COMMITMENT swapped (1 fail), refund_failed counted as settled (2 fail), reservation not consumed and compensation without voids (7 fail), step 2 always run on resume (3 fail). Equivalent or masked mutants: removing the supplier-code-order check inside the capture start guard changes nothing observable (the loop already picks the first non-captured operation; it is defense in depth); removing the resolution hook from the pending poll or the abandon path is masked by the reconciler backstop (authorized + cancelled without a void gets one next step 6). A first attempt to run a mutant inside the real tree was refused by the auto-mode classifier ([Security Weaken]); the edit was reverted at once (grep verified) and the mutants were run in the scratch copy instead. Test-code defects found while writing: void clears last_error_code (assertion moved to the call row), a retryable refund leaves the operation refund_pending, a hand-made capture row needs the operation's amount. No production defect was found by a failing test.
remainingIssues: npm test is RED by exactly one test in both full runs (ev:ev-mv3tmhcb-01d1ce5d and ev:ev-mv3tocgo-01208df8: 2055 tests, 2039 pass, 1 fail, 15 skipped): test/api/contracts.test.js 'NFR6: every registered route has a scenario in the table' lists GET /api/paypal/return, GET /api/paypal/cancel and POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey (e2/e3 routes). It is e6's file; the new execute route is NOT in that list because plan-execute.json and plan-execute-replay.json already have table rows (still skip rows 'not registered yet': e6 should enable them; the real answers match the fixtures' key sets). npm run test:browser passes 8/8 (ev:ev-mv3tok1s-012c36bd).

RS-39 flake reported by the coordinator (ev:ev-mv3t54i6-01a9b844, passes alone ev:ev-mv3t6bo7-015fdd78): the root cause is in test/api/uploads-retention.test.js (d3): it checks the file right after the row is gone while the sweep unlinks after deleting the row. I reduced the load by starting the reconciler's first tick after the startup retention pass; the race itself remains in the test and the orchestrator should route the one-line fix (wait for the file or for retention.started). Both of my full npm test runs passed that test.

Re-plan drain: drainReplanQueue lives in reconciler.js (2 entries per tick, runPlanningFor, failed_drains + 1 and next_attempt_at = now + min(5 min, 15 s x 2^old failed_drains), entries of archived or deleted requests dropped). f1 owns supersession.js and the queue semantics: if f1 wants it elsewhere or the exponent to use the incremented count, it is a one-line change here, but F-PL-3 forbids f1 from editing reconciler.js, so decide before f1 starts. The 'after 5 failed drains the next step is REPLAN' rule is derive.js's and already works from failed_drains.

Stale model-spend rows (FU-22 owner): both the retention sweep (d3) and reconciler housekeeping call gate.settleStale; it is one compare-and-set UPDATE on status = 'reserved', so a row settles once whichever runs first. d3's call was left in place (not my file).

Stock helpers: consume and restock ledger rows are written by local functions in saga.js because services/ledger.js (c3) has no consume/restock function. They follow ledger.js's row format and the SUM(delta) invariant is asserted in the tests; moving them into ledger.js is a later tidy-up.

The webhook route (e3) moves operations without running the compensation hook for captured; the reconciler backstop (step 6) queues the refund on its next tick instead. If e3's file is touched later it should call queueRefundWhenCancelled (exported from saga.js) in the same transaction.

RESERVATION_EXPIRED on execute also runs the expiry pass inline (expireDueReservations) so the answer and the stored state agree: the plan becomes non_executable (RESERVATION_EXPIRED), stock released, voids sent. The spec does not say; it is the same pass the reconciler would run.

A authorization expired/voided found when a void is refused (resolveRejectedVoid, e2) ends as void_failed by the spec's 'anything else' rule; step 2 compensation after an authorization the provider already shows VOIDED ends voided (the void is refused, getAuthorization says VOIDED).

Not covered here by design: the two-OS-process execute test (e6), SIGKILL/SIGSTOP restart and lease-takeover tests with real processes (f4); the in-process fence test uses a second saga identity over the same database, and the freeze hooks were not used. LIVE-DEPENDENT: real PayPal behaviour of final_capture, DUPLICATE_INVOICE_ID on the capture invoice id (rs-so-<id>-cap), AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED semantics and request-id retention is unverified until test:live-paypal runs (OQ-D5).
Mutation proofs have no ev ids (plain runs in a scratch copy of the project); the list is in completedWork.
handoff.nextAction: delivery-lead: (1) send e4 to independent review (reviewer, not the author); (2) test-engineer (e6): add the three missing route rows to contracts.test.js and enable the two execute fixtures; (3) route the one-line fix of test/api/uploads-retention.test.js (RS-39) to its owner; (4) f1/f4: see the notes in remainingIssues and the contract notes below. NOTES FOR e6/f1/f4: execute answers 202 {claimed:true, plan:{id,status:'executing'}, requestId} or 200 {claimed:false, plan:{id,status}, rescueStatus, requestId}; refusals are 409 PLAN_SUPERSEDED, PLAN_NOT_EXECUTABLE (details.reason), RESERVATION_EXPIRED, AUTHORIZATION_PENDING, AUTHORIZATION_MISSING, COMMITMENT_MISSING, AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, INVALID_STATE (plan not approved, or approved without any reservation), each audited as denied. Tests drive the saga with h.app.deps.saga (autoRun, start(planId, epoch), idle(), stop(), executorId; createSaga(deps, {executorId}) makes a second identity over the same database) and the reconciler with createReconciler(h.app.deps, {saga}).tick(); a tick starts resumed sagas in the background (await saga.idle()). Tests must install the real void port (h.app.deps.voidRule = createVoidRule({clock, provider: createVoidPort({clock})})) because createApp keeps the recorder as its default. Fault names used: lost_response:<kind> (effect applied), timeout:<kind> (nothing applied), http_429/422/500:<kind>, capture_declined, capture_pending, refund_pending, refund_failed, authorize_pending, authorize_denied, crash_after_return_commit, capture_lands_after_void_intent. For f4 (restart recovery): a stale started intent becomes unknown after 2 x RS_PAYPAL_TIMEOUT_MS (error_code STALE_INTENT); takeover needs lease_until <= now and happens only when no operation is capture_pending/unknown; the resumed saga repeats step 2 when every capture has send_count 0, else resumes at step 3 and re-sends an unknown capture (same key) only after the reconciler restored the operation to authorized by reading. For f1: supersession of an approved plan still goes through ctx.voidRule; the execute claim refuses a superseded plan and a plan whose authorization expiry is inside the margin runs markNonExecutable(AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED) in the refusal's transaction.

review.summary:
Technical review of rework-4 (sub-mv3t8kff-017759bd: migration 006, the fail-open general limiter, the access-hook wiring and six test files, plus the submission), against the resolution conditions of TR-D-3 (phase D review rev-mv33xoyz-0143dd56) and SEC-R-1 (rework-1 review). The security draft rework-4-security-1.md (FINAL) is folded in with its ids.

Decision: changes requested, for one major finding, SEC-RW4-1. The security reviewer rates it minor; I raise it to major, with my own reproduction.
- **What goes wrong:** 006 seeds sqlite_sequence from the highest id that survives. Ids hard-deleted on 005 above that id are handed out again after the upgrade, while audit_events and model_spend still name them.
- **My reproduction (ev:ev-mv3u855g-011d4c00):** X deletes request 2 with image 11, run 101 and plan version 30 on 005. After 006, Y's next rows get exactly 2/11/101/30, and 2 of X's audit rows sit on Y's request id. With the security reviewer's ~10 lines of sequence statements, the next ids are 3/12/102/31, the FK and integrity checks are clean, and the rows are unchanged.
- **Why major:** the rebuild exists for databases that already hold data, and on exactly those the condition 'ids never reused' fails. It can be repaired only before 006 is applied anywhere: NFR1 refuses an edit afterwards, and a 007 cannot take back ids already handed out. The rework limit is used, so a change after approval would need a fifth rework from the user. Now it is a reset of this task.

Everything else holds.

Declared checks:
- Green set: 120/120 (ev:ev-mv3teu8p-01309af2).
- npm test, runs 1 and 2: 2055 tests, 2039 pass, 1 fail, 15 skipped each. The one failure is e6's known route-table row (ev:ev-mv3tgz6r-011bfe69, ev:ev-mv3tiyy9-01f99271).
- npm test, run 3, through a known-failure filter, after e4's final commit: 2062 tests, 2054 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped, ECCODE_EVAL 200/200 (ev:ev-mv3u0bm4-018df267).
- npm run test:browser: 8/8 (ev:ev-mv3tj9bo-01e55981).

My own checks:
- Falsification (ev:ev-mv3toj9i-01cfede3): the control is green, 87/87. The pre-rework source fails 7 of 14. All 13 mutants are killed: 6 on the migration, 5 on the limiter, 1 on the hook.
- Probes (ev:ev-mv3tp49m-017879bb): SEC-R-1 end to end through createApp, and 006 on a seeded WAL file database (all 3454 rows equal; schema equal to a fresh one).
- Migration cost (ev:ev-mv3tpe9a-016d484a). Coverage: 9 declared, 9 changed, 9 submitted (ev:ev-mv3tps3r-01befc44). sha256 of the artifacts unchanged (ev:ev-mv3tpsb0-01a2c0fe).

SEC-R-1 is resolved. The other findings are minor or info: TR-R4-1..TR-R4-4 and TR-R4-6..TR-R4-9, and SEC-RW4-I1..I5. TR-R4-5 is merged into SEC-RW4-I2.

criteria.description: FU-23 and SEC-R-1: ids never reused; general limit fails open on busy reads

Phase D review rev-mv33xoyz-0143dd56 TR-D-3 and security draft: rescue_requests, plan_versions, images and planning_runs use INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, so after a hard delete of the highest id the next row reuses it and audit rows or a model_spend row point at another customer's request; migration 006 rebuilds those tables with AUTOINCREMENT (app-only, data preserved), model_spend.request_id gets a foreign key or check, and an RS-39 test shows no id is reused. Rework-1 review SEC-R-1: src/auth/general-limit.js takes the write lock on every signed-in call; GET and HEAD fail open on a busy error (the request proceeds uncounted and the event is logged), with a lock-holder test. Only b1 and c1 (approved) owned these files. Required before e4.
criteria.notes:
Not met: on an upgraded database, the next row takes over an id that was hard-deleted before the upgrade, and that id's audit rows then point at another customer's request. That is the very harm the condition names, and it is reproduced in ev:ev-mv3u855g-011d4c00 and ev:ev-mv3twi5f-015c7a17.

The safety argument's point 6 ('a deleted highest id is never handed out again') holds only for deletes made after the upgrade.

What is met:
- The existing checks pass (run 3 is green).
- The scope extension was justified.
- The record of the refused second handoff is complete (TR-R4-7).
- 'Before e4': e4 was built in parallel (TR-R4-8).

criteria.description: The rework's not-applicable decision on mem-sd-mv1audrd-013b7102 holds
criteria.notes: The lesson applies to hooks or guards that map file writes to a project record or root. The rework's nine files are a SQL migration, the application's rate limiter and access hook, and tests. None of them is a tool-call guard, a pre-commit hook or root discovery. Not applicable.

findings.title: Migration 006 hands out again ids that were hard-deleted before the upgrade, so FU-23's cross-customer audit mix-up reappears on every upgraded database
findings.detail:
006 re-inserts the surviving rows, which sets each sqlite_sequence to max(id) of the survivors (comment at L20: 'the best high-water mark that is known'). Higher ids are known, though:
- audit_events.entity_id (request, image, plan_version);
- audit_events.detail_json of plan.create (planVersionId, runId);
- the staged model_spend.request_id.

Reproduction:
- Mine (ev:ev-mv3u855g-011d4c00): X hard-deletes request 2 (image 11, run 101, plan version 30) on 005. After 006, Y's next request, image, run and plan version get 2/11/101/30, and 2 of X's audit rows name Y's request id.
- The security reviewer's, through the real HTTP flows (ev:ev-mv3twi5f-015c7a17): Y gets request 5 and image 4, and the admin timeline of Y's request lists X's request.create, extraction.run and request.delete. It also reproduces in isolation (ev:ev-mv3u2o6u-0130d038).

The proposed statements raise each sequence to the highest named id before the staging tables are dropped. With them the next ids are 3/12/102/31, the FK and integrity checks are clean and the rows are unchanged; both reviewers ran this.

Severity: security rates it minor, like the original FU-23. I raise it to major for three reasons.
1. It defeats the rework's own condition ('an RS-39 test shows no id is reused') on the databases the rebuild exists for.
2. It becomes irreversible as soon as 006 is applied to a persistent database: NFR1 refuses an edit, and a 007 cannot reclaim ids already reissued.
3. The rework limit is used, so after approval the only route is a fifth rework from the user, whereas now it is a reset of this task.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer, after the orchestrator resets rework-4. Resolved when all of the following hold:
- 006, before it drops the staging tables, creates any missing sqlite_sequence row and raises each rebuilt table's sequence to the maximum of its surviving ids and every id still named. For rescue_requests that means audit request entity ids and the staged model_spend.request_id; for images, audit image entity ids; for plan_versions, audit plan_version entity ids and plan.create detail planVersionId; for planning_runs, plan.create detail runId. The statements in rework-4-security-1.md are acceptable.
- The comment at L20 and safety-argument point 6 are corrected.
- A new test (named RS-39) deletes the highest request, image, run and plan version on 005 before migrating, and asserts that none of those ids is handed out afterwards and that no earlier audit row names the new rows. It must be recorded failing on the submitted 006 and passing on the fixed one.
- The existing migrate-006 assertions are kept, with the sequence expectation updated to the new high-water mark.
- The green set, npm test and the browser suite pass.

findings.title: Migration 006's run time grows quadratically with the number of plan versions: about 9 s at 5000 request trees, holding the write lock
findings.detail:
Measured on scratch file databases, with 2 plan versions per tree and every 5th tree also holding a reservation and a supplier order:
- 1000 trees: 0.27-0.35 s.
- 2000 trees: 1.1 s.
- 4000 trees: 5.3 s.
- 5000 trees: 8.7 s.
(ev:ev-mv3tpe9a-016d484a; ev:ev-mv3tp49m-017879bb P3)

Nearly all of the time is in DROP TABLE plan_versions and INSERT INTO plan_versions. That fits the deferred-FK child scans over columns that have no index: plan_versions.superseded_by, reservations.plan_version_id and supplier_orders.plan_version_id.

The submission describes this cost as linear; it is not. Beyond about 4000 trees, a second process starting at the same time would hit its 5 s busy timeout. This is irrelevant at the demo's scale.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer in the same reset (optional), else the orchestrator. Resolved when either of these holds:
- 006 adds temporary indexes on plan_versions(superseded_by), reservations(plan_version_id) and supplier_orders(plan_version_id) and drops them before the end, so the schema stays identical, and a re-measurement shows near-linear growth.
- The operator note and the verification report state the measured cost and that one process upgrades before traffic.

findings.title: SEC-R-1 has no committed HTTP-level test; HEAD answers 405 through the router
findings.detail: The limiter unit test uses a real lock-holder process, and the hook test uses a mock. Both are mutant-tested. My P1 probe covers the HTTP path: GET 200 in 54 ms, one busy_open line, POST 503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After 1. HEAD never reaches the hook, because the router answers 405 first; the security reviewer confirms this.

findings.title: Pre-existing: a state-changing call waiting for a lock held by another process stalls the whole process for RS_DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS

The read fail-open therefore helps only while no write of the same process waits. SEC-RW4-I4 is the same class, for the session touch.

Resolved when the phase E review confirms that reconciler and saga transactions are short (no await inside db.tx) and the verification report lists the residual; or a later rework shortens the write wait for request handlers.

findings.detail: From the security draft. 40 concurrent writes plus 120 reads by one user were all counted, with no busy_open line, because the app uses a single synchronous connection. While the lock was held, reads throttled the process to about 18 per second. Accepted by design.

findings.detail: From the security draft. A GET took 1057 ms under a held lock with a 1000 ms busy timeout (src/auth/sessions.js, the touch UPDATE). This is the same class as TR-R4-3.

findings.detail: Confirmed on a 005 database filled through the app: a model_spend row naming a reused id is unchanged after 006. This cannot be repaired from the data, and the submission discloses it.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
Condition met.
- take() fails open only for GET and HEAD and only on a busy error, uncounted, with one rate_limit.busy_open line that carries the request id only.
- Reads wait at most 50 ms, and the timeout is restored.
- State-changing methods, and a call with no method, fail closed with 503 DB_BUSY.
- The hook passes req.method, which cannot be spoofed: there is no override header or parameter, as the security reviewer confirmed.
- Through createApp, a signed-in GET answers 200 under a held lock and a POST answers 503 (P1).

The spec says 'the server log shows exactly one GET /api/paypal/return with the session's user id'. The helper asserts the user through the audit event written under the SAME request id (action payment.return / payment.cancel, actor_user_id = the journey's user, role customer, outcome ok), and asserts the log line's userId equals the user whenever the line carries one, so the check tightens by itself once app.js copies ctx.user into logState after the handler (a three-line fix in a `finally`). journey-happy prints '# GET /api/paypal/return log line userId: absent ...' each run. Route to the backend-engineer who owns src/app.js.

They encode the spec's guesses and will fail loudly where the Sandbox differs (A13 approvable statuses after a buyer cancel, invoice id rs-so-<id>-a1, final_capture refusing a second capture with a new request id, what verify-webhook-signature answers to a forged request, void of authorizations by the void rule). RS-23 needs a genuine signed delivery (RS_LIVE_PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_SAMPLE, replayed within 15 minutes) and RS-31(b) needs a person and RS_LIVE_PAYPAL_HEADED=1; both report SKIPPED otherwise. RS-32(b) covers the void of the superseded authorizations only, not the approval of the replacement plan (phase F). OQ-D5, LIVE-P1/P2 stay open until the user runs them.

data.title: test:live-paypal keeps the spec's node --test line
data.decision: The npm script stays the spec's form, pinned by test/unit/config/node-version.test.js; each live file refuses with exit 2 on its own, while the script as a whole exits 1 because node --test reports a failed child as 1. test/live/paypal/run-live-paypal.js remains an optional launcher with a single clean exit 2; the README (g2) documents both.
data.rationale: Changing the script line requires changing an approved phase B test together with it; the refusal itself is proven per file. Reversible.

lessonDecisions.note: This rework changes a request-logging line in src/app.js and one API test; it builds no hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record or root, so the lesson's applies-when conditions do not hold.

handoff.objective: Rework of e4 for one defect found by e6 (ho-mv3uq93d-0114f12e, refusal 2): the http.request log line of the public routes GET /api/paypal/return and /cancel carried no userId, because src/app.js copied ctx.user into the log state before the handler ran and these routes identify the session inside the handler. RS-31(a) needs the session's user id in the server log.
handoff.context: The original e4 handoff is ho-mv3tpmcv-01dc0d69 (saga, reconciler, execute route, main.js wiring) and stands unchanged. This claim changes src/app.js (log state copied again in the handler's finally block, only when it was not set before: userId and role of the identified user, nothing else; an anonymous call still logs neither) and adds one test to test/api/execute.test.js. rework-4 files (src/db, test/unit/db, src/auth/general-limit.js) and public/** were not touched.
handoff.expectedOutput: The request log line of GET /api/paypal/return and /cancel carries userId (and role) of the session user.
acceptanceCriteria: an authenticated GET /api/paypal/return and /cancel log line carries userId; an anonymous one carries neither userId nor role; no other identifier is added
failing-first test recorded red, then green
task verification, npm test (twice) and npm run test:browser run and cited honestly
handoff.completedWork: Everything of the first completion (ho-mv3tpmcv-01dc0d69: src/services/saga.js, src/services/reconciler.js, execute route in src/routes/plans.js, saga wiring in src/app.js, reconciler and real void port in src/main.js incl. the first tick after the startup retention pass, the five API test files) is unchanged and still passes. New in this claim: (1) src/app.js: in the handler's finally block, `if (ctx.user && logState.userId === undefined)` copies ctx.user.id and ctx.user.role into the log state, so a public route that calls ctx.auth.identify inside the handler is logged with the session user; the copy before the handler for policy routes is unchanged. (2) test/api/execute.test.js: new test 'RS-31(a): http.request for GET /api/paypal/return and /cancel carries the identified userId (and role); an anonymous call carries neither' (asserts userId equals the session user id, role customer, no other *id key besides requestId, and no userId/role key for the anonymous call). Recorded RED first: ev:ev-mv3uru6g-012c91d5 (1 test, 1 fail, 'the session user of the return is in the server log: undefined !== 6'), then GREEN after the fix: ev:ev-mv3us3wi-01051c67 (1 test, 1 pass). The test was written before the fix, so it is failing-first, not mutation-proven after the fact. Task verification after the fix: ev:ev-mv3uslbn-014d622e (71 tests, 71 pass, 0 fail). npm test run 1 ev:ev-mv3uv5wy-01d75149 PASSED (2087 tests, 2079 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped); run 2 ev:ev-mv3uxq3y-01cc943c PASSED (same counts). test:browser FAILED twice (ev:ev-mv3uzcl3-01c59200 and rerun ev:ev-mv3v19sz-014d5d49: 10 tests, 8 pass, 2 fail), see remainingIssues.
remainingIssues: npm run test:browser is RED by the two viewport cases of test/browser/journey-happy.test.js (e6's test; ev:ev-mv3uzcl3-01c59200 and ev:ev-mv3v19sz-014d5d49): after the first approval round trip it waits 30 s for [data-testid="paypal-returned"] and times out. This is not caused by the log change: with the app.js fix disabled the same two cases fail the same way (checked by a temporary edit, restored, grep-verified). Cause as far as I can tell: returnNoticeModel in public/js/views/request-detail.js (e5, being reset by the frontend-engineer) shows the 'returned' notice only while the order's payment status is one of the waiting statuses, but with the fake provider the return handler authorizes at once (status authorized), so the notice is never rendered. Either e5 shows the notice for the returned outcome or journey-happy must not wait for it. Because the failure comes before the point where the test prints the log line's userId, I could not read that output line; the unit test above proves the log line.
Everything in remainingIssues of ho-mv3tpmcv-01dc0d69 still applies, except that the contracts.test.js NFR6 row is no longer red in the full suite (npm test is green in both runs here).

review.summary:
Technical re-review of rework-4, iteration 2 (sub-mv3ussgo-0158904e, responding to rev-mv3ua9lc-01c4624b). Only two files changed since iteration 1: 006_autoincrement_ids.sql (the sequence floor, and the extractions/requirements rebuild) and migrate-006.test.js. All ten artifacts match the submission's sha256 (ev:ev-mv3uuxsy-01e2b908). Coverage across all three handoffs: 9 declared, 9 changed, 9 submitted, 0 undeclared (ev:ev-mv3v5xoc-01f38485). The security draft rework-4-security-2.md (FINAL: SEC-RW4-1 resolved; no new blocking, major or minor finding; new info SEC-RW4-I6) is folded in.

SEC-RW4-1 is resolved, verified by me.
- **Code:** before the staging tables are dropped, 006 creates any missing sqlite_sequence row and raises each sequence to the highest id still named. The sources are: audit entity ids (request, image, plan_version), the plan.create details planVersionId and runId, the extraction.run detail extractionId, and the staged model_spend.request_id. Each detail read is guarded by json_valid. I checked against the code that the app writes exactly these keys: extraction.js L509-L510, plans.js L259-L263.
- **The header comment and safety point 6 are corrected.**
- **The new RS-39 test** deletes X's ids on 005, before the upgrade. It fails on the previous 006 (engineer ev:ev-mv3udofz-01b7eb42; my P1 with 12 of 21 failing).
- **My re-check on the current 006 (ev:ev-mv3v55rb-01a9eca2):**
  - S1, my iteration-1 scenario: Y now gets 3/12/102/31/8 instead of 2/11/101/30/7, and none of X's audit rows sits on Y's ids.
  - S2: with every table empty at the upgrade, audit-named ids are still not reissued.
  - S3: the upgraded schema equals a fresh one, the triggers fire, and the foreign keys of extractions and requirements are intact.
  - My unchanged iteration-1 script now fails its 'reproduces' expectation, as intended: ev:ev-mv3v562s-0146e998 (reproduction, not cited as passing).
- **Falsification (ev:ev-mv3v5pr0-01e44852):** the control is green, 42/42. All 12 mutants are killed:
  - each of the 7 floor sources removed, one at a time;
  - the json_valid guard removed;
  - extractions not restored;
  - requirements without AUTOINCREMENT;
  - the extractions_request index dropped.
  Removing the defensive 'create missing sequence rows' INSERT is an equivalent mutant on SQLite 3.50.4: an INSERT ... SELECT into an AUTOINCREMENT table creates its row even when it copies nothing. Keeping the INSERT is right.

data.decision: Accepted for version one: when a webhook moves an operation into captured on a superseded or cancelled plan, the reconciler's backstop queues the refund on its next tick (RS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS) instead of the webhook route running the compensation hook inline.
data.rationale: No phase F or G task owns src/services/webhooks.js and the rework limit is used; the backstop is tested by e4 and the delay is bounded by the tick interval; listed in the verification report.

data.title: Four security info items accepted as residuals
data.decision: SEC-R-2 (a cross-site page can spend a signed-in victim's general budget only through many permitted popups), SEC-R-3 (sign-out is counted by the general limit), SEC-RW4-I2 (an extract racing a hard delete answers 500 instead of 404, before any spend) and SEC-RW4-I4 (a session touch on GET waits the full busy timeout) are accepted as residuals for version one and listed in the verification report with their reviewers' suggested fixes.
data.rationale: All four are info severity; none discloses data, moves money or bypasses authorization; no remaining task owns src/auth/** or the extraction service, and the rework limit set by the user (4) is used.

criteria.description: Payment adapters: DB-backed fake with faults and replay model, fake approval listener with its own CSP, Sandbox REST v2 adapter (stub-verified), merchant mapping
criteria.notes:
The e1 plan command passes 487/480/7 skipped by design.

What I checked in the code:
- The Sandbox adapter sends paypal-request-id = requestId on every call that carries one (sandbox.js L169), and checkArguments refuses a mutating call without a well-formed requestId before anything is sent (provider.js L76). One AbortSignal covers OAuth and the call.
- The fake runs each call in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE: fault, replay by (merchant_key, request_id), effect, then a fake_paypal_calls row.

What my runs show:
- Mutant M18 (listener CSP form-action without the app origin) is killed by the browser journey (2/2 red).
- The TR-R4-3 probe counted 2019 entries into the fake and Sandbox provider methods across the suites, none inside a transaction.

The fake and stub interpretations (deltas 18, 19, 20) are acceptable. The adapter remains unverified against real PayPal (LIVE-P1, LIVE-P2).

criteria.description: Provider call protocol and payment flow: paypal/create, return and cancel handlers, abandon, void rule with the resolution hook, order presentation and receipt
criteria.notes:
The e2 plan command passes 92/92.

The protocol matches spec section 2-4:
- Start is its own transaction with CAS status = 'intent' AND started_at IS NULL, and status = 'unknown' AND send_token IS NULL only for a caller that resolved the call (L139-L147).
- Send happens outside any transaction under a deadline of the timeout + 1 s (L370).
- Record is a CAS on id, send_token and status 'intent', with the mapped transition and an optional fence in the same transaction. Zero rows log provider.result_fenced.
- Every sender passes requestId = call.operation_key (L318-L326). The capture sender in saga.js does the same.

Mutants killed:
- M1: create amount from the operation row (2 RS-19 tests red);
- M5: start CAS without started_at (the protocol unit test red);
- M11: in-flight authorize voided locally;
- M12: no provider void queued (20 red);
- M13: the resolution hook removed from the authorize record.

The return handler's steps 1-6 match the spec. A foreign token is 404 before any provider call.

SEC-E-2 (TR-E-2, minor) concerns the return route's provider reads and rides an e2 reset with TR-E-1. Its acceptance criteria are otherwise met.

findings.title: (= SEC-E-1) A late, validly signed PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED moves capture_pending and unknown(prev authorized|capture_pending) back to authorized: a pending purchase is compensated, and an unknown capture is re-sent without a read
findings.detail:
Where:
- src/services/webhooks.js L54 maps 'PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED' to target 'authorized' with no `from` list.
- L261-L264 then admit every edge into authorized that the payment table allows. That includes capture_pending -> authorized (an edge that exists for CAPTURE.DENIED) and unknown -> authorized when prev_status is authorized or capture_pending (effective === target, or canTransition(capture_pending, authorized)).
- The spec maps this event 'pending -> authorized' (spec Webhooks, events list).
- e3's mapping table (test/api/webhooks.test.js L521-L527) has rows for authorization_pending, approved, unknown(prev approved), authorized, voided, created and unknown(prev refund_pending). It has none for capture_pending or unknown(prev authorized), so no test notices.

My reproduction (ev:ev-mv3wp57z-01f9ce7d, which passes when the defect is observed):
- P1: fault capture_pending on A, then execute. A is capture_pending. A signed late AUTHORIZATION.CREATED is answered 200 applied, and A becomes authorized. Over the next ticks the plan is taken over and compensated (non_executable CAPTURE_FAILED): A's void is refused because a capture is pending, resolveRejectedVoid puts A back in capture_pending, and B is voided. When the provider completes A's capture, A is captured and then refunded: the buyer is charged and refunded, and the purchase is lost.
- P2: fault lost_response:capture on A, so A is unknown(prev authorized) with the capture applied. The late event moves A to authorized, while the capture call stays unknown. With get_authorization and get_order failing (http 500), the next tick takes the plan over and the saga re-sends capture:1 with no successful read. Only the fake's PayPal-Request-Id replay prevents a second capture (capture:A:replayed).
- Security reproduced both (W-ORDER S2, S3; ev:ev-mv3w48uy-0190adfa, a reproduction run).

Money was neither lost nor doubled in any run. Layer 3 of 'why no double capture' (read before any re-send, spec Payment saga step 6) is bypassed, leaving layers 4-5, which are LIVE-DEPENDENT for the Sandbox (request-id retention, final_capture). PayPal does deliver events late and out of order: it retries for days, and this route answers 503 whenever verification is unreachable.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer, through an e3 reset inside this phase (webhooks.js and webhooks.test.js are e3's).

Resolved when all of these hold:
1. PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED gets from: ['approved', 'authorization_pending']. 'approved' stays because the event can beat the return handler's own answer. The existing effective = prev_status rule keeps unknown(prev approved | authorization_pending) resolving.
2. capture_pending, unknown(prev authorized), unknown(prev capture_pending) and every other origin are answered 200 flagged TRANSITION_NOT_ALLOWED, with no column change and no audit.
3. The e3 mapping table gains those three rows, named after this finding.
4. My probe tr-probe-webhook-order.test.js and security's W-ORDER are re-run unchanged, and their P1/P2 and S2/S3 'OBSERVED'/REPRO assertions now fail. S1 and S4 still pass.
5. The e3 plan command, npm test and npm run test:browser are green.

The defence in depth for saga.js is TR-E-4 (f2).

findings.title: (= SEC-E-2) GET /api/paypal/return is public, so the 300/min user limit does not apply: every hit on an unapproved order is one provider getOrder with the merchant's credentials
findings.detail:
src/routes/paypal.js registers return with policy public. The general limiter is not applied to public routes. payments.js L200 calls getOrder on every hit while the operation is created.

Security's reproduction (ev:ev-mv3wkmdf-014def88): 400 hits within one minute gave 400 getOrder calls and no 429, while 400 paypal/create calls are cut at 300.

Impact: availability, not money or data. In single-credential mode one account can spend the shared PayPal app's rate budget, and other buyers then see retryable/503.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer, through an e2 reset dispatched with TR-E-1 (routes/paypal.js and services/payments.js are e2's).

Resolved when a test shows the return route bounded per identified user, with the anonymous redirect, the 404 for a foreign token, the RS-20 three-hit and the crash-hook tests unchanged. Either:

findings.title: Mutant M6 survives: the F-TR-7 pause guard inside captureLoop (saga.js L531) is untested; the saga also re-sends an unknown capture relying on the reconciler's earlier read (SEC-E-1 recommendation 5)
findings.detail:
From my first mutant run (ev:ev-mv3wo4q9-014c6847, which fails by design because my driver fails on any survivor): replacing the condition at saga.js L531 with false leaves the e4 suite 71/71 green.

The rule is pinned elsewhere:
- the takeover exclusion: M7 is killed (ev:ev-mv3xewar-0170b19e);
- the pause after a PENDING or unknown answer (L566).

So L531 is defence in depth that matters only when an operation changes between the takeover and the run, for example through a webhook or a second process.

Related: captureLoop treats an authorized operation with an unknown, token-less capture call as resendable (L552, L559) without its own read. Spec step 6 says the new holder reads before any send. Today that is safe only because step 2 of the same tick read first, and TR-E-1 is the path that breaks it.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: f2-compensation-takeover-admin (owns saga.js), by follow-up.
- (a) Before re-sending an unknown capture call in captureLoop, read the authorization under the lease, as spec step 6 says.
- (b) Add a test where an operation becomes capture_pending or unknown after the takeover and before the resumed run; it must pause and send nothing. M6 must then be killed.
This is not a condition of this gate.

findings.title: Mutant M2 survives: no test pins the capture (or refund) amount to supplier_orders.total_cents when payment_operations.amount_cents disagrees
findings.detail:
Taking the capture amount from payment_operations.amount_cents instead of supplier_orders.total_cents leaves 78/78 green (ev:ev-mv3wo4q9-014c6847). M2b (+1 cent) is killed (31 red).

The mutant is equivalent in practice. amount_cents is written once, at reservation, equal to the order total (reservations.js L177), and is never updated. total_cents is never updated either (security AMT-3). Refunds use amount_cents (calls.js L326).

The RS-19 test pins only create_order against a disagreeing row (amount-tampering.test.js L106).
findings.recommendation: Optional, for f2 (capture-compensation.test.js): assert the capture and refund request amounts against supplier_orders.total_cents with a disagreeing operation row, or document that the two columns are equal by construction. The verification report lists it with delta 24 (TR-E-6).

lessonDecisions.note: The lesson applies to a hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record or root in a repository with several records; this rework adds a per-user rate limit to two routes and designs no hook, guard or root discovery, so its 'Applies when' list does not hold.

handoff.objective: Fix SEC-E-2 / TR-E-2 (phase E review): the public GET /api/paypal/return and /cancel routes were not covered by the per-user general limit, and every return hit on an unapproved order cost one provider getOrder (400 hits, 400 calls).
handoff.context: Rework of e2 after rev-mv3xhtuz-017cfbef (phase-e-1.json TR-E-2, phase-e-security-1.md SEC-E-2, repro ev:ev-mv3wkmdf-014def88). The access hook does not run for public routes and src/auth/general-limit.js is not an e2 file, so the count is done in e2's own files with the existing rate_events machinery, the same way planning counts (plan:u:<id>). No provider was contacted; RS_LIVE_MODEL and RS_LIVE_PAYPAL were never set.
handoff.expectedOutput: Return and cancel hits of an identified customer are counted per user before any lookup or provider call and answered 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After beyond the limit; anonymous hits keep their redirect.
acceptanceCriteria: after ctx.auth.identify (and the customer role check) the user's return and cancel hits are counted against a per-user limit in rate_events
the limit answers 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After before any provider call; anonymous hits stay on the 303 sign-in path
failing-first test: N+1 hits by one user give exactly N provider calls and a 429; another user is unaffected
handoff.completedWork: src/services/payments.js: takeReturnSlot(ctx, userId), RETURN_LIMIT = 30. One BEGIN IMMEDIATE deletes expired rows, counts and inserts (kind 'general', key pp:u:<userId>, so it never mixes with u:<id> or plan:u:<id>); window = config.generalRateWindowSec (60 s default), limit = min(30, config.generalRateLimit); a refused hit is not recorded; refusal is AppError 429 RATE_LIMITED {limit:'general'} with Retry-After, the same shape as the other limits. Why 30/min: a buyer makes about two hits per supplier approval (return plus a refresh), at most five suppliers, so real use stays far below 30, and the worst case per account is now 30 provider reads a minute instead of unbounded; the general limit's 300 would still allow 300 reads. src/routes/paypal.js: the shared buyer route calls takeReturnSlot right after the anonymous redirect and the customer role check and before the token lookup, so return and cancel share one count and a foreign-token hit counts against the caller. Anonymous hits are not counted (no provider call). Red first: ev:ev-mv3xmnj7-016333c5 (the new SEC-E-2 test failed on the unfixed tree: the 31st hit was not limited); green after the fix. The test (paypal-return-idempotent.test.js) asserts: 30 hits give 30 provider getOrder calls and 303, hit 31 is 429 RATE_LIMITED details {limit:'general'} Retry-After 60 with still 30 provider calls, a cancel is also 429 and leaves buyer_cancelled_at unchanged, the refused hit is not recorded (30 rows), another buyer gets 404 (not 429) and an anonymous caller gets the 303 sign-in redirect, and after 61 s the next hit is 303 again. Counts: plan verification 93 tests, 93 pass (was 92 plus the new test); npm test 2088 tests, 2080 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped (skips as in the review); test:browser 10/10.
remainingIssues: TR-E-1 / SEC-E-1 (webhooks.js) is e3's and not part of this reset.
paypal/create remains limited only by the general 300/min per-user limit (state-idempotent: only the 'Try approval again' path makes a getOrder); not part of SEC-E-2.
The limit constant (30 per general window) is not an environment variable; it is capped by RS_GENERAL_RATE_LIMIT and follows RS_GENERAL_RATE_WINDOW_SEC.

data.title: A webhook never resolves an unknown operation
data.decision: PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED and every other webhook event leave an operation in unknown untouched (stored flagged); only the reconciler resolves unknown operations, by reading the provider first (contract delta 27).
data.rationale: The phase E review (TR-E-1) showed a webhook resolving unknown could re-send a capture without a successful read; the reconciler's read-first path is the single place that resolves an uncertain outcome. Costs at most one reconciler tick of delay.

data.title: Correction of dec-mv3yeak6-01af9b6d: which webhooks resolve unknown operations
data.decision: Supersedes dec-mv3yeak6-01af9b6d, whose wording overstated the rule. PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.CREATED never resolves an operation in unknown (stored flagged; the reconciler resolves it by reading first). VOIDED, CAPTURE.COMPLETED, CAPTURE.PENDING, CAPTURE.DENIED and CAPTURE.REFUNDED may move an unknown operation only forward to the state the provider reports, and only from the previous states listed in their fromUnknown lists (contract delta 27 as the submission states it).
data.rationale: The phase E security review iteration 2 (SEC-E2-1) showed the earlier decision text claimed a property the code does not have; the code and the e3 mapping table are correct and every such move is forward to what the provider reports. The orchestrator wrote the overstated wording.

Every event now has an explicit origin list, checked before the state table, which stays as a second gate (L266-L273). I checked the seven lists against the spec and states.js:
- CREATED: approved and authorization_pending only, never from unknown. This is the spec's 'pending -> authorized'; approved is the same moment before the return handler records it.
- VOIDED: from authorized and unknown(authorized).
- COMPLETED: from authorized, capture_pending and the same two as unknown.
- PENDING: from authorized and unknown(authorized).
- DENIED: from capture_pending and unknown(capture_pending).
- REFUNDED: from refund_pending and unknown(refund_pending).
- ORDER.APPROVED: informational.
Every listed edge exists in states.js. No list admits a terminal state or a backwards money move, except DENIED capture_pending -> authorized, which is correct because a denied capture moved no money.

textContent only; contract fixtures for the new states; recovery.test.js checks the pure view-model against them
