A next-step sentence missing from the server falls back to the brief's sentence by code (texts.js). APPROVE: the Approve plan button now also shows when the next step is REVIEW_NEW_PLAN and the current plan is proposed (before, after a price change or refusal there was no way to approve the new version). IF SOMETHING FAILS: compensationOf now carries kind (void|refund) and says void queued, cancelled before authorization (voidedLocally), refund queued (captured with cancelRequested), declined, void failed / refund failed with 'contact the organiser'; a summary line 'Voids: n outstanding, n done. Refunds: n outstanding, n done.' (testid compensation-summary); the supplier's refusal reason is shown as text with dir=auto. CONTRACT ASSUMPTION F1-b: while a re-plan is queued the view is status replanning, rule 4a, nextStep WAIT with text 'Finding a new plan with current stock…'; after five failed drains nextStep.code REPLAN 'Re-plan with current stock'. currentPlanId may be null while only superseded versions exist, and orders is [].

CONTRACT ASSUMPTION F1-c: an expired reservation reads reservation.status 'expired' (or message exactly 'Reservation expired — no money was taken; re-plan with current stock'), nextStep REPLAN. The Re-plan button calls POST /api/requests/:id/plan and expects 201 {planningRun, plan|null}; a 409 PLAN_IN_PROGRESS is shown as an error.

CONTRACT ASSUMPTION F1-d: a supplier refusal gives the refused Order refusalReason (text, up to 300 chars) and presentation 'refused'; while its voids are outstanding the older orders are in cancellingOrders with payment.cancelRequested true; an unsent void queued under cancelRequested shows as 'Void queued'. A real abandon gives presentation 'cancelled' and fulfilment 'cancelled' (not cancelled_payment_incomplete).

CONTRACT ASSUMPTION F2-a: Payment.cancelRequested, voidedLocally and voidFailed are exposed in RequestView.orders and cancellingOrders for every state (the text 'Cancelled before authorization' needs voidedLocally; 'contact the organiser' for a failed void needs voidFailed).

CONTRACT ASSUMPTION F2-b: after an admin refund_order the payment goes captured -> refund_requested/refund_pending -> refunded, the order presentation becomes 'refunded' once refunded, and rescueStatus follows rows 3, 5a and 7 with the exact messages 'Order from <supplier> was refunded by the organiser' and 'All payments were refunded by the organiser'. A captured payment with cancelRequested true is read as 'Refund queued'.

CONTRACT ASSUMPTION F2-c: POST /api/admin/faults answers {applied: {kind, ...}, superseded?: Id[]}; supplier_refusal applied carries supplierOrderIds (as src/services/admin.js does today; the spec only says '...ids'); refund_order applied carries supplierOrderId. POST /api/admin/reset with force answers {reset, archivedOperations, stranded?: {id, status, providerAuthorizationId?, providerCaptureId?}[]}; the UI shows the optional provider ids when present (the code today sends id and status only).

CONTRACT ASSUMPTION (return redirect): the return handler redirects to /#/requests/<id>?paypal=not_approved|check_failed&order=<soId> (src/services/payments.js redirectTo); the notice reads the order from the query.

For f4: stable data-testid hooks added: contact-organiser, compensation-summary (on compensation: data-state and data-kind), failure-<code>[-earlier]-refusal, success-plan, success-replan, paypal-not-confirmed, reset-stranded, input-refusalReason (the fault form's reason; input-reason is now the reset form's only), next-step-action (header button: Re-plan / Review the new plan), replan (the expired notice's button), approve-plan after REVIEW_NEW_PLAN. Admin fault rows carry the hidden attribute when not part of the chosen kind, so Playwright fill on a hidden control waits: choose the kind first.
The supplier Refuse button has no confirm dialog on purpose (a native confirm is auto-dismissed by Playwright and would make the click a no-op); the explicit reason form is the safeguard.
FU-40 UX is addressed for the case executed + live order still 'confirmed'; the journey-happy test still reloads before the receipt and was not edited (not my file).
Not done: no browser journey for the recovery states (f4 owns the browser tests); the 360 px layout was checked ad hoc only.

data.title: Re-plan after a supersession is drained by the reconciler, not the request handler
data.decision: Accepted deviation from the spec's 'drain after commit': the customer sees replanning ('Finding a new plan with current stock…', polling) for up to one reconciler interval (default 15 s) before the new plan appears; the request handler does not run the planner inline.
data.rationale: f1 found the behaviour consistent with dec-mv3vui7s-014f6e7c (drain lives in reconciler.js); an inline drain would put synchronous planner CPU work on the request path and contradict c3's approved test that asserts replanning right after a change. Listed in the verification report.

acceptanceCriteria: Compensation (step 5) in one transaction under the fence: plan non_executable (CAPTURE_FAILED | AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED), reservation consumed -> reconciling, queued captures cancelled, authorized -> void, captured -> refund_requested + so:<id>:refund:1; refund results to refunded / refund_pending (polled) / refund_failed (escalation); release check -> released with restock rows only when nothing is outstanding

Takeover (step 6): epoch + 1 inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE only when lease_until <= now and no operation is capture_pending or unknown (F-TR-7); every open capture call resolved by reading before any send; re-send only with the same PayPal-Request-Id; late result writes fenced by epoch and send_token (saga.lease_lost logged)
F-TR-6: a rejected void whose read shows CAPTURED moves the operation to captured and queues the refund in the same transaction

Admin refund_order only for captured operations of executed plans; forced reset per SEC-11 (void authorized, bounded 30 s read-resolve pass, stranded list in response and audit); reset archives operations and provider calls, never deletes

RS-22 (incl. PENDING capture with lease_epoch constant across ticks), RS-37, RS-38 (every reserve, release, expire, consume and restock writes a ledger row; per-product ledger sums equal on_hand and reserved) tests named with their ids
FU-36, FU-41 (a, b), FU-42, FU-45 answered; FU-22 remainder checked
handoff.completedWork: CODE. (1) src/services/calls.js: FU-45, an authorization read back as EXPIRED after a rejected void is settled (operation voided, last_error_code AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, void_failed stays 0, no escalation; the reconciler's unknown-void path reaches it through the same function); FU-42, the refund sender reads supplier_orders.total_cents like the capture (the two columns are equal by construction; the tests now disagree on purpose). (2) src/services/saga.js: FU-41(a) readBeforeResend: before an `unknown` token-less capture is sent again the lease holder reads the authorization itself under the lease; CREATED -> send with the same key, anything else or a failed read -> hold (call stays unknown, lease paused, the reconciler resolves by reading; logs saga.resend_held / saga.resend_read_failed); an archived plan (every operation archived) is never resumed (runSaga and captureLoop answer 'archived') and releaseIfSettled ignores a reservation with no live operation. (3) src/services/reconciler.js: readResolvePass(env, {budgetMs}) exported for the forced reset (stale intents, resolve unknown by reading, poll pending; bounded in REAL time, stops between items); resolveUnknownCalls and pollPending take a shouldStop; the takeover query skips plans whose operations are all archived. (4) src/services/admin.js and src/routes/admin.js: resetDemo is async; a forced reset with money held first ends approved plans through the void rule, voids the remaining authorized operations through the void port (cancel_requested_at, reason DEMO_RESET), sends the voids, runs ONE read-resolve pass (budget 30 s, RESET_RESOLVE_BUDGET_MS), sends the voids that pass queued, then archives in the single transaction and lists what is not terminal in `stranded` (response and audit; the audit also carries authorized, resolved, polled, resolveTimedOut, closedReconciling); a reservation still `reconciling` is closed WITHOUT restock rows by any reset; refund_order queues through moveOperation/queueCall, commits its `denied` audit row, answers 404 for an archived operation and SENDS the refund after the commit (Sender table), a refund that cannot be sent stays queued for reconciler step 6; applyFault is async. src/services/void-rule.js needed no change. TESTS (56, all in my five files). capture-compensation (18): RS-22 compensation end to end, AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED variant, refund results table, compensation as ONE transaction (a trigger refuses the refund row; nothing half done; next holder completes), FU-42, PENDING capture and unknown capture with lease_epoch constant across five and three ticks, takeover boundary (one millisecond before / at lease_until), stalled sender fenced by send_token with reads only and no takeover, epoch fence of its own, lease needed at the capture start (step 2 and step 3), FU-41(a) x3, FU-41(b) x2 (kills the reviewers' M6), retryable resume. void-capture-race (7): F-TR-6 end to end (one capture, one void attempt, one refund), F-TR-6 atomicity, lost void answer + PENDING capture landed, FU-45 x2 + its limit (void_fail stays an escalation), FU-34 webhook capture refunded once on the next tick. admin-reset (11): SEC-11 void/stranded/bounded/read-resolve, RS-37 guard and archive, RS-38 reconciling reservation (forced and unforced) and archived executing plan. admin-refund-order (13): refund_order transitions, results (COMPLETED, PENDING polled, FAILED, 429, lost answer, timeout), refusals, race, access, FU-42. ledgers (7): RS-38 for reserve, release, expire, consume, restock, supplier stock changes and exactly-once restock under two reconcilers; FU-36 row format. DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED (red at the base source): SEC-11 was not implemented (no void, no pass, sync reset); a reset left a reconciling reservation open so the reconciler later restocked it on top of the restored stock (RS-38); an archived executing plan could be taken over and marked executed; refund_order was not sent after commit; its `denied` audit row was rolled back with the throw; FU-41(a); FU-45; FU-42. FU-36: the consume and restock helpers already wrote the ledger.js row format; ledgers.test.js pins both paths and the running balances, moving the helpers was not needed. FU-22: nothing is missing (sessions, login failures, idempotency keys, invalid/unverified webhook rows by the reconciler, rate events and images by retention.js, stale model spend by both through one CAS). I may not edit these files; they need an orchestrator rework by their owners. (1) test/api/lost-response.test.js (e4), test 'RS-25: nothing was applied (a timeout): the reconciler reads CREATED, restores authorized and the lease holder re-sends with the SAME PayPal-Request-Id': it expects the call trail ['get_authorization','capture','capture']; FU-41(a) puts the lease holder's own read in front of the re-send, so the trail is ['get_authorization','get_authorization','capture','capture'] (trail[2] is A's key so:<A>:capture:1, trail[3] is B's); update the deepEqual, the two trail indices and the message. (2) test/api/admin-basic.test.js (c3), test 'refund_order: only an operation captured under an executed plan; it becomes refund_requested with a queued refund call ...': it asserts the refund stays refund_requested and the call stays intent/started_at null, but the spec's Sender table (refund: the refund_order handler sends right after commit) is now implemented; the test fabricates the capture id 'FAKE-CAP-1', which the fake does not know, so the operation ends refund_failed. Keep the 404 / early-409 / second-call-409 parts and assert only that one call so:<id>:refund:1 exists after the 200; the sending behaviour is covered by admin-refund-order.test.js. The forced-reset test of admin-basic.test.js (c3) stays green because the voids of an approved plan go through the void port, which is a recorder there.

A forced reset needs the real void port to send voids for authorized operations of plans that are not `approved` (startApp wires it; createApp's default is a recorder that sends nothing); without it those operations are listed in `stranded`, as the spec says for a failed clean-up.

A plan that was `executing` when a forced reset archived its operations stays status `executing` (the plan machine allows executing -> non_executable only for CAPTURE_FAILED / AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED). It is fenced: never taken over, resumed or marked executed (tests), but plansByStatus in the admin metrics still counts it until a later reset or a state-machine decision.

The send_token fence of recordCall cannot be proved on its own: the UPDATE also requires status = 'intent', which rejects the same late results; the epoch fence and the lease checks are each mutant-proved. A DB error inside resolveRejectedVoid's transaction leaves the operation `authorized` with a failed void call and void_failed 0; only derivation row 2 (b) escalates it after RS_PENDING_ESCALATE_MIN (test shows nothing half done, not a retry).
refund_order now waits for the provider call (up to RS_PAYPAL_TIMEOUT_MS + 1 s) before it answers; the API client aborts at 15 s, the call journal stays consistent if it does.
With a read that keeps failing, the FU-41(a) hold path pauses the lease and the next tick takes the plan over again (epoch + 1 per tick) until the order read recovers; no send happens meanwhile.

Documented design deltas for the verification report: refunds read supplier_orders.total_cents (delta 24 changed source, same value by construction); a forced reset's audit event gained authorized, resolved, polled, resolveTimedOut and closedReconciling; a reset closes reconciling reservations without restock rows.

Supplier A has one bundle, so build one world per scenario. test/browser/helpers/recovery.js: RECOVERY_ENV (reconcile interval 300 ms, admin password) for startBrowserHarness({env}), adminClient, signInThroughUi, refuseThroughUi, orderIdOf, waitForText(testid, pattern), testIdsOf, planLinesShown, assertNoOverflow. The re-plan after a refusal or a supersession appears within one reconcile interval (dec-mv40tgfo-01d03e4f), so journeys must start their server with RS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS small. 'Collected' needs the supplier's handover AND the buyer's receipt (ready + receipt alone leaves the order 'ready'). Use a fresh startBrowserHarness per buying journey.

handoff.completedWork: TESTS (all new, none skipped on this Linux host; the multi-process suites carry a skip with a reason for non-Linux platforms). (1) test/integration/lease-takeover.test.js (2 tests): two real server processes on one SQLite file with RS_SAGA_LEASE_MS 1500, RS_PAYPAL_TIMEOUT_MS 500, RS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS 200. Process 1 executes the plan and freezes itself in supplier A's capture (admin fault, SIGSTOP); the test waits for the kernel state T in /proc before anything else, process 2 takes over (epoch 2, one audited saga.takeover) and completes the plan; then SIGCONT. Variant A: process 2 READS the applied capture (order A has exactly one capture call, replayed 0, pid of process 1; B's by process 2); after SIGCONT process 1 logs saga.lease_lost and sends no call. Variant B: process 2 reads CREATED, sends the capture again with the same request id (first non-replayed capture), and the frozen request of process 1 is answered as a REPLAY (replayed 1) after SIGCONT, its only call. Both: exactly one non-replayed capture per order with request id so:<id>:capture:1, one capture per order at the provider, no void or refund, one consume ledger row per reserved item, no error log. (2) test/integration/rs26-restart.test.js (2 tests): the freeze hook makes the kill deterministic (stopped state observed, snapshot of every money and stock row, then SIGKILL, then a new process on the same file). Round 1 kills with A's capture applied but unrecorded, round 2 (fault for supplier B) with A recorded and B applied but unrecorded. After the restart: epoch 2 and one takeover audited, plan executed, both operations captured, the new process READ the provider (no capture is replayed, exactly one capture call per order), every pre-kill row is present and append-only rows (ledger, audit, provider call log, captures) are byte-identical, reservation consumed once, nothing restocked. (3) test/integration/return-crash.test.js (3 tests): (a) crash_after_return_commit kills the process in the return handler (the connection is cut, exit signal SIGKILL), committed state checked (operation approved, authorize call intent, never started, zero authorize calls at the provider); the restarted process sends it exactly once (request id so:<id>:authorize:1, pid of the restarted process, operation authorized, one authorization, supplier B untouched, buyer view shows A authorized); (b) the stored reservation expiry is moved into the past while no process runs (the stand-in for a restart after the TTL; a short write from the test process), then: authorize call cancelled, operation voided_locally, ZERO authorize calls and no money call, plan non_executable RESERVATION_EXPIRED, reservation expired, the request leaves cancelling and reads cancelled with the exact expiry message; (c) a retryable http_429:authorize (armed by inserting the fault_flags row, because the admin route accepts only http_500) on two processes: the call is queued again (intent, not started, http 429, next_attempt_at = the 429 call + 5 s), the second send happens at or after next_attempt_at with the same request id, exactly one effective authorization, send_count 2. (4) test/api/contracts.test.js: a recovery table drives the real routes into 23 states (request view rows 2, 3, 4, 4a, 5a, 6, 7 and 12, the admin fault answers per kind and the two errors, the forced reset with stranded, the supplier refuse errors, the re-plan answer) in a world of its own each, and compares status, envelope, requestId and field types with test/fixtures/contracts/recovery/*.json, pinning the status, rule and next step of the views; a coverage test requires one row per fixture. Phase F adds no route, so no route row was needed. 81 tests pass (57 before). (5) test/browser/refusal.test.js (RS-17, 2 tests): signs up, plans, approves and reserves A + B ($84.00), supplier B confirms and the buyer approves B on the fake page (round-trip helper), supplier A refuses through the supplier UI in a second browser context, the buyer page updates by itself: exact message 'Supplier A refused the order: Out of lids. No money was taken.', next step 'Review the new plan', B's authorization voided, focus moves to 'Why this plan', plan lines B and E only, total matches the stored new plan, the new plan is approved and reserved; data checks and round-trip totals (1 approval); no console, CSP, page or request problems; no horizontal scroll. (6) test/browser/journey-replacement.test.js (RS-32(a), 2 tests): A confirms, buyer approves A, the admin stock_depletion fault for B (answer superseded = [old plan]) supersedes the old plan with one void and B's order cancelled, the page offers 'Review the new plan' with A + E at $95.00, approve, reserve, A and E confirm, two more approvals, execute, ready + handover by the suppliers, both receipts, the request reads 'Collected'; one capture per order under so:<id>:capture:1; round-trip totals 3 approvals, 0 cancels. HELPERS: test/helpers/saga-flow.js, test/helpers/recovery-flow.js, test/browser/helpers/recovery.js (see remaining issues for what g3 needs). BITE PROOF in scratch copies (the real tree was never mutated; each run recorded, all red unless stated): M1 saga re-sends an unknown capture without reading and the reconciler ignores the provider state: lease-takeover variant A red (order A gets 2 capture calls), ev:ev-mv41xci3-014ccf69; M1b the same plus the re-send under another request id (a second non-replayed capture): all four takeover/restart tests red, ev:ev-mv41zi15-015b8359; M3 takeover without incrementing lease_epoch: red, ev:ev-mv41znig-013106f7; M5 only the reconciler backstop that cancels a queued authorize disabled: SURVIVED (passed, ev:ev-mv42027q-01074419; the void rule cancels the call in the same transaction, so the backstop is redundancy, honestly reported); M5b void rule and backstop both leave the queued authorize alone: return-crash (b) red, ev:ev-mv4221p9-01d81f4b; M6 sender ignores next_attempt_at: (c) red, ev:ev-mv4207ii-01b07056; M8 nobody sends a queued authorize: (a) and (c) red, ev:ev-mv4245d2-011141cc; M7 order view renames refusalReason: 10 contract rows red, ev:ev-mv420ljh-012e3426; M9 re-plan does not exclude the refusing supplier: both refusal journeys red (A instead of E), ev:ev-mv424wf5-0141f67c; M10 stock_depletion supersedes nothing: both replacement journeys red, ev:ev-mv425a8b-017ed7a1. The mutation 'a second capture at the provider' cannot happen in the fake (it refuses AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_CAPTURED and replays the same request id), so the tests count capture CALLS (replayed or not) per order, which is what the mutants change. The 8 skipped are the existing provider-contract cases of the fake harness (no OAuth to fail or inspect, no busy fault): none is mine. EARLIER RED RUN, with its cause: the first run of the verbatim command, ev:ev-mv43j15k-01209f8b, FAILED on one test, test/api/uploads-retention.test.js 'RS-39: startApp removes an expired image at startup and another one on the next tick' (line 711: the image file still exists at the moment its row has disappeared, because the sweep deletes the row and then unlinks the file; this is the known race of decision dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152, carried to phase G as FU-33, owned by neither f4 nor rework-5). Per that decision it was re-run once and reported, not skipped; the re-run passed. The test and the product code were not touched. Before rework-5 the same command failed only on the two stale tests (ev:ev-mv427kx5-01596443, 2 failures), which rework-5 fixed.
remainingIssues: The RS-39 uploads-retention timer race (test/api/uploads-retention.test.js line 711, dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152, FU-33) failed once in the first full run on this tree and passed on the single re-run. The one-line fix (wait for the file as well as the row) is carried to phase G; it can fail again until then.

The fixture defect found by the contract rows (recovery/plan-replan-feasible.json lacked `labels`) was fixed by f3 (ho-mv42ei0w-019037ae) and the tolerance in contracts.test.js was removed (ev:ev-mv43ohq1-01bc3f1c).

SURVIVING MUTANT M5: the reconciler backstop that cancels a queued authorize of a cancelled operation is redundant with the void rule (which cancels the call in the same transaction as the expiry); no test can distinguish them. Not a gap in the tests of the spec's behaviour.

return-crash (b) moves reservations.expires_at into the past with a short write from the test process while every server process is dead, because the real clock cannot be injected into a spawned server and RS_RESERVATION_TTL_MIN has a minimum of one minute. return-crash (c) arms http_429:authorize by inserting the fault_flags row (the admin route accepts only http_500 for kind faults). Both write only the rows the product itself would write.
return-crash (c) waits the real 5 s back-off of the first retryable answer (calls.js BACKOFF_MS); it waits on the database state, with a 40 s bound.

In the browser journeys the 'If something fails' section is empty once the voids are done and the new plan exists (the server returns no orders of the closed plan then), so the supplier's reason is asserted in the status message and failure-message, and the void through the data. The per-order hooks failure-<code>[-earlier]-refusal and compensation-summary appear only while a void is outstanding; a journey that needs them must hold a void back (the no-op void port exists only in-process, contracts rows view-cancelling-voids and view-failed-needs-attention cover those shapes).

The 22.5 pass condition of the spec covers these three multi-process tests; only Node 22.22 is available here, so the run on 22.5 is the user's. The tests spawn through test/helpers/node-proc.js (via server-proc.js).

data.title: Serialize full-suite evidence runs across agents
data.decision: From now on every full-suite evidence run (npm test, npm run test:browser, and any verification command containing them) is wrapped as: flock /tmp/rescuestock-suite.lock <command>. Smaller targeted runs are not wrapped.
data.rationale: Two concurrent full suites on this 4-CPU machine produced two different timing failures in one hour: the RS-39 retention race (ev-mv43j15k-01209f8b) and a SEC-B-1 per-call planner limit at 186.9 ms against 100 ms (ev-mv43keu0-0102c57c), both green on re-run. Contention-induced failures cost a re-run each and blur real regressions. A lock keeps parallel agent work while making suite timing comparable. The SEC-B-1 per-call bound itself is routed to phase G g3 as FU-46 (consider the p95 the test already computes), not changed here.

findings.title: refund_order subtest asserts only `notEqual 'refund_requested'`, and a provider-rejected refund recorded as `refunded` now passes the whole suite
findings.detail:
**The assertion.** admin-basic.test.js L403 asserts that the operation status is not 'refund_requested'.
- In this fixture, the hand-made capture id FAKE-CAP-1 is unknown to the fake, so the refund send is `rejected`.
- calls.js L296 maps that rejection to `refund_pending -> refund_failed`. This follows spec protocol section 4 (`rejected` -> failed + mapped transition) and saga step 5 (FAILED -> `refund_failed`, an escalation).
- The engineer's before-log ev:ev-mv439gxz-01147594 and the test's own comment both show that the real value is `refund_failed`.

**This is the only test that reaches that mapping.**
- admin-refund-order.test.js L250 covers the FAILED status of a 200 answer (calls.js L290-L291), not a `rejected` answer.
- No test references REFUND_REJECTED.

**My mutant MB** changes L296 to `moveOperation(db, clock, op, 'refunded', {})`. It survives:
- admin-basic plus admin-refund-order, 31/31 (ev:ev-mv43wead-01813f03);
- the full suite, 2267/2259/0 fail (ev:ev-mv448n2l-0137d6ac).

**Impact.** That defect would record money as returned when PayPal refused the refund. It would feed:
- derivation row 5a ('All payments were refunded by the organiser');
- the release check, which restocks, instead of an escalation.

**Gap.** The previous assertion (`refund_requested`) could not see this either, because nothing was sent then. Now that the handler sends, this subtest is where the outcome is observed, and the rewrite chose a bound that accepts any value but one.

**The fix is proven.** Pinning `assert.equal(..., 'refund_failed')`:
- passes on the real source, 18/18 (ev:ev-mv43xat4-0135d8cc);
- kills MB, with actual 'refunded' and expected 'refund_failed' (ev:ev-mv43x67w-01efa863).
findings.recommendation:
Owner: test-engineer (rework-5 owns test/api/admin-basic.test.js). Resolved when all of the following hold:
1. L403 pins `assert.equal(<status>, 'refund_failed')`.
2. Optionally, last_error_code is also pinned as a REFUND_* code from the rejection (for example via `safeCode(issue, 'REFUND_REJECTED')`), so that a rejected refund is distinguishable.
3. The resubmission shows a recorded run in which the L296 -> 'refunded' mutant fails admin-basic, and admin-basic alone and npm test (under the suite lock) are green on the final tree.
4. No source file changes.

findings.title: admin-basic comment cites 'FU-42 / SEC-11' for 'one refund per captured order'; neither says that
findings.detail:
admin-basic.test.js L407 gives the wrong sources.
- FU-42 (followups.md L263) is about refund and capture amounts against supplier_orders.total_cents.
- SEC-11 (spec.md L50) is about forced reset and audit naming.

The exactly-one-send rule rests on three sources:
- spec Admin routes, refund_order (L399): only `captured` under `executed`, so a second call is 409;
- the Sender table refund row (L827): one send, right after commit;
- protocol section 1: the deterministic key `so:<id>:refund:1` with UNIQUE.

Only the traceability is wrong; the behaviour is unaffected. The delivery-lead disclosed this as observation 2.
findings.recommendation: Owner: test-engineer. Fix it in the same edit as TR-R5-1. Resolved when the L407 comment cites spec Admin routes > refund_order, the Sender table refund row and the protocol's deterministic key in place of FU-42 / SEC-11.

findings.title: The exact RS-25 trail pins 'B is sent without a read', while ARCH-26 (2) and saga step 6 literally say intent calls '(queued or started)' are resolved by reading after a takeover
findings.recommendation: No change required for this gate. Optional, owner product-architect via the orchestrator: when the spec is next revised, reword saga step 6 and ARCH-26 (2) to say that only started or unknown capture calls are read, because a queued call is provably unsent. Resolved by that wording or by an explicit decision that the current behaviour stands.

findings.title: Disclosure (c): the surviving engineer mutant's code is gone; its explanation checks out against calls.js, and replacement and independent mutants cover the behaviour
findings.detail:
The engineer's 'send twice via runCall on a reset call' mutant (ev:ev-mv43b7zh-015445ff) survived, and its source was overwritten.

The stated reason is consistent with the code:
- calls.js L312 makes a refund sendable only while the operation is `refund_requested` or `refund_pending`;
- L364 cancels a call the operation no longer needs, instead of sending it;
- so after `refund_failed` no second provider call can occur, and the mutant was equivalent at the provider.

The replacement direct double-send is killed (ev:ev-mv43bm23-01f616d9). L409 and L412 of the test pin the provider-side count independently of the route taken.

The lost source is a process gap, not a test defect.
findings.recommendation: No change required. Going forward, owner delivery-lead and test-engineer: keep each mutant's diff (for example, in the evidence label or as a patch file under the draft area) and do not reuse a scratch directory for a new mutant. Resolved by noting that rule in the next handoff.

data.title: RS-25: a queued capture call is not read after a takeover
data.decision: The current behaviour stands: after a lease takeover the new holder reads provider state before re-sending any call that may have been sent (send_count > 0, unknown), and does not read a call still queued (intent, send_count 0). The spec wording of ARCH-26 (2) and saga step 6 ('intent (queued or started)') is to be clarified to 'started' at the next documentation pass (g2), not changed in code.
data.rationale: TR-R5-3 (rev-mv44amic-012cf420): a queued call is provably unsent under the provider call protocol step 2 and the Sender table (send_count is incremented in the same commit as the send attempt), so a read adds a provider round trip and no safety. The trail approved before rework-5 already pinned this, and the rework-5 reviewer found no money-safety consequence.

data.title: Correction to dec-mv44nzj5-01fbc177 rationale wording
data.decision: dec-mv44nzj5-01fbc177 stands. Its rationale is corrected: send_count and started_at are set by startCall in its own transaction before the HTTP send (src/services/calls.js L140, L145, protocol step 2), not 'in the same commit as the send attempt'. A call with started_at NULL and send_count 0 has therefore never reached the network.
data.rationale: The orchestrator checked the code after recording and found its own description imprecise; the conclusion is unchanged because the commit precedes any send.

review.summary:
Technical review of phase:f-compensation, iteration 1 (sub-mv44juz3-01ac72c7; commit aab23e6, tree a9aba38c; 61 artifacts, all unchanged on disk; no code change since aab23e6). The security draft phase-f-security-1.md (FINAL, verdict APPROVE, SEC-F-1 minor, SEC-F-I1..I7 info) is folded in.

**What I checked.** I read the full src diff bf1a723..HEAD: saga.js, reconciler.js, calls.js, admin.js and routes/admin.js (+219/-39), and the f3 public diff, and checked them against the spec: provider call protocol 1-7, the payment saga steps 1-6, the reconciler, Admin routes and derivation row 2.

**Plan commands, re-run verbatim.**
- f1: 40/40 (ev:ev-mv44zcfv-01cfa3ef).
- f2: 56/56 (ev:ev-mv44ztri-017e5d46).
- f3: 205/205 (ev:ev-mv44zv7u-010f184d).
- f4 under the suite lock: the first run had one failure, the known FU-33 race (ev:ev-mv451ngy-01bf3721). The single re-run allowed by dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152 passed: npm test 2267 tests, 2259 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped; NFR5 p95 65.7 ms; browser 14/14, with RS-17 and RS-32(a) at 360 and 1280 (ev:ev-mv455hce-01858e59).

**Mutation.** I ran 9 mutants of my own on phase F logic, each in a fresh directory with its diff kept (ev:ev-mv45c3hv-0174ae15; sources ev:ev-mv45fn0w-015fc010). 7 are killed. Of the two survivors, MF6 is equivalent and MF4 is reachable only inside one reconciler interval (TR-F-5). MF3 is killed only by a hang (TR-F-2).

**Correctness.** RS-13, RS-15, RS-17, RS-22 (PENDING), RS-26, RS-32(a), RS-37, RS-38, F-TR-2 and F-TR-6 conform as tested, and so do FU-36, FU-38, FU-41, FU-42, FU-43 and FU-45. Security confirms money never moves twice or backward (P-MONEY, P-RESET, P-FENCE).

**Decision: changes requested on TR-F-1 (major), FU-49.** My reproduction probe (ev:ev-mv455seu-01b2f7c0) shows the following:
- once the reconciler's read has restored the operation to `authorized` and later reads fail, the plan is taken over every tick (epoch 2 -> 10 over 8 ticks) with two reads per tick and no send;
- after 20 minutes the buyer still reads 'Payments are being captured' / WAIT. Nothing escalates, whereas the same outage with the operation still `unknown` escalates at 15 minutes with the epoch at 1.

**Disagreement with security.** Security measured the same thing (SEC-F-I2, ev:ev-mv452q7k-0170c0b2) and rates it info, as consistent with F-TR-7 as written. I agree there is no fencing hole and no money risk. I rate it major because:
- protocol section 6 requires that an unknown older than RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN feeds row 2;
- this silent stuck state is new in phase F;
- the fix is small.

**Other findings.**
- TR-F-2 (minor): the SEC-11 bound test can only hang.
- TR-F-3 (minor): two LIVE-P1 labels and RISK-18's title overstate the live coverage.
- SEC-F-1 (minor, with my concurrence; my TR-F-4 is merged into it): the compensation path of a rejected refund is unpinned by f2.
- Info: TR-F-5, TR-F-6, TR-F-7 (FU-33 priority) and SEC-F-I1, I3, I4, I5, I6, I7.

findings.title: FU-49: the FU-41(a) hold path repeats the takeover every tick while the holder's read fails, and the stuck plan never escalates
findings.detail:
**The state.** After a capture timeout, reconciler step 2 reads CREATED and restores the operation to `authorized`. The capture call stays `unknown` (reconciler.js L195-L201). Step 5 takes the plan over, because no operation is `capture_pending` or `unknown`. If the holder's read then fails, readBeforeResend returns 'hold' and pauseLease sets lease_until = now (saga.js L585-L597). The next tick repeats all of it.

**My probe** (ev:ev-mv455seu-01b2f7c0, scratch copy of the final src plus one added test file; source in ev:ev-mv45fn0w-015fc010):
- the first read succeeds, then the fake's get_authorization fails (http_500, unlimited);
- over 8 ticks of 2.5 min: epochs 2,3,...,10, two get_authorization per tick, 0 capture sends, 9 saga.takeover and 9 saga.resend_read_failed logs;
- after 20 min the operation is `authorized`, the call `unknown`, the plan `executing`;
- the buyer's rescueStatus is `payment_authorized`, rule 10, WAIT, 'Payments are being captured.';
- when the fault is cleared, the plan completes with one capture per authorization.

**Security measured the same** (SEC-F-I2, ev:ev-mv452q7k-0170c0b2: +10 epochs and +10 takeover audit rows over 10 ticks, zero sends, 'derivation row 2 and metrics unresolved stay silent').

**Compare** the same outage when the first read also fails (lost-response.test.js L256, 'F-TR-7: while an operation is unknown the plan is not taken over ...'): the epoch stays 1, and the request is `failed_needs_attention` after RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN.

**Why this does not conform.**
- **Escalation.** Spec, provider call protocol section 6: 'A read that itself fails leaves the call unknown until the next tick. An unknown older than RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN feeds derivation row 2.' derive.js row 2 looks only at op.status `unknown` (and authorize calls of `approved` operations), so an `unknown` capture call under an `authorized` operation never escalates.
- **F-TR-7.** F-TR-7's intent ('the reconciler takes over a paused plan only when that operation is resolved'; 'lease_epoch does not grow while ... pending') is defeated: the operation counts as resolved for the takeover query but not for its own holder.
- **Durability.** The state is new in phase F. Before FU-41(a) the holder re-sent at once, and a failed send put the operation back into `unknown`.

**Money is safe**, and security's F2 shows no fencing hole. The defect is a silent stuck plan with takeover and read churn (5,760 epochs and audit rows a day per plan at 15 s) for as long as the outage lasts, while the buyer is told the payments are being captured.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: backend-engineer (f2 owns saga.js and reconciler.js; src/domain/derive.js has no phase F owner, so the orchestrator scopes a rework if that file is chosen).

Resolved when both of the following hold:

(a) **The stuck state escalates.** With the holder's read failing for longer than RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN, the request reads `failed_needs_attention` (row 2), with a test. Either option is acceptable:
- On a failed or held holder read, the operation goes back to `unknown` (prev_status `authorized`, the original unknown_since kept), so the existing F-TR-7 takeover exclusion and row 2 apply unchanged. This is my preferred fix: it also stops the epoch growth.
- Or derivation row 2 escalates on a capture call `unknown` for longer than RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN.

(b) **The epoch is settled.** Either the same test shows that lease_epoch no longer grows per tick in this state (security's suggestion, lease_until = now + back-off on a failed read, also serves), or an orchestrator decision accepts the per-tick takeover with its rationale and the verification report states it.

The FU-41(a) tests and lost-response stay green, the full suite passes under the lock, and my probe's expectations flip: the epoch stays bounded and the status escalates.

findings.detail:
**The mapping is covered suite-wide, but only on the admin path.** It is calls.js L295-L297 (`rejected` -> `refund_failed`).
- Mutant MB (-> 'refunded') passes all 56 f2 tests (security, ev:ev-mv45a1qw-01b3e8ca).
- It is killed only by rework-5's admin-basic refund_order subtest: security's ev:ev-mv45adl5-0146e187, and my kill-check on the same tree, ev:ev-mv44wbl4-0121944a.

**On the compensation path the mutant misbehaves** (security, ev:ev-mv45ahqj-01d67bc3, P-MONEY M4 under MB). A refund rejected during compensation is recorded as `refunded`, the reservation is released with restock rows, and the buyer reads `cancelled` / 'being refunded' while no money came back.

**Today's code is correct** (P-MONEY M4 and M4b on the real tree, ev:ev-mv44uzzh-01744558).

**Answer to the orchestrator's question.** The admin-basic pin is enough to stop MB itself from shipping. It is not enough for f2's own compensation contract (reconciling, escalation, no restock), so this is a minor follow-up, not a block.

**Origin.** f2's handoff (remaining issue 1) proposed reducing admin-basic to 'assert only that one call exists'. That suggestion produced the TR-R5-1 gap; rework-5 corrected it.

findings.title: Two of my mutants survived: MF6 is equivalent, MF4 is reachable only before a regular reconciler tick
findings.detail:
**MF6** (saga.js L257, the empty-plan guard of releaseIfSettled, removed): any reset closes every `reconciling` reservation in the same transaction that archives the operations (admin.js closedReconciling). So no `reconciling` reservation with only archived operations reaches the release check. The guard is defensive, and the mutant is equivalent.

**MF4** (the reset pass skips 'stale started intents -> unknown'): a started intent becomes stale after 2 x RS_PAYPAL_TIMEOUT_MS (40 s), and every regular reconciler tick (15 s) marks it anyway. Only a stale intent that the regular tick has not yet marked (at most one interval) would be listed as stranded by a forced reset, rather than resolved.
findings.recommendation: No change required. Optional, owner f2 or phase G: a forced-reset test with a stale started void intent would pin MF4. Resolved by the verification report listing both survivors with this reasoning.

findings.title: A forced reset does not fence a live executing saga; a capture landing after the archive leaves a stale `stranded` entry
findings.detail:
settleForForcedReset queues voids for `authorized` operations of executing plans and runs a pass of up to 30 s outside any transaction. Meanwhile the plan's lease holder may still start a capture: the capture guard checks the lease and `authorized`, not cancel_requested_at, and nothing in the reset changes lease_epoch.

Security's P-RESET R4 and R5 (ev:ev-mv44xmul-01d64afc) show the in-reset races resolve correctly: a capture applied with its answer held is refunded, and a capture held before the provider is refused after the void.

The residual is a capture that lands after the archiving transaction:
- its result is recorded on the archived row;
- the refund that the cancellation hook queues is never sent, because startCall refuses archived operations (security confirms by reading);
- the `stranded` entry reported to the operator says `authorized`, while PayPal shows the authorization CAPTURED.

This complements SEC-F-I1. It is demo-only, admin-only, needs force plus a reason, and spends Sandbox money; SEC-11 accepts manual clean-up.
findings.recommendation: No change required for this gate. Owner: delivery-lead (verification report, item 16). Resolved when the report states that the `stranded` statuses are as of the archive, and that a capture in flight for an executing plan can complete after it. Optionally, the archive transaction could bump lease_epoch of executing plans to fence late result writes.

findings.title: FU-33: the race is in the test, not in contention; raise it to the first phase G item
findings.detail:
**Two of my last four locked full suites on the real tree hit uploads-retention.test.js L711:**
- rework-5 ev:ev-mv44rydx-01958248, with no other suite and no run of mine active (load average 2.3);
- phase F ev:ev-mv451ngy-01bf3721, while I ran the small f1-f3 commands beside it.

The delivery-lead's ev:ev-mv445oiq-01166891 and f4's ev:ev-mv43j15k-01209f8b failed the same way.

**Cause.** The cause is deterministic in the test. retention.js deletes the row (L37) and then unlinks the file asynchronously (L47). The test polls only for the row and then checks `existsSync` at once, so any scheduling delay between the two fails it. Load only widens the window.

**Cost.** Each occurrence costs a 2-4 minute full re-run, and it trains every role to discount red runs.

**Answer to the orchestrator.** Yes, this raises FU-33's priority.
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator (FU-33, dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152). Make it the first phase G change, before any further full-suite evidence is gathered. Resolved when the test waits for the file as well as the row (the one-line fix) and three consecutive locked npm test runs pass it.

findings.title: (security) The forced reset's `stranded` list does not say which captured money is owed back; its wording assumes the Sandbox
findings.detail:
**What the list shows.** A `captured` operation with cancel_requested_at set reads like a completed sale (R7). Captured operations of an executing plan are archived as they are and listed (R2, R4, R5), as SEC-11 specifies.

**Wording.** The admin screen says 'Check each one in the PayPal Sandbox dashboard' even with the fake provider (public/js/views/admin.js L130).
findings.recommendation: Owner: g2 or g3 via the orchestrator. Resolved when each stranded entry carries planStatus and cancelRequested (or owedRefund) and the intro is worded by provider, or when the verification report records the decision not to.

findings.title: (security) refund_order 404 and every 422 on the fault routes write no audit row
findings.detail: The spec says 'Every faults and refund_order call writes an audit event with the actor and the target ids'. The 409 refusals are durable (P-MONEY M1, M2). Because the admin is trusted, this is about completeness only.
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator (follow-up). Resolved when a denied audit row is written for 404 and 422 on the fault routes, or the verification report states the narrower reading.

findings.title: (security) The admin supplier_refusal reason bypasses checkRefusalReason
findings.detail: applyFault validates the reason with str(1, 300) only (admin.js L428). It therefore stores ESC/BEL and blank reasons that the supplier route refuses (P-REFUSE S4, S7). The buyer sees them as text.
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator (follow-up). Resolved when applyFault uses checkRefusalReason, with a test.

findings.title: (security) Admin metrics `reconciler.unresolved` is 0 while an operation is refund_failed (and for the TR-F-1 plans)
findings.detail: `unresolved` counts only unknown, *_pending and void_failed. `operationsByStatus` does show `refund_failed`.
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator (follow-up, or with TR-F-1). Resolved when `unresolved` also counts refund_failed and escalated reservations, or the verification report lists the narrower meaning.

findings.title: (security) Bidi override controls are accepted in a refusal reason
findings.detail: checkRefusalReason accepts U+202E, which can visually reverse the system's trailing sentence after the reason. Markup is inert in Chromium (ev:ev-mv45fi73-01be9d51).
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator (follow-up). Resolved when U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 are refused or stripped, or the reason is isolated (FSI...PDI) when the message is composed.

findings.title: (security) A refunded order can still be marked ready and handed over
findings.detail: After `refunded`, supplier A's card shows canMarkReady true, and ready and handover return 200 ('collected'), so the goods are released for a refunded payment. This matches the brief's literal guard (refund_* does not match `refunded`) and OQ-D2. orders.js L27 is c3's file, not phase F's.
findings.recommendation: Owner: orchestrator, as a product decision. Resolved when a decision states whether a refunded order may be collected; if not, add `refunded` to HANDOVER_BLOCKING_PAYMENT for that order, with a test.

lessonDecisions.note: This task builds no hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record or root (saga hold path and API tests only), so the lesson's applies-when conditions do not hold; it concerns root discovery in tool-call guards, not payment code.

handoff.objective: Close the review findings of rev-mv45ljos-01f00a5d on f2: TR-F-1 (major, FU-49) the FU-41(a) hold path re-takes the plan every tick and never escalates; SEC-F-1 (minor) no f2 test reaches the rejected-refund mapping; TR-F-2 (minor) the SEC-11 bounded-pass test can only hang.
handoff.context: Spec: provider call protocol section 6 (an unknown older than RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN feeds derivation row 2), saga step 6, F-TR-7 (no takeover while an operation is capture_pending or unknown). Reviewer's preferred fix for TR-F-1 taken: a held or failed pre-resend read puts the operation back to unknown. Previous f2 handoff ho-mv41a3s6-0138e24d. Every mutant ran in its own fresh scratch directory under scratchpad/f2r2/ with its diff kept as a file; the real tree was never mutated. No live suite was run; network 127.0.0.1 only. The known FU-33 race did not fail in any full run, so no re-run under dec-mv3tqbn4-01d43152 was used.
handoff.expectedOutput: The stuck hold path escalates and its epoch is bounded; the rejected-refund mapping and the SEC-11 bound are pinned by tests that go red under their mutants; all suites green.
acceptanceCriteria: TR-F-1: after RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN of failing reads the plan escalates to failed_needs_attention, lease_epoch stays bounded (<= 2: the initial 1 plus the one takeover the reconciler's single successful read allows), and once the reads recover the same key is sent once and the plan executes (test in capture-compensation.test.js)
TR-F-1: SEC-F-I2's fencing still holds: a stale holder whose read fails after a takeover writes nothing and sends nothing (test, red under the no-fence mutant)

SEC-F-1: a provider-rejected compensation refund ends refund_failed, the reservation stays reconciling with REFUND_FAILED and is not restocked, the buyer sees failed_needs_attention; red under mutant MB
TR-F-2: the SEC-11 bounded-pass test fails (does not hang) when the budget is removed; recorded mutant run
handoff.completedWork: CODE (src/services/saga.js only). New holdOperation(env, lease, op): when readBeforeResend does not answer 'send' (the read failed, or showed CAPTURED / VOIDED / EXPIRED), captureLoop now moves the operation authorized -> unknown (prev_status authorized) before pausing the lease, in one transaction that (a) needs the fence of a call result (plan row still at this executor and epoch, the same fence recordCall uses; a stale holder writes nothing and logs saga.lease_lost), (b) compare-and-sets on status authorized and on the capture call still being unknown with no send_token, and (c) keeps the unknown_since of that call (the original timeout), so the escalation clock is not restarted. Effect: the existing F-TR-7 takeover exclusion applies (the reconciler no longer takes the plan over every tick), derivation row 2 escalates the unknown after RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN, and the reconciler restores the operation again when ITS read shows CREATED, after which one takeover and one same-key re-send complete the plan. derive.js, reconciler.js and calls.js needed no change. BOUND: in the reviewer's scenario lease_epoch is 1 at the timeout, 2 after the single takeover that the reconciler's one successful read allows, and stays 2 over 8 ticks (20 minutes) of failing reads (reviewer measured 2..10 before); 8 failing reads for 8 ticks (one per tick, not two); after recovery it is 3. In general each successful reconciler read can enable at most one takeover, so the epoch grows only with progress, not with ticks. TESTS. capture-compensation.test.js (+3 tests, 20 in the file): (1) TR-F-1 FU-49 stuck plan: not escalated at 11 min, failed_needs_attention at 21 min, epoch <= 2, <= 1 takeover audit row, 1 read per tick, original unknown_since kept, nothing sent while reads fail, then recovery: A sent twice with the same key in all, 2 captures at the provider, plan executed, purchase_confirmed, epoch 3; (2) TR-F-1 fencing: epoch-2 holder blocked in its read, lease lapses, epoch-3 takeover (also blocked), the stale read fails: the operation stays authorized, saga.lease_lost logged, no send; the epoch-3 holder then sends once and the plan executes; (3) SEC-F-1 rejected refund (fault http_422:refund on A, capture_declined on B): refund_failed with INJECTED_UNPROCESSABLE, refund call failed and sent once, no refund at the provider, reservation reconciling with REFUND_FAILED, zero restock rows, buyer rescueStatus failed_needs_attention and no refunded in the view. One existing assertion changed on purpose: the FU-41(a) CAPTURED-by-then test now expects the held operation to be unknown (prev_status authorized) instead of authorized, which is the reviewer's recommended state. admin-reset.test.js: a within(ms, promise, what) helper fails a test after 5 s with a message naming the missing budget; both tests that await a never-answering provider (the SEC-11 bound test and the RS-37 already-archived test, which had the same hang) use it and carry { timeout: 20000 }. The bound test's assertions are unchanged.
remainingIssues: Mutant survivor, disclosed: a first version of the TR-F-1 test did not kill the mutant that restarts unknown_since at the hold (ev:ev-mv45svt4-01979495 passed 20/20) because the first tick came at the same clock instant as the timeout; the test now advances 60 s first and the mutant is killed (ev:ev-mv45vbm0-01dbd580). Scratch dirs mut-trf1-nofence, mut-trf1-since and mut-reset-unbounded-new are the superseded versions; the -b and -final dirs are the evidence for the final tests.

A hold on a CAPTURED/VOIDED/EXPIRED read also makes the operation unknown for the moment until the reconciler's next read resolves it; derive.js row 2 then escalates only after RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN, as for any unknown.

Both are small, reversible product defaults the user delegated.

data.title: Correction to dec-mv46ovf2-017bf12d (FU-59): block handover per order, not per plan
data.decision: dec-mv46ovf2-017bf12d stands in intent, but its implementation note is wrong: handoverAllowed (src/services/orders.js L51-58) checks every payment operation of the plan, so adding refunded to HANDOVER_BLOCKING_PAYMENT would also block the sibling orders of a partially refunded plan, against OQ-D2 and spec row 7. The rule is: an order whose OWN payment operation is refunded cannot be marked ready or handed over (409 HANDOVER_BLOCKED); its siblings keep the existing plan-wide rule. The backend rework's test must show the refunded order refused and a sibling still marked ready and handed over. The rework also carries the security reviewer's two other conditions: FU-58 covers the supplier route's own checkRefusalReason (refuse or strip U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069, or isolate the reason), and FU-54's owedRefund is true exactly for a captured operation with cancel_requested_at set, with planStatus on every entry and no Sandbox wording for the fake provider. Security reviews that rework before delivery.

handoff.context: Decision dec-mv46ovt6-01a662af. findings.title: (merges SEC-F2-I1) Under flapping reads the epoch is bounded by successful reconciler reads, not constant; the plan still escalates
findings.detail:
**What still happens.** holdOperation returns the operation to `unknown` after each failed holder read. If, on the next tick, the reconciler's own read succeeds (CREATED), the operation is restored, taken over (epoch + 1) and held again. Security's G5 (ev:ev-mv46u1oo-0168894e) shows epochs up to 7 within 12 random-failure ticks for some seeds; most stay at 2.

**Why it is acceptable.**
- Every takeover is backed by a fresh CREATED read.
- No send happens without a holder read showing CREATED, and no seed doubled a capture.
- The operation reads `unknown` between ticks with the ORIGINAL unknown_since, so row 2 escalates after RS_UNKNOWN_ESCALATE_MIN. MG2 confirms that the clock is not restarted.
- The persistent-outage case keeps the epoch constant (my probe v2).
findings.recommendation: No change required. Owner: delivery-lead (verification report, item 21). Resolved when item 21 states that the epoch grows only with successful reconciler reads, and that a flapping provider still escalates through row 2.

findings.title: (security) Three conditions on the backend rework that dec-mv46ovt6-01a662af opens after phase F approval
findings.detail:
1. **FU-59 / SEC-F-I7:** the handover block must apply per order, not per plan. handoverAllowed (orders.js L51-L62) checks every operation of the plan, so adding `refunded` to HANDOVER_BLOCKING_PAYMENT as written would also block the sibling orders of a partially refunded plan, contrary to spec revision 2 row 7 / OQ-D2.
2. **FU-58 / SEC-F-I6:** the supplier route's checkRefusalReason itself must refuse or strip bidi overrides (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069), or the server must isolate the reason when it composes the message.
3. **FU-54 / SEC-F-I1:** `owedRefund` must be true exactly for `captured` with cancel_requested_at set. Each stranded entry also carries `planStatus`, and the fake-provider wording must not mention the Sandbox dashboard.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
**Fix.** saga.js holdOperation (L547, called at L617) puts a held operation back to `unknown` with the original unknown_since, under the epoch fence.

**Condition (a), the stuck state escalates.** Met. My probe v2 on the new tree: `failed_needs_attention` from tick 7 (17.5 min after the timeout).

**Condition (b), the epoch is settled.** Met by the code, so no decision is needed. Epochs are 2,2,...,2 over 8 ticks, with one read per tick and 0 sends; after recovery the plan is `executed` with one capture per authorization (ev:ev-mv47n3s8-015a5cc7).

**Discrimination.** The same probe fails on the iteration-1 tree with epochs 2..10 (control ev:ev-mv47n4y0-0138cad2).

**Tests.** The new tests (capture-compensation L563 and the stale-holder test at L632) kill all three of my mutants of the fix: hold reverted, clock restarted, fence removed (ev:ev-mv47pa98-0198bb63).

**Security.** P-HOLD G1-G5 (ev:ev-mv46u1oo-0168894e) agrees.

**Regression.** The full suite passes under the lock (ev:ev-mv47tl1n-016af5d0).

admin-reset.test.js adds within() (L50) and `{ timeout: 20_000 }` to the SEC-11 bound test (L235) and to the RS-37 already-archived test, which had the same hang.

The unbounded-pass mutant (MG5) now fails both by assertion in 17 s (11 tests, 2 fail, 0 cancelled), instead of hanging (ev:ev-mv47pa98-0198bb63).

**Labels.** The RS-21, RS-22 and F-TR-6 rows now read 'LIVE-DEPENDENT and not covered by LIVE-P1'.

**RISK-18.** Its title is corrected in the risk record to 'live RS-19/20/23/24 evidence' (updatedBy delivery-lead, 18:48:29Z).

**Routed.** The evidence table and the verification report are FU-52 (owners: g3 and the delivery-lead).
Info, accepted. Verification report item 20 lists the MF4 and MF6 survivors with my reasoning.

Info, routed as FU-53: the verification report will state that stranded statuses are as of the archive. dec-mv46ovt6-01a662af declines the optional lease_epoch bump, as my recommendation allowed. Security accepts this (late completions are recorded but never sent).

Info, routed. dec-mv46ovt6-01a662af opens rework-6 (test-only, test-engineer) now for FU-33 (wait for the asynchronous unlink) and FU-46, ahead of further full-suite evidence. FU-33 did not hit in my iteration-2 suite.

data.title: FU-50: completed voids of a closed plan are not listed in If something fails
data.decision: No view change. The If something fails panel lists outstanding voids and refunds of the current plan with their outcome, as spec Frontend section 7 states; completed voids of a closed plan are not listed. The verification report states this limit, and g2's runbook notes that an admin can see past operations. Revisit after the hackathon if users ask.
data.rationale: The spec does not require completed voids of a closed plan to stay visible; adding them means a server view-shape change in view.js (no remaining owner) plus contract fixtures and browser checks late in phase G, a cross-task integration risk for a secondary display. The buyer already sees the refusal reason and that the new plan needs approval; money state stays correct and auditable.

criteria.description: The retention behaviour the test asserts matches the spec, and the no-unlink survivor does not hide a defect
criteria.notes:
**The spec.** L773: 'The hourly sweep deletes rows and files ... and writes an image.retention_delete audit event per image. Startup also removes orphan files older than 1 day.' L979: 'orphan files, and an audit row per deletion'.

**Why the engineer's first no-unlink mutant passes** (ev:ev-mv476e0b-01cc6895):
- the orphan step of the same pass removes the file, with its own image.orphan_delete audit row;
- so the file and the row are gone and every deletion has an audit row, as the spec requires;
- the outcome is spec-conformant and hides no product defect.

**Its survival depends on the date.** The orphan age check (retention.js L79) compares the pinned clock, FIXED_NOW_MS 2026-10-20T06:00Z (app-harness L24), with the file's real mtime. After 2026-10-19T06:00Z wall-clock time, a freshly written file is not 'older than 1 day' by that clock, and the same mutant would die at L718.

The gap in attribution is pre-existing. It is recorded as TR-R6-4 (info).

findings.title: SEC-B-1 lost its per-call latency sensitivity below 1 s: an exact, non-throwing mutant that holds the event loop 300 ms on 49 inputs passes the revised test
findings.detail:
**What SEC-B-1 was about.** rev-mv1ijr52-01b2f4b6 raised it with two harms: PLANNER_LIMIT on fillable requests, and 'holds the event loop up to about 0.3 s'.
- The first harm is still pinned exactly.
- The second was pinned by the per-call bounds: 50 ms for test 1, 100 ms for each sweep call, 250 ms for each 12-offer catalog. All three are now 1000 ms (L63, L84, L124).
- The only aggregate bound left is the sweep p95, and it is blind to any slowdown that affects up to 5 % of the 1,008 calls. Test 3 has no aggregate bound at all.

**The survivor.** Mutant pl-delay (scratchpad/tr-r6/pl-delay/mutant.diff, printed first in each log):
- planner.js busy-waits 300 ms when cups >= 10,000, maxPickups is 5 and every offer holds 100-200 bundles;
- that is 48 sweep calls (4.8 %) plus the stock-100 / 10,000-cup headline call;
- the results stay exact and nothing throws.
- **The revised file passes it, 3/3** (ev:ev-mv493ssw-01fd0bfd, exit 0 = survives). Test 2 takes 14.9 s instead of about 0.3 s.
- **The pre-rework file kills it** on exactly the removed bounds, 'took 301.7 ms' in test 1 and 'took 302.0 ms' in test 2 (kill-check ev:ev-mv493ue1-01c2135e).

**Why it is minor, not blocking.**
1. FU-46 itself prescribes 'the p95 plus a generous per-call ceiling', and that is what was built and disclosed (disclosures 1 and 2).
2. Real algorithmic regressions are still killed:
   - full enumeration, by PLANNER_LIMIT (engineer);
   - no lower bound, by PLANNER_LIMIT at the 2M cap (7 catalogs throw, ev:ev-mv49479d-013eb6ff);
   - no lower bound with the cap at 40M, by the ceiling alone (ev:ev-mv493yql-018b9f5c).
   The other five single-cut mutants (no dominance table, no irredundancy cut, no subset mandatory cut, no incumbent break, no subset root bound) do not change timing under either test. The worst is pl-noroot, at 137-216 ms on a 12-offer catalog across my runs, which is under the old 250 ms too (ev:ev-mv49479d-013eb6ff).
3. What slips is an input-targeted hold of 0.1-1 s, which a pure planner is unlikely to acquire.
4. The old bounds were a recorded source of red full runs (186.9 ms, 327.9 ms).

The residual is still real for the security reading of SEC-B-1: an attacker picks one input, and a p95 does not protect a single input.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: test-engineer, through phase G or the next rework that owns test/timing/** (the orchestrator routes it).

**Fix: re-time on exceed.** When a call exceeds its pre-rework bound (50 ms test 1, 100 ms sweep, 250 ms 12-offer), call plan() on the same input twice more and fail only if the MINIMUM of the three timings is still above the bound. Keep the 1000 ms ceiling on the first timing as the runaway guard.
- Host contention and steal are transient and do not repeat three times on one input. A deterministic hold does.
- This needs no new constant.
- As an alternative or addition, give test 3 a p95 bound over its 150 catalogs.

**Resolved when:**
- the revised test fails on pl-delay (scratchpad/tr-r6/pl-delay/mutant.diff), shown by a kill-check that passes only on that failure;
- the file stays green 3/3 under the same 3 x nproc CPU-contention runs as ev:ev-mv47feek-01fdb68f;
- one locked npm test is green.

**Alternative:** an orchestrator decision accepts a per-call hold of up to 1 s as a SEC-B-1 residual, alongside SEC-B-1R / RISK-19, and the verification report lists it.

findings.title: uploads-retention L711-L713 attribute to 'spec: Retention' a sentence that is the source comment at src/services/retention.js L35
findings.detail:
The comment quotes 'row and audit event first; an unlink that fails leaves an orphan for the orphan sweep' as 'spec: Retention'.
- That wording is not in spec.md.
- It paraphrases retention.js L35: 'Row and audit event first: if the file cannot be unlinked it is an orphan, and the orphan sweep removes it later.'
- The spec says only that the sweep deletes rows and files with an audit event per image, and that startup removes orphan files older than 1 day (L773, L979).

The behaviour and the fix are unaffected; only the traceability is wrong. This is the same kind as TR-R5-2 (minor), and the delivery-lead disclosed it (disclosure 4).
findings.recommendation:
Owner: whoever next owns test/api/uploads-retention.test.js (test-engineer). It can be folded into the TR-R6-1 or TR-R6-4 change.

Resolved when the comment cites src/services/retention.js L35 for the ordering, and spec 'Retention and deletion' (L773) only for what that section says.

findings.title: Disclosure 2's 'no mutant can show the ceiling alone firing' is inaccurate: an exact, non-throwing mutant is killed by the 1000 ms ceiling alone
findings.detail:
**The ceiling fires.** Mutant pl-nolb-cap removes the node lower-bound cut and raises the node cap from 2M to 40M. It never throws, and the revised test fails only at test 3: 'catalog 35 took 1335.6 ms (runaway ceiling 1000 ms ...)' (kill-check ev:ev-mv493yql-018b9f5c).

**What stays true.**
- The p95 line is still not shown firing by any mutant.
- With the same cut and the 2M cap, 7 of the 150 catalogs throw PLANNER_LIMIT, so exactness kills that variant (ev:ev-mv49479d-013eb6ff).

This corrects the record in the test's favour; it is not a defect.
findings.recommendation:
No change to the tests.

Resolved when the verification report states FU-46's coverage as: exactness (PLANNER_LIMIT) plus the ceiling, both shown firing by a mutant; the p95 not shown firing.

findings.title: No RS-39 test attributes a swept image's unlink to the image step; the no-unlink mutant survives through the orphan step, and only while the wall clock is before 2026-10-19
findings.detail:
**Why the engineer's first no-unlink mutant passes** (ev:ev-mv476e0b-01cc6895).
- The orphan step of the same pass unlinks the file and writes image.orphan_delete. The outcome is spec-conformant (L773, L979), so this is not a product defect.
- Survival needs the orphan age check (retention.js L79) to see the fresh file as older than 1 day, measured against the pinned clock (FIXED_NOW_MS 2026-10-20T06:00Z, app-harness L24).
- From 2026-10-19T06:00Z wall-clock time, the same mutant would be killed at L718.

**Pre-existing gap.** No test pins that the image step itself unlinks. The 7 d + 1 min test checks only that the file is gone. The gap is not introduced by rework-6, and the rework's new wait is not weakened by it: my ur-never kill-check is red at L718 (ev:ev-mv493g8c-013ac111).
findings.recommendation:
Optional, for the next owner of uploads-retention.test.js. In the 'kept at 6 days 23 hours, deleted at 7 days + 1 minute' test, assert `swept.imageFilesLeft === 0` and that no image.orphan_delete event names the swept file.

Resolved when the engineer's one-line no-unlink mutant (shown in the log of ev:ev-mv476e0b-01cc6895) fails that test whatever the wall-clock date, shown by a kill-check. Otherwise, close it as accepted in the verification report.

findings.title: Disclosures 5 and 6 accepted: one scratch directory reused (both diffs recoverable from their logs); the 20-run loop log shows exit codes, not counts
findings.detail:
**Disclosure 5, the directory reuse.**
- ur-nounlink/mutant.diff now holds only the extended version.
- I checked both logs: ev:ev-mv476e0b-01cc6895 prints the one-line `leftForOrphanSweep += 1` diff, with 33/33 pass; ev:ev-mv476u2l-01edbb7b prints that line plus the orphan-sweep `continue`, with 30/33.
- Both versions are recoverable. The one-directory-per-mutant rule (TR-R5-4) was broken once; nothing was lost.

**Disclosure 6, the loop log.**
- ev:ev-mv47lom9-015c619a stops at the first non-zero exit, and node --test exits non-zero on any failing or cancelled test. The 20 'run N ok' lines therefore prove 20 clean runs.
- The command has no name filter, so each run executed the whole file. Only the per-run counts are missing.
- My own locked runs supersede the loop for FU-33 in any case.
findings.recommendation:
No change for this gate. For later loops, print each run's '# tests/# pass/# fail' lines (for example `| grep -E '^# (tests|pass|fail)'`) instead of discarding the TAP, and never reuse a mutant directory.

Resolved going forward when the next mutant or loop evidence follows this.
